Using the one-dimensional stochastic heat equation, we demonstrate that incorporating multiplicative noise is necessary to recover the expected gamma distribution for temperature in the canonical ensemble, whereas additive noise models yield a Gaussian distribution that fails to capture non-zero skewness and excess kurtosis. We also derive analytical expressions for inherent modeling errors that persist in the limit of vanishing time step for a variety of boundary conditions. Furthermore, we introduce an improved formulation for Dirichlet boundary conditions that eliminates large boundary-adjacent errors in the third central moment present in traditional boundary treatments. We also examine higher-order temporal integration schemes, demonstrating that Stratonovich-based integrators, such as Heun's predictor-corrector method, can reduce these modeling errors. Finally, numerical simulations of the full compressible, stochastic Navier--Stokes equations confirm the generality and practical applicability of the findings obtained from the stochastic heat equation.

authors.name: John B. Bell
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: From Safety-Driven Redundancy to Value-Driven Architecture: An ODD-Based Rationalization Framework for Level 4 Autonomous Vehicles
papers.abstract: Level 4 autonomous vehicles require fault-tolerant architectures that preserve critical driving functions under sensing, computing, communication, power, and actuation failures. As these systems progress toward industrial scalability, architectural complexity, validation burden, integration effort, and lifecycle cost become increasingly relevant. This study proposes an Operational Design Domain (ODD)-based, safety-constrained systems-engineering framework for architecture rationalization. ODD-specific capabilities, physical fault assumptions, post-fault operational policies, and spatial sensing requirements are propagated through an integrated safety-feasibility gate. Architecture transformations, including removal, relocation, functional reassignment, and consolidation, are evaluated only within the resulting safety-feasible design space, followed by lifecycle-cost sensitivity and robust multiobjective Pareto analysis. A generic, synthetically parameterized Level 4 architecture is used as a demonstrative computational case study. Within this modeled design space, direct ablation showed limited rationalization potential, whereas directional redistribution and functional consolidation generated a broader set of safety-feasible candidates. Under the illustrative lifecycle-cost model, the best nominal candidate achieved a 5.55% normalized cost reduction and remained cost-reducing across all 5,000 sampled points in the prescribed uncertainty domain. The analysis identified 15 non-dominated architecture-policy solutions representing seven physical transformations. The results support capability-based, policy-conditioned, and lifecycle-aware architecture rationalization under the stated assumptions, with safety retained as a non-compensatory feasibility constraint. The reported transformations are design candidates rather than validated production architectures.

papers.title: File Size as a Potential Dataset Bias in Audio-Visual Deepfake Data
papers.abstract: Deepfake detection benchmarks are commonly designed to evaluate whether models can distinguish authentic from manipulated audiovisual content. However, benchmark construction pipelines may introduce unintended associations between class labels and simple file-level properties. In this work, we identify a potential file-size bias in two widely used audio-visual deepfake datasets. In the 1M-Deepfakes Detection Challenge dataset, a score derived from file size alone achieves 70.13% AUC on the validation set. When file size is considered together with video duration, simple file-level methods exceed 90% AUC on 1M and 85% AUC on FakeAVCeleb. Although the same pattern is not observed in DFDC, the results suggest that the observed association is dataset-dependent rather than an inherent property of deepfake videos. We discuss several possible explanations, including differences in encoding, compression, source data, manipulation procedures, and post-processing, although the present analysis does not establish the underlying cause. We further discuss whether the factors associated with file size may also leave traces in decoded video or audio, and consequently whether they could influence content-based deepfake detection, as an important direction for future work. Our findings highlight the importance of examining simple file-level properties when constructing and evaluating deepfake datasets and benchmarks.

papers.title: Load Balancing Neurons: Firing-Rate Control Sustains Plasticity in Continual Learning
papers.abstract: Neural networks in continual learning often lose plasticity: some neurons become inactive, while others fire almost constantly. This limits adaptation to shifting data and wastes capacity. Prior work mitigates this by periodically reinitializing low-utility units, but such resets can destroy previously learned features and do not proactively prevent low utility. We study a simple diagnostic measure: the firing rate of ReLU units, defined as the fraction of positive pre-activations. Low rates identify dead units, while very high rates indicate linearized, always-on units. Based on this view, we introduce a lightweight load-balancing mechanism that adjusts per-neuron thresholds to keep firing rates within a target range. Across continual ImageNet and class-incremental CIFAR-100, firing-rate distributions explain differences in plasticity across a range of approaches, including well-known techniques such as L2 regularization and non-affine normalization, and load balancing matches or exceeds reset-based methods on both benchmarks. The same mechanism carries over to reinforcement learning, improving Rainbow DQN on Atari over a LayerNorm baseline.

authors.name: Jan Robine
authors.institution: Lamarr Institute for Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence

papers.title: Counting elliptic curves by discriminant
papers.abstract: We prove an asymptotic formula with a power saving for the number of $\mathbb{Q}$-isomorphism classes of elliptic curves $E/\mathbb{Q}$ ordered by minimal discriminant, assuming the $abc$ conjecture. Unconditionally, we obtain the same asymptotic for the curves with $|\Delta_{\min}(E)| \le X$ and $c_4(E) \le X^{8/3 - \delta}$ for any fixed $\delta > 0$, by obtaining new bounds for the number of integral points $(c_4, c_6)$ near the cusp $c_4^3 = c_6^2$.

papers.title: On the leading constant in Manin's conjecture
papers.abstract: We disprove a conjecture of Batyrev and Tschinkel concerning counting rational points of bounded height. Our results strongly suggest that the transcendental Brauer group plays a role in the leading constant in problems of the same nature such as the Manin--Peyre conjecture.

papers.title: Supercuspidal representations and types via double covers and the Fourier--Weil representation
papers.abstract: We present a construction of supercuspidal representations and types for tame $p$-adic groups whose input is a generic essentially depth-zero representation of a double covers of twisted Levi subgroups. This clarifies and simplifies existing constructions by automatically producing and explaining the twisting quadratic character of Fintzen--Kaletha--Spice, the roots of unity in the Harish-Chandra character formula, and making the connection to the Galois side of the local Langlands correspondence immediate. The main innovation is the use of a Fourier model of the Weil representation defined on an extension of the symplectic group by the Witt group.

papers.title: Twisted $L^2$-torsion functions obstruct fibring over the circle
papers.abstract: The vanishing of the L^2-Betti numbers of the universal covering of a closed manifold is an obstruction to fibring over the circle. When the L^2-Betti numbers vanish we introduce a secondary obstruction based on the asymptotic behaviour of the twisted L^2-torsion function at 0 and infinity. We provide a number of examples showing the invariant is indeed non-trivial.

papers.title: Determining the electron-hole pair creation energy in a 4H-SiC p-n diode via X-ray spectroscopy
papers.abstract: This paper reports on a measurement to determine the electron-hole pair creation energy in a 4H-SiC p-n diode. By measuring the spectra of several X-ray sources and comparing the response between the silicon-carbide diode and a commercial silicon diode, the electron-hole pair creation energy in 4H-SiC is determined to be (7.87 $\pm$ 0.09) eV. This is the first result obtained using X-ray spectra from several sources and including an estimate of the uncertainty. The result is in good agreement with studies of comparable devices.

papers.title: Efficient reconfiguration, polynomial decompositions and approximate counting
papers.abstract: We consider reconfigurations of integer assignments to planar lattice regions that preserve specified line totals, which are motivated by questions of combinatorial construction, algorithmic sampling and approximate counting. An elementary prototype is provided by contingency tables, i.e. two-dimensional grids of non-negative integers with prescribed row and column sums, which can be reconfigured by basic switches of the form $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}1&-1\\-1&1\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. More difficult combinatorial instances include reconfiguration of Latin squares or queens configurations. Our main technical ingredient is the following polynomial decomposition lemma. Fix a positive integer $k$. Let $F(x)\in \mathbb{Z}[x]$ be a polynomial of degree at most $n$ such that $(1-x)^k\mid F(x)$ and the sum of the absolute values of the coefficients of $F$ is $m$. We prove that $F$ can be written as a sum of $O(m+n)$ basic polynomials of degree at most $n$ of the form $\pm x^a(1-x^{a_1})\cdots (1-x^{a_k})$ where $a,a_1,\ldots,a_k$ are non-negative integers. The proof uses the existence of a miraculous high-dimensional coupling of signed distributions on cross polytopes that has independent interest. We will apply this lemma to questions of combinatorial construction in other papers; in this paper we illustrate its application to approximate counting.

papers.title: Dominoes tiling a common figure
papers.abstract: Call a two-element subset of $\mathbb{Z}^2$ a domino. Given finitely many dominoes $D_1,\ldots,D_k$, we show that there exists a finite non-empty $B\subset \mathbb{Z}^2$ such that $B$ can be partitioned into disjoint translates of $D_i$ for all $i$. The proof uses a new absorption mechanism for perfect matchings in algebraically defined hypergraphs.

papers.title: A homogeneous mass campaign of transiting sub-Neptunes around FGK stars
papers.abstract: Sub-Neptunes are among the most common planets in our Galaxy, but are still poorly understood. Addressing their origins and compositions requires precise bulk densities, but literature values come from studies using different radial velocity (RV) extraction methods, stellar activity treatments, and statistical frameworks, which introduces systematic biases that can lead to spurious conclusions in population-level analyses. We conducted a systematic and homogeneous mass-measurement campaign for 12 sub-Neptune systems observed by Kepler and K2, selected for their absent or poorly constrained masses ($\sigma_{M_p}/M_p > 25\%$). Using new HIRES, HARPS-N, and ESPRESSO spectroscopy as well as archival data, we applied a unified hierarchical Bayesian framework with homogeneous data curation. For HARPS-N and ESPRESSO, we applied four independent extraction pipelines (CCF, SERVAL, LBL, sBART) and combined the posteriors via leave-one-out cross-validation stacking, so that no mass would hinge on a single pipeline. A preferred noise model for each target was selected through a uniform Bayesian procedure. We obtained $>3\sigma$ masses for four transiting planets: Kepler-21 b ($5.66^{+0.65}_{-0.96} M_\oplus$, $7.61^{+0.96}_{-1.28}$ g cm$^{-3}$), K2-66 b ($17.9 \pm 3.2 M_\oplus$, $4.69 \pm 1.31$ g cm$^{-3}$), Kepler-538 b ($10.8^{+2.4}_{-2.8} M_\oplus$), and K2-182 b ($20.1^{+4.5}_{-7.8} M_\oplus$). We also provide updated masses for the non-transiting giants Kepler-65 e and Kepler-129 d, and upper limits for the remaining 15 signals, including the first constraints for K2-184, K2-244, and K2-269. No new non-transiting companion was detected in any system. The semi-amplitudes of the four reductions span a median of $0.75\sigma$ of the stacked posterior, and up to $2.7\sigma$, a systematic that a single-pipeline analysis would ignore.

papers.title: On the concentration of the ambiguity function on centered balls
papers.abstract: We show that the Gaussian uniquely maximizes the $L^2$ concentration of the ambiguity function on every centered ball, up to time-frequency shifts and multiplication by a unimodular constant. The proof relies on ideas from quantum information theory.

papers.title: Parallel and perpendicular: a two-population test with POSSUM radio galaxies confirms hint of CMB birefringence
papers.abstract: Analyses of the cosmic microwave background (CMB) polarisation find an isotropic rotation of the linear polarisation plane, cosmic birefringence, of $\beta\sim0.2^\circ$--$0.3^\circ$, hinting at parity-violating physics. An independent test at low redshift with different systematics is needed. Radio galaxies provide such a test because their Faraday de-rotated polarisation angle $\chi_0$ is statistically aligned with their position angle $\psi$. Previous tests fitted only the population with $\chi_0-\psi\approx90^\circ$. We add the population with $\chi_0-\psi\approx0^\circ$, which is rotated by the same angle. We fit $\chi_0-\psi$ with two axial von-Mises distributions plus a uniform background, with an unbinned likelihood including each source's angle error. We apply this to 33,298 components of 16,649 double radio sources from the Polarisation Sky Survey of the Universe's Magnetism (POSSUM), with both components at polarised S/N $>10$ and separated by more than half the beam. Both populations are equally abundant. In the CMB convention we measure $\beta=0.48^\circ\pm0.35^\circ$, agreeing with the CMB in sign and amplitude. Including the $0^\circ$ population halves the variance of $\beta$. Components closer than half a beam carry no information on the source axis; excluding them leaves $\beta$ unchanged and makes the two populations consistent in all morphological classes. Combining with the joint ACT and Planck likelihood for a late-time rotation yields $\beta=0.282^\circ\pm0.056^\circ$, $5.0\sigma$ from zero. At $z\sim0.5$, radio galaxies probe the rotation of the last $\sim$ 5 Gyr. A CMB-sized rotation there would point to a late-evolving field such as axion-like dark energy, whereas a rotation before reionisation, e.g. by axion-like dark matter, predicts $\beta\approx0$. Given absolute angle calibration, the full POSSUM survey can test the CMB result independently.

authors.name: Marco Regis
authors.institution: Istituto Nazionale di Fisica Nucleare, Sezione di Torino

papers.title: Automated classification of modal displacements
papers.abstract: The bending, torsional, or coupled character of a mode shape helps determine the dynamic behaviour of aerospace and civil structures. In vibration testing, it is assigned by inspecting mode shape plots, and depends on the analyst. This work proposes four indices to describe the motion of a mode from a few sensor vectors: a bending score, a torsion score, a twist share and an in-plane ratio. They are assessed on the first eight finite element modes of a tapered plate with a swept trailing edge. They are applied to identified XB-2 wing modes and to the published modes of the Sheraton Universal Hotel, a reinforced concrete (RC) building. On the plate, the twist share separates bending, coupled and torsion modes. The XB-2 modes include one bending and three coupled modes (one dominated by in-plane bending and two by out-of-plane bending). The coupled mode dominated by in-plane bending (15.25 Hz, in-plane ratio 1.33) was not investigated in earlier campaigns on the wing. On the RC building, all five modes are bending (twist share below 0.0005). The twist share and the in-plane ratio indicate the type of each mode. Hence, modes are classified without visually inspecting the mode shapes. Code and processed data are openly released.

papers.title: Exact Response Theory based on Karhunen-Lo\`eve Expansions for Brownian Oscillators
papers.abstract: We extend Exact Response Theory (ERT) to an overdamped Brownian oscillator driven by thermal white noise. The stochastic forcing is represented by a Karhunen--Lo\`eve series and embedded into an autonomous, augmented phase space using a harmonic auxiliary phase. This representation allows us to construct the ERT dissipation function for fixed mode amplitudes and recover stochastic averages by averaging over the amplitudes and the initial phase. For the variance, we derive the response at finite spectral truncation and show analytically that, with uniform phase sampling, the full-spectrum white-noise limit reproduces the generator-based result for a sudden temperature change. Furthermore, a comparison with first-order linear response theory highlights how this may fail in general. In particular, if the noise-induced variance is quadratic in the noise amplitude, it is completely omitted by linear response. The analysis provides a framework for this model and for studying more general forcing; extensions to non-Markovian dynamics require separate convergence and regularity analyses.

papers.title: Overparameterized Simulation-Error Minimization for Nonlinear System Identification: Horizon-Uniform Landscape and Identifiability
papers.abstract: Simulation-error minimization is a standard criterion in nonlinear system identification, but its landscape is nonconvex and its conditioning can degrade geometrically with the data horizon N. We propose to lift the trajectory with a free, softly penalized per-step correction, which yields a fit loss that gradient descent provably minimizes: under a rank condition on the output map and a bound on the one-step Jacobian, it satisfies a Polyak-Lojasiewicz inequality with an explicit constant independent of N. A zero-loss model leaves the physical parameter undetermined. Identifiability is restored by a minimal-correction selection principle: under structural identifiability, the global minimizer of the penalized loss returns the true parameters for every positive penalty weight, and under noise and unmodeled dynamics the parameter error grows at most linearly with the mismatch. The resulting estimator, gradient descent on the fit loss followed by a homotopy in the penalty weight, reconciles fit and selection, with a local convergence guarantee. In experiments, it recovers the parameters on long records of expanding and chaotic systems on which single shooting fails.

papers.title: Average density of rational points on quartic surfaces
papers.abstract: We establish an average asymptotic for the number of rational points of bounded height $B$ on quartic surfaces in $\mathbb{P}^3$ of height bounded by $A$, refining an argument of Le Boudec and using techniques of Browning-Le Boudec-Sawin. We extend the range of the asymptotic from $B=o(A)$ to $B=O(A^2)$. As an application, we show that almost all quartic surfaces of height $H$ have no rational point of height $o(H^{5/2})$.

papers.title: Dynamical conditions for tilting Neptune during planetary migration
papers.abstract: Giant planets are expected to form with near-zero obliquities, so that their current tilts must be the result of some post-formation processes. Capture into spin-orbit resonances has been shown to provide a viable mechanism for explaining the current obliquities of Jupiter, Saturn, and Uranus. We aim to determine whether specific configurations of a primordial satellite system of Neptune could have enabled the tilting of its spin axis during planetary migration. We modeled Neptune's secular spin-axis dynamics, including the presence of a primordial satellite system that enhanced the planet's precession constant. We numerically explored the conditions on the primordial satellite system that could trigger a spin-orbit resonance. We identified an open set in the parameter space that led to a successful tilting of Neptune. In particular, the total mass of the primordial system must have been $\geq 4\times 10^{-4}\,M_N$. A representative configuration consists of an inner satellite of mass $5\times 10 ^{-5}\,M_N$ and semi-major axis $35\,R_N$, and an outer satellite of mass $3.5\times 10 ^{-4}\,M_N$ and semi-major axis $100\,R_N$. Such a system could have survived during the unstable phase of the planetary migration if the gravitational encounters between Neptune and Uranus were not too close. The eventual ejection of the outer moon, possibly due to the encounter with a planetesimal, froze Neptune's obliquity to its current value. Neptune's current obliquity can be attained during planetary migration if the planet initially possessed a satellite system with a suitable architecture. The required satellite properties are not far from theoretical predictions and are consistent with recent scenarios proposed for the tilting of Uranus. Once the outer moon was ejected, the system matched a configuration suitable for the following capture of Triton and its fast evolution toward its current orbit.

authors.name: Andrea Moretti
authors.institution: Azienda Ospedaliera Citta' della Salute e della Scienza di Torino

papers.title: Positive recurrence of weakly reversible stochastic reaction networks with mass-action kinetics
papers.abstract: We study finite stochastic reaction networks with mass-action kinetics. A network is weakly reversible if every reaction lies on a directed cycle of complexes. We prove that, for arbitrary positive rate constants, the Markov chain of every such network is non-explosive and positive recurrent on each communicating class. This settles the long-standing chemical recurrence conjecture. The proof is by construction of a Lyapunov function. For a fixed choice of weights on the species, the function is the exponential of a weighted count of the molecules, adjusted by a bounded quantity which is defined through the paths of reactions leading back to a reference population, and which accounts for the species that are absent or scarce. Before the adjusted count can decrease, several preparatory steps may be needed. We count faster and slower steps separately, giving priority to paths that require fewer slow steps. Weak reversibility controls how competing reactions can change these counts. Finitely many choices of weights are then combined, and a minimization over a scale parameter gives a single function on each communicating class.

papers.title: R{\o}mer all ears: An auditory analog of Ole R{\o}mer's demonstration of the finite speed of light using smartphones as an acoustic vernier
papers.abstract: We present an undergraduate experiment for teaching Ole R{\o}mer's 1676 method for demonstrating the finite speed of light. Two smartphones emit periodic sound pulses whose synchronization is evaluated directly by the participants' hearing, acting as an "acoustic vernier" that achieves millisecond travel-time resolution without microphones or external sensors. Because the measurement relies strictly on propagation delays between stationary stations, it establishes a direct experimental analogy to R{\o}mer's original argument and dispenses with auxiliary wave phenomena absent from the 1676 analysis, such as acoustic beats or the Doppler effect. The pedagogical strength of the experiment lies precisely in this direct appeal to the senses. Loss of synchronization becomes perceptible starting at a separation of approximately 5 m and grows progressively clearer across several tens of meters. Despite its simplicity, systematic blind measurements determine the speed of sound in air with single-run uncertainties of 2 to 5 m/s (around 1%) and agree within 1.1% with theoretical predictions across ambient temperatures from 9 to 25 $^\circ$C. Beyond numerical measurement, anchoring the method in explicit sensory perception helps to clarify the recurring conceptual entanglement between R{\o}mer's geometric delay and the kinematic Doppler effect, while highlighting how this same travel-time principle underpins contemporary astrophysical techniques, such as pulsar timing and eclipse timing variations (ETV).

authors.name: Gabriel Antonio Carita
authors.institution: Deutsches Zentrum für Luft- und Raumfahrt e. V. (DLR)

papers.title: Thermal evolution of Uranus and Neptune, hydrogen-water phase separation and the role of methane
papers.abstract: Adiabatic evolution models of Uranus and Neptune with constant compositional stratification miss their observed luminosities: Uranus is fainter than commonly predicted, while improved equations of state (EoS) have recently led to a brightness problem for Neptune. In adiabatic models of Jupiter and Saturn, helium rain is thought to enhance luminosity. In the ice giants, hydrogen-water phase separation (H2-H2O demixing) with water rain has recently been predicted. We aim to understand how H2-H2O demixing and the EoS of water influence the luminosity of Uranus and Neptune. We use state-of-the-art EoS of H, He, H2O, and the H2-H2O phase diagram to build adiabatic three-layer models of the present-day structure that match the observed gravity field and the phase diagram. We compute evolution tracks with and without demixing, and for Neptune, with and without latent heat and methane, for which we provide an updated large-scale EoS including entropy. Without demixing, adiabatic Neptune with the revised AQUA EoS, without methane or latent heat, cools to its observed luminosity within 4.5 Gyr, in good agreement with the age of the Solar system. Applying the same assumptions to Uranus would require a Bond albedo of 0.43 to explain its luminosity. With demixing, the radii expand while the luminosity decreases. For Uranus, demixing leads to an equilibrium evolution with the incident flux that naturally explains its faintness. Demixing also makes Neptune fainter. Methane reduces the radius expansion but not the faintness problem. Favored Neptune models include demixing and methane at an initial C/O ratio of $\sim$1 due to CO ice accretion, with cooling times of $\lesssim 4 Gyr. Neptune requires an additional heat source unless its structure is primordial and the outer envelope is ice-poor, while hydrogen-water phase separation is an option to explain the structure and faintness of Uranus.

authors.name: Marina Cano Amoros
authors.institution: Deutsches Zentrum für Luft- und Raumfahrt e. V. (DLR)

authors.name: Nicola Tosi
authors.institution: Deutsches Zentrum für Luft- und Raumfahrt e. V. (DLR)

papers.title: Space Postman and ATLAS: Enabling Startup Participation in the Orbital Logistics Economy
papers.abstract: Debris removal, in-orbit servicing and refuelling, last-mile delivery, in-space recycling and constellation deployment are separate businesses built on one planning problem: a single spacecraft must visit many targets whose orbital planes drift apart under Earth's oblateness, within a propellant tank and a deadline. Solving it well takes orbital dynamics and optimisation expertise that is rarely the core business of payload, tug or constellation companies; this keeps young operators out of orbital logistics or leaves them with costly hand-made schedules. This paper presents Space Postman, a planning service that turns a target list, a spacecraft and a time budget into a priced and, for rendezvous tours, verified mission plan, and ATLAS, a tug concept whose payload bay takes debris kits, client spacecraft or propellant. As most start-ups fail when the money runs out, the offer starts with software and adds the vehicle later. Two case studies show what it changes. For a notional follow-on to the DEXTER project, which develops ways to turn scrap aluminium into propellant, it plans a tour of ten high-risk upper stages that share one orbital shell: waiting alone cannot close the tour, an even split of the time costs a third more propellant, and time is the currency of the mission. For a tug that releases eight clients from one rideshare, the delivery order decides whether the tank suffices, and the plan prices each delivery by the plane it must reach. The planning engine reproduces the published winning solution of a public debris-removal benchmark at that solution's fidelity and, given the same launches, plans cheaper trajectories for most of them: an independent check for operators and investors. A calibrated planner paired with a payload-agnostic tug offers new operators a practical way into orbital logistics, provided its numbers are read at the fidelity at which they were obtained.

authors.name: Omer Burak Iskender
authors.institution: Deutsches Zentrum für Luft- und Raumfahrt e. V. (DLR)

papers.title: A model colloidal gel former for the measurement of inter-particle forces
papers.abstract: Tracking of particle coordinates in colloidal model systems is an established technique. Recently, an emulsion system has been introduced where not only the coordinates, but also contacts and compressive forces between the droplets can be determined [Dong et al. J. Chem. Phys. 156 214907 (2022). Here we develop this system to control both the density mismatch and refractive index contrast between the emulsion droplets and the solvent. The former is important in minimizing sedimentation due to gravity and the latter is necessary for 3d imaging with confocal microscopy. By mapping our system carefully to computer simulation, we quantify interdroplet forces and packing geometries in depletion gels and probe the relationship between local structure and compressive stress. The simulations also provide ensemble measurements of the attractive part of the force between droplets and related quantities such as the stress tensor. Finally, we implement an improved measure of local stress in our experiments, which can be directly compared with the corresponding quantity in simulations. We find that locally rigid minimum energy clusters are associated with regions of higher stress in the gel network.

authors.name: Tanniemola B. Liverpool
authors.institution: Isaac Newton Institute for Mathematical Sciences

authors.name: C. Patrick Royall
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: An XR-Based System for Enhanced Spatial Awareness in Mobile Robot Teleoperation
papers.abstract: Teleoperation of mobile robots represents a critical capability for operations in hazardous environments, yet maintaining adequate situational awareness remains challenging without effective visualization and control interfaces. This work presents a multi-modal extended reality (XR) system for robot teleoperation and scene exploration that integrates immersive visual and haptic feedback modalities. To address motion sickness commonly induced by 360-degree camera feeds in head-mounted displays (HMDs), the system employs a fixed dual-camera configuration: a forward-facing camera for primary navigation and a rear-facing camera for enhanced situational awareness without operator discomfort. For navigation in confined or low-visibility conditions, a 16-channel Velodyne LiDAR generates real-time 2D occupancy grid maps, which are converted into vibrational haptic feedback on handheld controllers to provide intuitive, non-visual obstacle detection. User evaluation with 20 participants demonstrates that this haptic modality significantly reduces the cognitive load associated with obstacle avoidance during teleoperation.

papers.title: The Old Scene Lives in the Cache: Diagnosing and Shedding Stale History in Streaming Video Generation
papers.abstract: Switching scenes while preserving the original subject in streaming video generation exposes a conflict: cached history helps maintain the subject but also sustains old-scene objects that should disappear. Through controlled interventions on text conditioning, denoising steps, the local window, and the attention sink, we identify how cached visual history keeps this obsolete content. When the original frames remain in the cache, KV flush and sink recomputation still leave old-scene objects in the generated videos. Replacing this history with target-scene history largely removes those objects, but also changes the subject, reducing face similarity to the pre-switch subject. We then propose Molt Forcing, a training-free method that rebuilds scene history from a cold-start target scene while selectively retaining subject tokens from the original cache. Across 16 scene families, Molt Forcing removes old-scene objects at least as reliably as an Echo-Forcing hard cut while keeping the subject much closer to its pre-switch appearance.

authors.name: Hao Qin
authors.institution: Tianjin Medical University Cancer Institute and Hospital

papers.title: CrossCheck I: Cost Bounds of Imperative Programs as Constrained Optimization, with a Sound Cost Logic and a Verified Certificate Checker
papers.abstract: Static analysis of imperative programs often relies on iterative fixed-point approximations or concrete path exploration. We show that structured imperative control flow---while loops, linear recursion and branching recursion---can be mapped into constrained optimization problems over the free monoid of execution traces and the free algebra of computation trees. Ordering traces and trees by an intensional \textit{order-by-composition} ($\sqsubseteq$), halting is characterized as finding the minimal trace or tree that satisfies the exit condition, and we prove that this characterization coincides with the standard big-step semantics. Exact state recurrences are undecidable in general, so we relax them into cost envelopes, using ranking potentials and the tropical $(\max,+)$ reading of the timing schema, and obtain sound upper bounds on execution cost. The bounds compose over whole programs in a cost logic for a small language with nondeterministic actions, procedures, recursion and assumed contracts, which we prove sound for terminating and non-terminating executions. A linear instance of the logic has certificates---programs annotated with invariants, potentials and Farkas multipliers---and a checker that validates them with integer arithmetic only; an accepted certificate bounds the cost of every execution. All results, the checker and the worked examples are machine-checked in Lean~4. A companion paper describes a Clang plugin that produces such certificates and its evaluation.

papers.title: CrossCheck II: A Compiler Plugin for Certified Cost Bounds of Real-Time C and C++ Code, and its Evaluation
papers.abstract: We describe a plugin for the Clang compiler that bounds the cost of C and C++ functions intended for real-time use, and rejects at compile time the functions that allocate, throw, call through pointers, or contain a loop or a recursion for which no bound is found. Loops are bounded by affine ranking potentials synthesized with an SMT solver through Farkas' Lemma, or by logarithmic ones, recursion by depth and size potentials, and callees are analyzed in the calling context in which they are used. For functions in a linear fragment, the plugin emits a cost certificate that a checker, compiled from a Lean~4 definition proved sound in a companion paper, validates with integer arithmetic only; the bound then depends neither on the analyzer nor on the solver. On the 29 kernels of the TACLeBench collection, without annotations, the plugin bounds 142 of 220 loops in the calling contexts of the programs, 131 of them exactly as the benchmarks' flow facts, and 161 of the 165 bounded functions receive a certificate that the checker accepts, 152 of them also validated against an independent description of the source. On the CMSIS-DSP library for Cortex-M (786 functions), with assumed input ranges, it bounds 616 functions. We compare the loop bounds with loop counts observed by running the kernels and with five existing analyzers (LLVM's ScalarEvolution, KoAT2, CoFloCo, Infer and oRange), and the plugin with KoAT2 and CoFloCo on the C programs of the Termination and Complexity Competition: without annotations, 147 of 553 programs receive a certified bound that holds for all inputs, where the two tools bound 288 and 264. Loop bounds, exported annotations and the checker program are also tested on random programs and on mutated certificates.

papers.title: PRC4D: Physical Relation-Constrained Persistent 4D Reconstruction
papers.abstract: A faithful 4D reconstruction should capture both the shape and motion of objects, even when they disappear from view. Existing methods preserve previously observed geometry and extend motion through occlusion using local spatial and motion associations. However, treating short-term contact or shared motion as sufficient evidence of persistent rigidity can introduce incorrect motion constraints and distort overall reconstruction. To address this limitation, we present PRC4D, a physical relation-constrained framework that identifies reliable rigid relations and uses them to maintain spatial consistency through occlusion. PRC4D combines 3D contact and relative motion consistency with sequence-level verification to distinguish persistent couplings from transient interactions. The resulting graph guides observed-pose refinement and motion propagation from visible to occluded components without altering reconstructed geometry. Experiments on diverse real-world multi-object sequences and controlled occlusion simulations demonstrate improved reconstruction accuracy, reduced relative pose errors, and more consistent object configurations under changing visibility.

authors.name: Junho Kim
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Teichm\"uller spaces with conical singularities and Virasoro coadjoint orbits
papers.abstract:
We study Teichm\"uller spaces of hyperbolic \(0\)-metrics on a disk with ideal boundary and a marked point carrying a conical singularity with angle $\theta = 2\pi \beta$. For all $\beta>0$, we show that $\rm{Teich}^{\beta}(\overline{\mathbb D})\cong S^1\backslash \rm{Diff}(S^1)$, and we construct natural closed 2-forms $\omega_\beta$ induced by the Atiyah-Bott construction. For non-integer $\beta$, the form $\omega_\beta$ is symplectic, and one can identify $\rm{Teich}^{\beta}(\overline{\mathbb D})$ with the corresponding elliptic Virasoro coadjoint orbit.
  For positive integers $\beta=n$, $\omega_\beta$ is presymplectic, and it descends to the Kirillov-Kostant-Souriau symplectic form on the exceptional Virasoro orbit $\mathrm{PSU}^{(n)}(1,1)\backslash\rm{Diff}(S^1)$. Infinitesimal isometries of a hyperbolic \(0\)-metric on a disk with a conical singularity with angle $\theta=2\pi n$ are given by the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb R)$ which integrates to the group $\mathrm{PSU}^{(n)}(1,1)$ on the boundary of the disk but not in the interior for $n>1$. It is remarkable that the presymplectic structure of the corresponding Teichm\"uller spaces recovers this group and descends to the corresponding Virasoro coadjoint orbit.

papers.title: Turbulent Epidemics: Scale-dependent Fluctuations as a Probe of Population Heterogeneity
papers.abstract: Heterogeneous dynamics, including phenomena such as superspreading and clustering, is a hallmark of many infectious diseases. A key challenge lies in identifying observables that constrain heterogeneous dynamics. We here adapt the technique of turbulence decomposition from fluid dynamics to extract scale-dependent fluctuation spectra and correlation functions from disaggregated epidemiological data as a probe of population heterogeneity. To investigate possible explanations for the observed heterogeneities during the COVID-19 winter wave in Germany in 2020/21, we calculate synthetic observables using the new network-based simulation code \textsc{Epimetheus} for an idealized structured population. The code can flexibly incorporate clustering, heterogeneous connectivity and susceptibility, superspreading as well as temporal modulations of transmission risk and factors like waning of immunity and vaccination. A qualitative comparison of simulated and observed fluctuation spectra and correlation functions as well as the secondary attack rate and the overdispersion indicates that both clustering and variations of susceptibility across population substructures of all scales are required to produce the observed dynamics. Combined with heterogeneous connectivity, it is likely that self-limiting effects would have limited the winter outbreak to $0.2\texttt{-}0.35$ of the population without further behavioral changes after the autumn of 2020. A uniform population-wide reduction of transmission risk alone does not adequately explain the observed heterogeneities. Further analysis of the relative contributions and interplay of interventions and self-limiting effects on COVID-19 disease dynamics is required. We outline avenues towards a better integration of heterogeneity in models for predicting infectious disease dynamics and diagnosing effects of interventions.

papers.title: ArEssays: Towards Robust Arabic Handwritten Text Understanding in Educational Settings
papers.abstract:
Automated understanding of handwritten Arabic student essays remains challenging due to script complexity and high variability
  in children's writing. We introduce ArEssays, a large-scale dataset of authentic essays from primary to secondary students
  across Egypt, with both verbatim transcriptions and linguistically corrected versions. We benchmark 34 vision-language and OCR
  models, including fine-tuned systems, and find large performance gaps on real student handwriting. We release the dataset,
  training pipelines, and results to support research in Arabic OCR, document understanding, and educational NLP.

papers.title: A Text-to-SQL Benchmark for Official Statistics
papers.abstract: Official statistics are critical datasets for a wide variety of actors, including policymakers and businesses. For providers of official statistics, improving accessibility, governance, and disclosure of their data is of key importance. This can be improved by providing question-answering systems based on text-to-SQL approaches. However, existing text-to-SQL benchmarks do not resemble this setting. Official statistics are published as open-domain catalogs of thousands of wide tables whose columns and values are codes, and whose meaning is recorded in separate metadata rather than in a relational schema. To address this gap, we introduce LOCuST, a text-to-SQL benchmark that pairs over two thousand English and Dutch tables from Statistics Netherlands with a semantic knowledge graph. The graph describes the tables, measures, and dimension codes through labels, definitions, hierarchies, and units, and is the external knowledge a system needs to find the right tables and ground a question in the right codes. The benchmark includes expert-annotated questions for different query and aggregation types, including raw value retrieval, summations, proportion calculations, and joins. Alongside standard evaluation measures, we introduce an observation F1 metric that measures how close a query is to the ground truth even when the answers are different. We evaluate a variety of state-of-the-art LLMs and find that they struggle to write SQL that answers the questions correctly.

authors.name: Frank Pijpers
authors.institution: IMT School for Advanced Studies Lucca

papers.title: Predictive Self-Entropy in Dirichlet Universal Coding: A Factor-Two Central Limit Theorem and a Markov Extension
papers.abstract: Sequential universal coders produce both a realized log-loss and, before each symbol is observed, a predictive distribution with its own Shannon entropy. We compare the realized arithmetic code length with the cumulative predictive self-entropy, the prequential sum of the self-expected logarithmic scores of the issued forecasts. This forecast-only quantity is neither a plug-in entropy estimate nor a posterior entropy functional. For finite-alphabet memoryless sources and Dirichlet (add-$\alpha$) sequential predictors, we prove a joint central limit theorem for the two normalized quantities. They have the same first-order entropy limit but different second-order fluctuations: for every nonuniform i.i.d. source, cumulative predictive self-entropy has exactly twice the leading asymptotic variance of realized code length, and the ordinary mean-square-error ratio converges to two. We also give its logarithmic bias coefficient. For fixed finite-order Markov sources with context-wise Dirichlet predictors, the factor-two result becomes a context/innovation covariance decomposition, recovering the i.i.d. factor two when only the innovation component contributes.

papers.title: On the invertibility of saddle-point matrices: exact algebraic conditions and applications to constrained dynamics
papers.abstract: The solvability of constrained dynamical systems governed by D'Alembert--Lagrange mechanics relies directly on the invertibility of the coefficient matrix describing the underlying saddle-point structure, which couples system inertia with kinematic constraints. Standard formulations often rely on overly restrictive sufficient assumptions, such as global positive definiteness or semi-definiteness of the mass matrix, frequently combined with generalized inverses to handle singular mass distributions. In this work, we establish the purely necessary and sufficient algebraic conditions for matrix invertibility: the kinematic independence of the constraints and a kernel intersection condition between the allowed directions of motion and the induced inertial forces. We provide a physical interpretation of this requirement, demonstrating that it eliminates non-zero admissible motions whose generated inertial forces are entirely absorbed by constraint reactions. Furthermore, by completely avoiding generalized inverses, this formulation offers a unified and coordinate-free framework capable of handling massless components and indefinite inertia structures within a computationally robust setting.

papers.title: Late-time cosmic acceleration from matter inhomogeneities: constraints from DESI DR2 and SNe Ia
papers.abstract: We present the first observational constraints on the Misner-Sharp (MS) mass of the universe, within a newly proposed exact General Relativity solution providing a non-perturbative description of nonlinear cosmic structure formation. At early times, when statistical homogeneity and isotropy are satisfied, our model reduces to usual FLRW cosmology, accommodating Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) data. At late times, the departure from homogeneity and isotropy on scales $\lesssim 200$ Mpc -- codified in the scale-dependent redshift distribution of the MS mass -- naturally induces cosmic acceleration, through an extensive term generated by the MS mass asymptotic limit on large scales. We derive the MS mass from Baryon Acoustic Oscillation data from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) and Type Ia Supernovae, obtaining a value of the cosmological constant in agreement with $\Lambda$CDM results. We outline broader implications and future observational prospects, highlighting how multi-probe strategies -- particularly CMB lensing and the late Integrated Sachs-Wolfe effect -- can ultimately test this solution to the dark energy puzzle.

authors.name: Riccardo Murgia
authors.institution: Istituto Nazionale di Fisica Nucleare, Sezione di Cagliari

authors.name: Andrea P. Sanna
authors.institution: Istituto Nazionale di Fisica Nucleare, Sezione di Roma I

papers.title: Exterior $p$-capacitary rigidity on groups of Heisenberg type
papers.abstract:
We study the exterior Bernoulli overdetermined problem for sub-elliptic operators. Let $\mathbb{G}$ be a group of Heisenberg type with Property (H), and let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{G}$ be a domain enjoying a partial symmetry property and containing a Kor\'{a}nyi-Kaplan ball $\overline{B_r}$ centered at the origin. We consider a function $u$ that is $p$-harmonic with respect to the $p$-sub-Laplacian $\Delta_{\mathbb{G},p}$ in the annular region $\Omega \setminus \overline{B}_r$, satisfying the boundary conditions $
  u = 0 \;\text{ on }\; \partial\Omega,
  \quad
  u = 1 \;\text{ on }\; \partial B_r.$ We show that if $p$ is even and $u$ satisfies a mild overdetermined condition on the sub-Riemannian norm of its gradient on the outer boundary $\partial\Omega$, then $\Omega$ must itself be a Kor\'{a}nyi--Kaplan ball centered at the origin, and $u$ is the corresponding normalized capacitary potential; equivalently, away from the pole it is an affine normalization of the fundamental solution of $\Delta_{\mathbb{G},p}$.

papers.title: Tube-Based Robust Data-Driven Predictive Control for Linear Parameter-Varying Systems With Noisy Data
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a tube-based robust data-driven predictive control scheme for unknown discrete-time linear parameter-varying (LPV) systems using offline noisy input-scheduling-state data. We establish a multi-trajectory simplified LPV fundamental lemma yielding a collective Hankel representation of finite-horizon trajectories. Constraining the Hankel coefficients to a scaled simplex uniformly bounds the noise-induced predictor mismatch but may exclude relevant constrained lifted trajectories. A convex-hull coverage condition for admissible receding-horizon continuations restores the required representability. LPV data-consistency and robust positively invariant sets provide tube-tightening ingredients computed directly from noisy data. The online problem is a quadratic program, for which recursive feasibility, closed-loop constraint satisfaction, and practical input-to-state stability are established. Numerical results illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

papers.title: Rigidity for semiconvex entire solutions of Hessian quotient equations
papers.abstract: We prove that every smooth admissible semiconvex entire solution of $\sigma_k(D^2u)/\sigma_l(D^2u)=1$ in $\mathbb R^n$, where $0\le l<k\le n$ and $k-l=1$ or $2$, is a quadratic polynomial. The proof uses a shifted Legendre transform and interior Hessian estimates for Hessian quotient equations to reduce the problem to equations of lower order. We then conclude by induction on the order of the equation.

authors.name: Xingchen Zhou
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Reversible Self-Assembly of a P-Ir(100)-P Trilayer on Ir(111)
papers.abstract: Adsorbate-induced surface reconstructions offer a route to engineer low-dimensional materials with atomic arrangements and electronic properties fundamentally different from those of their parent substrates. Here, we demonstrate how phosphorus adsorption on Ir(111) drives the formation of an incommensurate P-Ir-P trilayer, in which a square Ir(100)-like atomic lattice emerges from the underlying hexagonal crystal. This transformation illustrates how strong adsorbate-substrate interactions can stabilize unconventional atomic coordination within an ultrathin metallic structure. Remarkably, the process is reversible, allowing the system to switch between distinct structural phases through phosphorus deposition and thermal annealing. The resulting trilayer exhibits a two-dimensional, semimetal-like electronic structure dominated by Ir 5d states. Our findings establish adsorbate-driven symmetry transformation as a strategy for engineering atomically thin transition-metal compounds with structural and electronic properties inaccessible through conventional surface growth.

authors.name: A. A. Makarova
authors.institution: Helmholtz-Zentrum Berlin für Materialien und Energie

papers.title: Lattice models of chiral random motion: A short review
papers.abstract: Chirality, a systematic rotational bias, is ubiquitous in many random motion patterns, from bacteria cells, that swim in circles near surfaces and spinning colloids, to charged particles diffusing under the influence of magnetic fields. In two dimensions, chirality renders random transport \textit{odd}: the diffusion tensor acquires an antisymmetric part that leaves the mean-squared displacement invariant but modifies fluxes and boundary currents. Lattice models for random motion are a natural setting to study chirality, since they are exactly solvable, connect directly to heterogeneous media, cellular automata, and programmable robots, and in discrete time admit fully chiral limits with a localised bulk and edge transport. Lattice walks with a rotational bias have been introduced in different communities several times since 1960, yet without a common language or conceptual connection between them. Here we review these models from the perspective that on the lattice, chirality requires memory. Taking the recently introduced chiral random walk model as a template, we describe the walker with an internal degree of freedom. With a chiral biased updating rule, the full diffusion tensor of this chiral walker turns odd. Within this picture, we can unite persistent and chiral walks, run-and-tumble motion, and cyclic random motions in one framework. We discuss how the memory is followed into the environment; in Lorentz lattice gases, kinetic and rotor walks, and random odd environments; and into the path; in spiral self-avoiding walks.

authors.name: J. Wojcik
authors.institution: Wrocław University of Science and Technology

authors.name: N. Sherf
authors.institution: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill

papers.title: High-density correlation energy of the electron gas
papers.abstract: The high-density expansion of the correlation energy per electron of the unpolarized three-dimensional electron gas, $\epsilon_c = A\ln r_s + B + C r_s\ln r_s + D r_s + \dots$, is used in many approximations to the correlation functional of density-functional theory. The coefficients $A$, $B$ and $C$ are known exactly. We revisit the three diagram classes used to estimate $D$, namely bare rings, rings with one first-order exchange insertion, and third-order diagrams with three distinct momentum transfers. Their sum is $-0.0077880(9)$ Ha per electron, compared with the earlier estimate of $-0.010$ Ha. The difference comes mainly from the coupling-constant weighting of the exchange rings in the calculation of Carr and Maradudin. At order $r_s^2$, seven contributions to the single-logarithm coefficient $E_1$ sum to $(3.653 \pm 0.010)\times 10^{-3}$ Ha per electron. The three long-wavelength contributions to the double-logarithm coefficient $E_2$ sum to $\alpha^2(36\pi^2 - 208\ln 2 - 221)/(192\pi^4) \approx -1.433\times 10^{-4}$ Ha per electron, where $\alpha = (4/9\pi)^{1/3}$. Available diffusion Monte Carlo energies at $r_s = 0.5$ cannot distinguish between the two estimates of $D$.

authors.name: Miguel A. L. Marques
authors.institution: Research Center Future Energy Materials and Systems

papers.title: AI-assisted formal proofs for static and time-dependent density functional theory on lattices
papers.abstract: The Hohenberg-Kohn theorem fails on lattices, where two potentials that differ by more than a constant can share a ground state. We prove that such potentials are exceptional. We consider spinless fermions on any connected lattice, at any filling other than empty or full, with hopping amplitudes of a common sign and any density-density interaction. The potentials whose ground state is shared with a potential differing by more than a constant lie in a closed, nowhere dense set of zero Lebesgue measure. The densities of non-degenerate shared ground states form a set of codimension at least two. The statement about the potentials also holds for the Kohn-Sham potential and for spin-density functional theory, where a uniform shift of the magnetic field is the only additional freedom. In time-dependent density functional theory on lattices, we show that not every ground state of a connected lattice can serve as the initial state of the density-potential map. A counterexample is the ground state of two fermions on a square that Penz and van Leeuwen found as a counterexample to the Hohenberg-Kohn theorem. For almost every static potential, however, every real ground state can serve as an initial state, also for spin-resolved densities. We also give formal proofs that the time-dependent Kohn-Sham potential exists, locally in time, for almost every static Kohn-Sham potential, and of known results: local existence and uniqueness of the time-dependent potential for an admissible initial state, continuation in time up to the boundary of the set of admissible states, and the convergence properties of a regularized Kohn-Sham iteration. All theorems and propositions are formalized in the proof assistant Lean 4 and checked by computer.

authors.name: Miguel A. L. Marques
authors.institution: Research Center Future Energy Materials and Systems

papers.title: Spoofing Wireless Sensing with Metasurfase-based Physical Deepfakes
papers.abstract:
Wireless communication networks are expanding from mere information transfer to sensing: in the Integrated Sensing and Communication paradigm, existing infrastructure and signals are reused to capture physical information about the surroundings of devices, envisioned to inform high-stakes applications such as healthcare and autonomous vehicles. From a security perspective, wireless sensing inherently trusts physical observations of the radio environment. However, as in wireless communication, the open nature of radio propagation allows attackers to tamper with victim signals. In particular, attackers can use programmable metasurfaces to manipulate wireless channels and thereby mislead sensing systems. Yet, prior metasurface-based manipulations target only individual channel features such as variance or Doppler shifts. Thus, they require knowledge of the victim sensing system and produce implausible channels that are easy to detect.
  In this work, we show that metasurfaces enable physically plausible manipulation of wireless sensing that is independent of the features used by the victim sensing system. Our attack reproduces genuine pre-recorded events at the physical layer and thereby synthesizes physical deepfakes of wireless channels. To this end, we develop an attack framework that controls the amplitude and phase of victim channels across time, frequency, and antennas. The key challenge here is to build a deep learning model of the interaction between metasurface and victim channel. We demonstrate that attackers can solve this challenge in several settings, e.g., by exploiting Wi-Fi Beamforming Feedback Information or replicating the victim environment. We validate the attack both in a controlled lab study on MIMO channels and with off-the-shelf Wi-Fi sensing. Our results fundamentally challenge the trustworthiness of wireless sensing.

authors.name: Christof Paar
authors.institution: Max Planck Institute for Security and Privacy

authors.name: Paul Staat
authors.institution: Max Planck Institute for Security and Privacy

papers.title: ab-indices for lattice path matroids
papers.abstract: The base polytopes of connected lattice path matroids admit subdivisions into snakes. We use these to obtain an explicit positive combinatorial description of their ab-indices, their Chow polynomials and their chain polynomials. We finally apply this description to the particular case of the ab-index of Schubert matroids.

papers.title: Mask-Based Speech Enhancement for Spatial Audio: Effects of Signal Representation and Channel-Specific Masking
papers.abstract: Speech enhancement for spatial audio needs to improve speech quality and intelligibility while preserving the spatial characteristics of the acoustic scene. Time-frequency masking provides an effective approach for speech enhancement, but its performance and spatial fidelity may depend strongly on the signal representation in which the mask is applied. This work systematically compares time-frequency masking in the microphone, beamformer, and first-order Ambisonics domains in simulated reverberant acoustic scenes. Both an ideal ratio mask (IRM) and a lightweight deep-learning-based mask estimator are considered, with performance evaluated in terms of speech reconstruction, perceptual quality, intelligibility, reverberation preservation, and binaural spatial-cue preservation. The results show that channel-specific masking in the beamformer domain provides the highest speech quality and intelligibility, while channel-specific masking in the Ambisonics domain better preserves the spatial characteristics of the residual interference. Reducing the spatial representation from third- to first-order Ambisonics substantially reduces the performance gap between the beamformer and Ambisonics domains due to the lower spatial resolution of the resulting beamformers. Furthermore, a shared mask across first-order Ambisonics channels achieves speech enhancement performance close to that of channel-specific masking while requiring only a single mask-estimation network. These results demonstrate that the choice of signal representation and masking strategy should be considered jointly, and indicate that first-order Ambisonics with shared masking provides a practical compromise between speech enhancement performance, spatial fidelity, and computational complexity.

papers.title: PublicnEUro: A FAIR and TRUSTworthy infrastructure for controlled access to human neuroimaging data
papers.abstract: Sharing brain imaging data supports secondary analysis and reproducibility, but privacy risks and differing legal and governance requirements can make unrestricted release inappropriate. The PublicnEUro repository was developed to support discovery and reuse under diverse legal requirements. Here, PublicnEUro's governance, architecture, BIDS-based deposition and curation, metadata and identifier services as well as open and controlled retrieval workflows are described. We then assess the repository published datasets against FAIR subprinciples and the repository public information against TRUST principles. The FAIR assessment shows strong findability and public metadata accessibility. The TRUST assessment documents governance, stewardship, continuity provisions and technical safeguards. Together this demonstrates that PublicnEUro, by separating open discovery from governed data retrieval, supports FAIR-aligned and trustworthy reuse of sensitive brain imaging data without requiring unrestricted disclosure.

authors.name: Peter S Jensen
authors.institution: University of Arkansas for Medical Sciences

papers.title: CAPE: Coordinating Calibration and Search for Tool-Use Policies
papers.abstract: A tool call can fail even when the operation behind it is correct, because the receiving tool parses delimiters, dates or record layouts under a configuration the agent cannot inspect. Compiling a tool-use policy for such a tool requires both calibration, which evaluates candidate calls on candidate configurations, and search over the evaluated calls. The two share one compilation budget: calibrating everything first postpones any improved policy until the end, while re-solving every partially known model delays the next useful query. A call becomes usable as soon as its effects are known on the configurations that reach it. We present CAPE, a training-free compiler built on this observation. It maintains an executable policy at all times, directs calibration to the calls that can improve this policy, and tightens bounds only where doing so ends calibration early. Returned policies preserve every configuration the initial policy completes, and CAPE certifies optimality when its executable and optimistic values meet. On CSV and JSON workflows built from 64 requests, CAPE reaches the independently computed optimum in 502 of 504 compilations while taking 22.0% less compilation time than eager exact search. On larger CSV families it returns policies with higher completion at similar compilation time, and it raises completion by 15.38 to 34.66 percentage points over an LLM that revises its serialization from error feedback.

authors.name: Jiahao Wang
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: What to Change, What to Keep: Experience-Evolving Agents for Video Recasting
papers.abstract: Video recasting aims to transform the entities and environments of existing videos into new visual worlds while preserving their essential actions and interactions. However, achieving coherent transformations remains challenging, as coordinated edits can disrupt the original event structure. In this paper, we introduce RecastAgent, an experience-guided agentic framework for source-conditioned video recasting that operates under frozen model weights. Our framework employs an Experience-Guided Planner to choose edit prompts and input video states under qualitative visual critique, allowing the agent to build upon partial progress or backtrack to preserve source structure. Across tasks, an Experience Accumulation module distills completed trajectories into conditional, evidence-linked principles that record both an editing strategy and its scope of validity. We additionally construct a benchmark of 67 source videos with 134 paired-specification tasks across six creative categories for evaluation. Experiments demonstrate that RecastAgent outperforms single-pass and agentic rewriting baselines across Bernini and Ditto. Furthermore, accumulated experience improves performance on held-out test videos and transfers zero-shot to external benchmarks like FiVE-Bench and VE-Bench.

papers.title: Sub-Riemannian Distances on Lie Groups: Tangent Asymptotics and Hermitian Matrix Formulas
papers.abstract:
Let $d_{\mathrm{SR}}$ be the Carnot--Carath\'{e}odory distance associated with a two-step Lie pair and let $d_0$ be the distance on its nilpotent tangent group. For compact Lie pairs we prove, locally uniformly in $(X,Z)$, \[
  d_{\mathrm{SR}}\!\left(e,\exp(rX+r^2Z)\right)^2
  =r^2d_0(e,(X,Z))^2+O(r^3). \] For symmetric pairs, the remainder improves to $O(r^4)$. This order is sharp in general, and the estimate remains uniform at cut points, abnormal endpoints, and points where the tangent endpoint map changes rank. If the tangent minimizer is unique, the endpoint differential is onto, and the constrained Hessian is coercive, we determine the coefficient of $r^4$ with remainder $O(r^6)$. For block subgroups of $\mathrm{SU}(N)$, we express the vertical squared distance on the tangent group as the attained minimum of a finite-dimensional functional on Hermitian matrices subject to linear constraints on their partial traces. Every minimizer gives a minimizing loop represented by a trigonometric polynomial. For one $m$-dimensional block and $q$ scalar blocks, the coefficient has weights $\lceil j/q\rceil$ and reduces to a trace norm formula when $q\ge\lfloor m/2\rfloor$.

authors.name: Zhicheng Han
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Zhipeng Yang
authors.institution: University College London Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust

papers.title: PromptSMC: Enabling Particle Exploration in Flow Matching via LLM-Based Prompt Rejuvenation
papers.abstract: This paper is concerned with prompt-image alignment at inference time through exploration of generative trajectories and dynamical prompt rejuvenation. We leverage sequential Monte Carlo (SMC), to offer a gradient-free and principled framework for this purpose through reward-guided trajectory selection. More specifically, we introduce LLM-based prompt rejuvenation, allowing for efficient particle exploration in SMC samplers along the diffusion time in flow matching models. The proposed method, PromptSMC, retains the selected latent states and uses a pretrained LLM to dynamically revise the prompts of duplicated particles under semantic-preservation constraints. These revised prompts induce alternative conditional velocity fields, allowing particles to explore different continuations from a shared intermediate state. The method further uses a reward model to evaluate each particle's alignment with the original prompt, and the resulting scores guide particles through resampling. PromptSMC thus integrates prompt-based exploration with reward-guided sampling, achieving faithful prompt-image alignment without additional noise injection, model training, or reward gradients. Our experiments and ablation studies across multiple benchmarks and backbones demonstrate the effectiveness of the method for text-to-image flow matching. Code is available at https://github.com/shermanlian/PromptSMC.

papers.title: Identifying the critical mass in a quasilinear chemotaxis model with indirect signal production
papers.abstract: The mass threshold separating boundedness and unboundedness of global solutions to a critical quasilinear parabolic-elliptic chemotaxis model with indirect signal production is identified in the radially symmetric setting in a ball. Specifically, solutions emanating from initial values with mass below a critical mass M\textsubscr{c} > 0, which is characterized in terms of a variant of the Hardy-Littlewood-Sobolev inequality, are global and bounded. In contrast, for any M > M\textsubscr{c}, there are initial values with mass M such that the corresponding global solutions are unbounded. The proof relies on the variational structure of the system and a detailed study of the stationary states.

papers.title: How Use Case Tables Enable the Elicitation of Explanation Needs
papers.abstract: [Context and motivation] While software systems get more integrated into people's daily lives - like driver-assistance systems or smart-home applications - they are also becoming increasingly complex. When complex software is used, needs for explanations may arise. At present, explanation needs are usually elicited through the testing of prototypes or existing software. However, detailed documentation of software interactions, such as use case tables, might be a suitable alternative. Since use cases provide early insights into the key interactions within the system, they are appealing to employ as resources for explanation needs. [Question/problem] As of now, it remains unclear whether use cases allow the elicitation of explanation needs. Or, from a different perspective, whether their utilization for this purpose is desirable. [Principal ideas/results] We conducted a study in which users perused the description sections of use cases extracted from existing software. While reading through these use cases, they reported any explanation needs they encountered. Our findings indicate that use case steps are sufficient to induce explanation needs in the participants as they read the steps. [Contribution] This paper explores the novel idea of utilizing use cases for the elicitation of explanation needs and reports on a study that provides insights into the applicability of this concept with stakeholders.

papers.title: Ancient solutions of mean curvature flow in a slab
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study complete ancient solutions of the mean curvature flow in arbitrary codimension contained in slabs in Euclidean space. Under a natural principal-angle condition, we prove that a translating soliton contained in a slab of width less than $\pi$ cannot be bounded from below in the translating direction, and characterize the grim reaper cylinder in form of a rigidity result at the critical width $\pi$. We derive corresponding results for ancient solutions confined in slabs.

papers.title: Robust inverse dielectric design of skin phantoms for implantable wireless link evaluation
papers.abstract: Skin phantoms support reproducible evaluation of implantable wireless links, yet published complex permittivities of skin predict different propagation losses. We formulate a robust inverse design to determine a homogeneous phantom permittivity that minimizes the largest channel-loss difference across selected skin reference models, incidence angles and both transverse-electric and transverse-magnetic polarizations. Computed candidates and analytical lower bounds bracket the optimal mismatch and constrain the critical depth. Across seven frequencies from 5 to 500 GHz, the minimax mismatch at 1.3 mm ranges from 1.13 to 13.72 dB. For a 3 dB tolerance, suitable permittivities exist at every investigated depth at 5 GHz, while critical depths at the other frequencies range from 0.23 to 1.01 mm. Only one of seven material cases from the literature meets a 6 dB tolerance at 1.3 mm. These results translate channel-loss tolerances into quantitative design criteria for skin phantoms used in implantable wireless link evaluation.

authors.name: Ali Alhaj Abbas
authors.institution: King Fahd University of Petroleum and Minerals

papers.title: Moir\'e-Induced Interlayer Electron-Phonon Coupling in Graphene/hBN Superlattices
papers.abstract: Electron-phonon coupling (EPC) plays a vital role in the electrical and optical properties of materials, ranging from superconductivity to charge dynamics. In moir\'e superlattices, out-of-plane vibrations can modulate the moir\'e potential and enhance interlayer EPC. Here we report the first direct observation of a resonance arising from coupling between moir\'e electronic excitations and phonons in graphene-based moir\'e superlattices. Using Fourier-transform infrared photocurrent spectroscopy, we detect the nominally silent hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) out-of-plane optical (ZO) phonon as a pronounced absorption peak. The phonon interferes with moir\'e flat-band excitations to form a characteristic Fano resonance. Displacement field-dependent measurements confirm that the feature originates from coupling to the moir\'e electronic continuum rather than simple zone folding. We further observe similar resonances in devices with different graphene layer numbers and twist configurations. This enhanced EPC provides a pathway for understanding and controlling emerging quantum phenomena, such as superconductivity, and engineering novel optoelectronic devices.

authors.name: Hongyuan Li
authors.institution: Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications

authors.name: Feng Wang
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Computing expectations associated with McKean--Vlasov stochastic differential equations via probability-flow ordinary differential equations
papers.abstract: This work considers the numerical approximation of expectations of functionals of $d$-dimensional McKean--Vlasov stochastic differential equations (MV-SDEs) with random initial conditions. Standard numerical schemes employ a stochastic interacting particle system of $P$ coupled $d$-dimensional SDEs, whose empirical measure converges to the MV-SDE law. However, naive Euler--Maruyama Monte Carlo (MC) estimators based on particle systems achieve a computational complexity of $\mathcal{O}\left( \text{TOL}^{-4} \right)$ to satisfy a prescribed error tolerance TOL. To reduce this complexity, this work reformulates the associated nonlinear Fokker--Planck equation as a Liouville equation describing the evolution of the law of a deterministic mean-field ordinary differential equation (ODE) with random initial conditions, sharing the same marginal distributions as the original MV-SDE. The resulting mean-field ODE eliminates the need to approximate It\^{o} integrals and permits the use of higher-order integration schemes in time and stochastic space. However, simulating trajectories requires the score function of the MV-SDE's marginal law, which is approximated using a statistical estimator based on a system of $P$ coupled $d$-dimensional ODEs. The proposed estimator combines randomized quasi-MC in the stochastic variables and Runge--Kutta integrators in time, with efficient score estimation. Under assumptions on weak-error and variance convergence, the resulting estimator achieves a computational complexity of $\mathcal{O}\left(\text{TOL}^{-\left(\max\{\beta/\alpha,2\} + 1/\gamma \right)}\right)$, where $\alpha$ and $\beta$ denote, respectively, the weak-error and variance convergence rates with respect to $P$, and $\gamma$ is the order of the time-integration scheme.

authors.name: Shyam Mohan Subbiah Pillai
authors.institution: King Abdullah University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Multistable Thermoelectric Josephson Automata
papers.abstract: Multistable systems can store and process information, yet their elements usually only burn the drive energy. Here, we build an automaton whose elements actively convert heat into electrical power. Heat alone stabilizes the states at zero bias, and each state routes generation and dissipation to different junctions. The elements, gap-asymmetric superconducting tunnel junctions, deliver up to 2.6 pW at either polarity under fixed heating and support a magnetic-field-tunable Josephson current. Two junctions sharing a heated island split the bias hysteretically and, even at zero bias, lock into opposite voltages encoding the sweep direction. With a load and current bias, the automaton accesses states spanning junction polarity combinations, including zero voltage; the magnetic field sets which are available and the bias history selects the occupied one.

papers.title: Weighted pointwise estimates for the damped wave equation and global solutions to Nakao's problem in three dimensions
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish weighted pointwise estimates for the Duhamel term of the three-dimensional damped wave equation. The estimates combine the parabolic weight $\langle t+|x|^2\rangle$ with the wave-cone weight $\langle t-|x|\rangle$, and thereby account for both the diffusive part of the damped wave flow and source terms with wave-like decay. As an application, we study Nakao's problem, a weakly coupled system consisting of one semilinear damped wave equation and one semilinear wave equation. Under explicit conditions on the exponents of nonlinear terms, we prove small-data global existence and uniqueness of mild solutions in weighted $L^\infty$ spaces. The result covers both the full parabolic decay and slower pointwise decay for the damped-wave component, and allows either the standard wave decay or slower pointwise decay for the wave component. The proof combines the new Duhamel estimate with weighted estimates for the free wave equation and a contraction argument.

papers.title: Dynamic scaling behaviors induced by periodic drivings at continuous Ising quantum transitions
papers.abstract: We investigate the out-of-equilibrium scaling behaviors induced by periodic driving protocols in quantum many-body systems near continuous quantum phase transitions at zero temperature. We consider two paradigmatic one-dimensional systems: the quantum Ising chain subject to periodic longitudinal fields and the Kitaev fermionic wire with periodically driven chemical potentials, equivalent to a quantum Ising chain with a periodic transverse field. Within a renormalization-group (RG) framework, we develop a dynamic scaling theory for both finite-size systems and the thermodynamic limit, identifying scaling variables associated with the driving amplitude and period.
