papers.title: A Barsotti-Weil isomorphism for Taelman units
papers.abstract: The positive-characteristic analogue of motivic cohomology with coefficients in an Anderson A-motive M over a function field of transcendence degree one was introduced in an earlier work of the author. In this paper, we prove that, when M arises as the dual of the A-motive of an Anderson module E that is abelian, uniformizable, and has everywhere good reduction, the corresponding A-motivic cohomology coincides with the module of Taelman units of E, up to a twist by the module of K\"ahler differentials of A. To this end, we recast the theory of Anderson generating functions in the spirit of earlier work of Maurischat and the author on special functions.

papers.title: Is Prosody Encoded in the Neural Audio Codec Mimi?
papers.abstract: Neural audio codecs (NACs) have become a fundamental infrastructure for modern speech-language models, discretizing continuous speech signals into token sequences that enable large language models to process and generate audio. Most research evaluates codec quality at the decoding phase, assessing the naturalness of reconstructed speech. However, little research investigates what phonetic information is captured during encoding. In this paper, we investigated the potential correlates of prosody in the NAC Mimi, a codec used by conversational speech agents such as Moshi and Sesame and used in downstream tasks such as speech-to-speech translation (Hibiki).

authors.name: Erin Pacquetet
authors.institution: University at Buffalo, State University of New York

papers.title: Local subspace encoding for spectral prediction: from TabPFN to operator-adaptive calibration
papers.abstract: TabPFN has already shown useful predictive performance on near-infrared spectra. RamanPFN subsequently proposed two spectral representations for tabular inference: Global Compositional Unmixing (GCU) and Local Vibrational Subspace Encoding (LVSE). We assess whether these representations also help on datasets assembled through the nirs4all ecosystem, and whether their value extends to classical calibration. We reanalyse completed experiments from a public spectral dataset catalogue. On a post-hoc subset of 61 matched numerical prediction tasks, after excluding ten class-code, metadata or semantically ambiguous targets, LVSE reduces RMSE relative to raw-spectrum TabPFN by 10.22%, 12.80% and 14.52% on average for checkpoints 2.5, 3 and 3.5, respectively, with median reductions of 4.99%, 4.74% and 7.82%. Across 76 classification datasets, weighted F1 increases by 2.22, 2.56 and 3.81 percentage points. The 2.5 classification procedure uses output coding on 15 datasets exceeding the checkpoint's native class limit. GCU alone is less reliable in this implementation. LVSE also improves PLS and Ridge in many cases, with median RMSE reductions of 4.75% and 1.89%. Adding LVSE candidates to an operator-adaptive model is feasible, but a separate 35-task panel derived from the public AOM benchmark shows only small median gains. These results motivate evaluating LVSE alongside existing representation choices. They do not establish that a selector choosing between raw and LVSE inputs will improve every task.

papers.title: Strong-lensing tests of angular structure in the radial acceleration relation
papers.abstract: The radial acceleration relation (RAR) links the radial acceleration inferred from galaxy rotation curves to that predicted from the observed baryonic distribution. Whether it has a counterpart in the angular structure of gravitational fields remains unknown. We develop an observational framework to test for such a non radial correspondence using strong gravitational lenses, without assuming that a generalized RAR exists. The singular perturbative approach reconstructs two angular fields from lensed image morphology without imposing a parametric mass profile. We separate contributions from projected mass inside and outside the Einstein circle, normalize the inner baryonic and total fields, and define statistical comparisons of their radial and tangential components. We also derive higher order potential multipoles for a smooth elliptical, off centered projected halo and evaluate their dependence on NFW and Einasto profiles. The inner outer separation isolates the projected internal contribution most directly relevant to the RAR comparison. The inner dipole coefficients can be recovered without the source position contribution when both reconstructed fields are used. The quadrupole phase provides a measure of projected orientation, while the higher order moments quantify departures from a smooth elliptical profile. For the profiles and parameter ranges considered, the predicted higher order ratios remain small and vary only moderately with the Einstein radius to scale radius ratio. The framework provides a model independent observational test of whether a three dimensional non radial baryonic Total field correspondence leaves a statistical imprint after projection. The large strong lens population expected from Euclid could provide the sample needed for this test, subject to image quality, photometric, and selection function requirements.

authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Diffs Are Cheap, Show Me the Trajectory: An Empirical Study of Trajectory-Informed Code Review
papers.abstract: Code review typically starts from the final diff. However, the diff reveals little about how the code was developed. Coding-agent trajectories preserve intermediate decisions, failed attempts, and validation evidence that may assist code review. We systematically investigate whether and how these trajectories can help independent review agents identify problems in the resulting code, beyond inspecting the final diff and repository. We develop a procedure that generates review comments by comparing the initial and merged versions of pull requests, and assess it against withheld human review comments. Using held-out reference implementations as comparison targets for agent-produced code, we construct a dataset linking 339 implementations of 113 DeepSWE tasks with their trajectories and 882 synthetic reference review comments. Across three coding-agent configurations and two review harnesses, we compare diff-only review, full-trajectory access, and four alternative ways of presenting and using trajectories. Full-trajectory access raises mean reference recall from 23.03% to 25.87%, but improves recall in only four of six configurations. All four alternatives improve mean reference recall over diff-only by between 4.05 and 7.32 percentage points. The gains also extend to review comments that explain task-verifier failures. Higher recall can require more tokens and longer review time, while simpler trajectory views remain competitive. These results support development trajectories as an additional source of code-review context and show that their benefits and resource costs depend on how they are presented and used.

authors.name: Zijian Luo
authors.institution: Civil Aviation Flight University of China

papers.title: Ranking honeybee breeder colonies: a probabilistic method using vine copulas to consider multiple criteria
papers.abstract: Ranking honeybee colonies according to multiple performance criteria is central to selection in bee breeding, but deterministic scores provide limited information about how a selected colony compares with the population of available colonies. We propose a population-calibrated probabilistic score based on a weighted Euclidean distance to an ideal colony and an estimation of the joint distribution of the data. For a candidate colony, the probability-score is the probability that a colony drawn from a reference population outperforms the candidate. We estimate the dependence structure among criteria using a vine copula after apiary-specific rank transformations, allowing different marginal distributions while modelling a common dependence structure. Importantly, the joint distribution calibrates the distance into a probability but does not change the ordering induced by a fixed distance and weight vector. We apply the method to 265 observations from eight French and Italian apiaries during the 2024 and 2025 seasons. Dependence among the four criteria is weak in this dataset, and the vine-copula and independence probability-scores are therefore similar. A simulation study evaluates probability-score estimation under a range of dependence structures, while bootstrap and apiary-subset analyses quantify sensitivity to sampling and study composition. We additionally assess preference robustness by evaluating the proportion of admissible weight vectors for which a colony belongs to the top ranking. The framework provides an interpretable and reproducible population-relative score for multi-criteria colony selection.

papers.title: Depth of leaves in closed linear $\lambda$-terms: exact recurrence, limit law and edge window
papers.abstract: Let $K_n$ (resp.\ $D_n$) be the depth of a uniform leaf (resp.\ node) in a uniform closed linear $\lambda$-term of size $n$. A bijective \emph{grafting identity} yields an exact polynomial-time recurrence for the full depth profile. By the method of moments, $K_n/n$ converges in law to the density $3x/\sqrt{1-2x}$ on $[0,\frac12]$, i.e.\ $2K_n/n\to\Beta(2,\frac12)$, with $\mathbb E[K_n^r]/n^r\to3(r+1)!/(2r+3)!!$; likewise $1-2D_n/n\to\Beta(\frac12,1)$. A backward Markov chain gives the corresponding local limits for $k\le(\frac12-\varepsilon)n$. The limit density diverges at $\frac12$, and the profile has a second scale: a window of width $\sqrt n$ around $n/2$, which carries a fraction of order $n^{-1/4}$ of the nodes, at a density $n^{1/4}$ times larger than in the bulk. We prove that a single explicit function describes both regimes: uniformly in $d$, \[ n^{3/4}\,\mathbb P(D_n=d)=g\Bigl(\tfrac{d-n/2}{\sqrt n}\Bigr)+O(n^{-1/16}),\qquad n^{3/4}\,\mathbb P(K_n=d)=\tfrac{3d}{n}\,g\Bigl(\tfrac{d-n/2}{\sqrt n}\Bigr)+O(n^{-1/16}), \] where $g(y)=2^{-1/2}e^{-y^2}D_{-1/2}(2y)$ is a parabolic cylinder function. In particular $\mathbb P(K_n>n/2)\sim\frac34\,\mathbb E|Z|^{1/2}\,n^{-1/4}\approx0.6166\,n^{-1/4}$ with $Z$ standard Gaussian. The proofs rest on harmonic functions of the heat equation evaluated along the backward chain.

authors.name: Olivier Bodini
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Self-gravitating dust clumps: linear theory sets the threshold, the onset time and the spacing of their formation, then slow coarsening erases this pattern
papers.abstract: Planets form in disks of gas and dust. One step of their formation is the gathering of dust grains into dense clumps, under their own gravity. This work tries to predict when these clumps appear and how far apart they are. The grains attract each other through a gravity of finite range. The gas slows them down, and its turbulence spreads them out. The grains also cannot go beyond maximum packing: this is volume filling. The dimensionless model depends on two numbers. The first one is the gravitational number $\chi$, which compares attraction with turbulent spreading. The second one is the mean volume fraction $\rho_b$, which measures the amount of grains. We solve the model with second-order finite volumes on an adaptive Cartesian mesh. We then treat each field as an image. An Otsu threshold and a watershed transform isolate the clumps. The code conserves mass to within $10^{-15}$ and converges at second order. Two designs of experiments give 192 simulations in total, with $2\le\chi\le40$ and $0.05\le\rho_b\le0.7$. Linear stability theory predicts the start of clump formation. The instability starts at time $t_{on}\simeq3.0/\sigma^*$, where $\sigma^*$ is the growth rate of the most amplified mode. The dominant wavelength equals the most amplified wavelength to within $10\%$. The area fraction of the clumps equals $\rho_b$. The clumps then go through slow coarsening. A sensitivity analysis attributes most of the variance to $\chi$. The adaptive mesh reduces the computational cost only a little, because the clumps fill the whole domain.

papers.title: Constraining the Leptonic and Hadronic Contributions to the Gamma-Ray Emission of SNR HESS J1731-347 with CTAO Forecasts
papers.abstract: We present a Bayesian broadband spectral analysis of the supernova remnant HESS J1731-347, combining archival radio, X-ray, and H.E.S.S. data with a new analysis of 16 yr of Fermi-LAT observations. The LAT data allow the GeV emission of the western molecular-cloud core (MC-core) to be separated from that of the remaining shell. We fit purely leptonic and lepto-hadronic models with and without the MC-core region. Within a one-zone model with fixed distance and ambient density, the lepto-hadronic scenario is strongly preferred by the Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC) in both cases. Excluding the MC-core, we obtain $\Delta{\rm BIC}=33.67$, a magnetic field of $B = 84.9^{+27.5}_{-22.9}$ $\mu$G, a hard proton index of $\alpha_p = 1.69 \pm 0.10$, and a proton energy of $W_p = (4.37^{+0.64}_{-0.51})\times10^{48}$ erg for $n_{\rm H}=20$ cm$^{-3}$. The preference for a hadronic contribution is therefore not driven by the MC-core emission alone. CTAO simulations show that a 50 h observation with the southern array would detect the source at $13\sigma$ to $18\sigma$ and substantially improve the constraints on its TeV spectrum.

authors.name: D. B. Gotz
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Airy Path Integral Representation for the Kadomtsev-Petviashvili Equation
papers.abstract:
We give a representation for solutions of the Kadomtsev-Petviashvili II (KP-II) equation as path integrals over the Airy line ensemble. The initial condition enters directly as a potential, bypassing the usual direct and inverse scattering constructions. We establish the representation for broad classes of signed initial data, prove uniqueness in specified solution classes, and derive a restart identity expressing solutions as Airy path integrals of their own earlier states. For arbitrary real $L^2$ initial data, a centered version of the Airy occupation represents the standard global KP-II flow.
  We show how the representation recovers the classical Marchenko determinant for Korteweg-de Vries (KdV), and identify a Brownian-path amplitude with the classical KP-II heat-scattering coefficient. We obtain explicit formulas for soliton solutions and derive KP from a Toda equation for nonintersecting Brownian bridges. Finally, we use the restart identity to characterize one-point distributions of the KPZ fixed point through their singular initial conditions, and derive sharp lower-tail asymptotics directly from KP.

papers.title: Hi3R-VLA: Grounding Semantics and Actions in 3D
papers.abstract: While recent vision-language-action (VLA) models increasingly incorporate 3D geometry, how to effectively exploit it for precise and generalizable action prediction remains a central challenge. We introduce Hi3R-VLA, a 3D policy that grounds heterogeneous modalities - vision, language, and action - in explicit 3D geometry for robotic manipulation. Our model integrates spatially-aligned visual features and language conditioning into point cloud representations, enriching scene geometry with fine-grained, task-relevant semantics. It then anchors low-level control commands in the same 3D coordinate frame and uses 3D-RoPE enhanced action-to-point attention over coarse-to-fine point features to model geometric relationships between action targets and observed points. Our analysis demonstrates the importance of semantic fusion within 3D and spatial alignment between observations and actions. With fewer than 250M trainable parameters, Hi3R-VLA achieves state-of-the-art performance on RoboCasa, RLBench, RoboTwin2, DexJoCo and DexSuite across diverse manipulation tasks and embodiments, from single-arm and dual-arm grippers to dexterous hands. Real-robot evaluations further demonstrate its effectiveness in the physical world. The model, code and dataset are publicly released at https://cshizhe.github.io/projects/hi3r_vla.html.

papers.title: An Introduction to Semialgebraic Geometry
papers.abstract: The first chapter of these lecture notes explains algorithms for counting real roots and the Tarski-Seidenberg theorem. In the next two chapters we study semialgebraic subsets of $\mathbb R^n$ , which are defined by boolean combinations of polynomial equations and inequalities. The main tool for this study is the cylindrical algebraic decomposition, which is introduced in Chapter 2. The principal result of Chapter 3 is the triangulation theorem. This theorem shows that semialgebraic sets have a simple topology, which can be effectively computed from their definitions. Chapter 4 contains examples of finiteness results and uniform bounds for semialgebraic families. In particular, we give an explicit bound for the number of connected components of a real algebraic set as a function of the degree of the equations and the dimension of the ambient space.

papers.title: Fairness and incentives in combinatorial assignment
papers.abstract: We consider the fair and efficient random assignment of indivisible goods subject to resource constraints. Agents receive bundles randomly, but individual lotteries over bundles that are feasible in expectation need not be jointly feasible. Consequently, we treat a lottery over feasible allocations as a public good. We show that every feasible finite economy admits an envy-free and Pareto efficient random assignment that may be supported as a Lindahl equilibrium. For a finite type space with specified expected utilities, we construct a mechanism whose outcomes are exactly feasible and Pareto efficient with respect to reported preferences. As the population grows and empirical type proportions and per-capita resources approach a limiting large economy, envy and gains from manipulation vanish. The approximate incentive compatibility of the mechanism holds for all type profiles that approximate the limiting economy. The argument combines sensitivity bounds for linear programs with proximity bounds between fractional and integer optima.

papers.title: H$_3^+$ forbidden rotational lines in a planetary nebula: JWST/MIRI detection in the Ring Nebula and ionization by the central star
papers.abstract: We report the detection of the forbidden pure rotational spectrum of H$_3^+$ in the Ring Nebula (NGC 6720), to our knowledge the first detection of H$_3^+$ in a planetary nebula. In JWST/MIRI spectra obtained toward the inner edge of the main ring, 0.1 pc in projection from the central star, the $(J,K) = (5,0)\to(4,3)$ line at 16.325 $\mu$m is detected at $32\sigma$, along with nine further unblended lines. The H$_3^+$ emission spatially follows the H$_2$ emission, whose rotational lines show warm (660 K) and hot (1700 K) components. A statistical-equilibrium model at these temperatures reproduces the subthermal H$_3^+$ line pattern, with much of the emission arising in the hot H$_2$. The emission requires an H$_2$ ionization rate of $\sim 3\times 10^{-12}\,{\rm s^{-1}}$ in the hot H$_2$ for an electron fraction of $2\times 10^{-4}$. The rate is $\sim 2\times 10^4$ times the cosmic-ray ionization rate in diffuse clouds. The extreme-ultraviolet and soft X-ray radiation (54-300 eV) of the 135 kK central star supplies this rate if the hot H$_2$ lies within an H-nucleus column density of (4-8)$\times 10^{19}\,{\rm cm^{-2}}$ of the ionization front of the dense globules. Static photoionization models, however, place the H$_2$ in gas too cold to excite the H$_3^+$ lines. The warm molecular gas and its H$_3^+$ thus suggest dynamical effects, most plausibly the advection of H$_2$ through a photoevaporation front into gas heated by the star. H$_3^+$ provides a new probe of the photoionization of molecular gas by very hot stars.

papers.title: A mixed-primal FEM for Poisson-Fermi interfacial problems
papers.abstract: This paper presents a mixed-primal FEM for a linearised Poisson--Fermi interface problem arising from the Bazant--Storey--Kornyshev theory, which describes electrostatic interactions in ionic solutions. It leads to a transmission problem coupling a fourth-order equation in the solvent region with a second-order equation in the solute region. To precisely compute the electrostatic stress and the interactive force in the electrolyte, we reformulate the fourth-order problem as a mixed system by introducing the gradient of the electrostatic potential, the divergence of its gradient, and the gradient of its divergence as additional independent variables. The second-order problem is studied in its primal form as this approach eliminates the requirement for Lagrange multipliers to enforce the transmission conditions. The resulting formulation is discretised using Raviart--Thomas finite elements for the vector variables and piecewise polynomial finite elements for the scalar variables. Well-posedness of the mixed-primal formulation and optimal a priori error estimates for the field variables as well as for the postprocessed Maxwell tensor are established under suitable regularity assumptions, in parameter-weighted norms in which the inf-sup constant is independent of the correlation length and of the permittivity ratio. The constants in the error estimates are independent of both parameters as well, up to a loss of at most half an order when the mesh does not resolve the length scale (square root of the relative permittivity); the Sobolev norms of the solution may still depend on the parameters through boundary layers. The postprocessed Maxwell stress converges with optimal order on quasi-uniform meshes, except for the lowest-order scheme in 3D. Numerical experiments validate the theoretical convergence rates and demonstrate the properties of the proposed method for problems in 2D and 3D.

authors.name: Neela Nataraj
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Modeling Lunar Power Harvesting and Battery Recharging In The Presence of Random Pointing Error
papers.abstract: In our work, we establish a lunar power beaming environment between a low-lunar orbiter and a circular solar panel mounted on top of a lunar vehicle located at the Lunar South Pole. Due to the random nature of the pointing errors, various upper bounds reflecting the severity of these errors are considered. Although harvested power is modelled stochastically in the literature, we extend this randomness to battery-storage analysis by deriving PDFs of state of charge, accumulated battery capacity and energy, and end-to-end efficiency for both battery charging modes. Then, our derivations are verified with extensive Monte Carlo simulations. Hence, our derivations provide a mathematical model that enables prediction and helps us understand the randomness of the corresponding variables. For the given pointing error levels, we quantify the differences between charging modes in these battery metrics. Our work explains the stochastic nature of these battery metrics in a realistic lunar environment. Regarding the end-to-end efficiency metric, which is the ratio of the stored electrical energy to the transmitted electrical energy, we observed that slow-charging efficiency is immune to pointing errors, and this mode can utilize only one-sixth of what the link can deliver under a mild pointing error.

papers.title: Ada-BFM: Adapting Behavior Foundation Models for Humanoid Scene Interaction
papers.abstract: Behavior Foundation Models (BFMs) have emerged as a promising paradigm for general-purpose humanoid control through pretraining on large-scale behavioral data. However, their proficiency in whole-body coordination does not readily extend to scene interaction, which requires adapting motion to scene-dependent geometric constraints and contact dynamics. To bridge this gap, we introduce Ada-BFM, a post-training framework that adapts pretrained BFMs for humanoid scene interaction. Ada-BFM augments the original architecture with a lightweight adapter, enabling interaction-specific adjustments while leveraging pretrained control capabilities. Rather than producing a separate controller for each task, the framework yields a shared model for each interaction domain, supporting diverse tasks involving terrain or object interaction. Extensive experiments in simulation and the real world demonstrate that Ada-BFM enables diverse scene interaction behaviors, accelerates learning compared with training from scratch, and largely preserves pretrained behavioral competence. These findings establish Ada-BFM as an effective and efficient approach to extending the capabilities of BFMs beyond their pretraining settings while retaining their strengths in general whole-body control.

papers.title: Scoring What Matters: Exact Feedback Reduction for Language Model Comparison
papers.abstract: Comparing language-model checkpoints requires estimating performance differences, yet evaluation pipelines can pay to score responses whose contributions cancel from those differences. We introduce Contrast-Aware Feedback Acquisition (CAFA), a sampler-agnostic method that identifies which scores a requested linear report needs before acquiring feedback. CAFA groups identical scoring inputs and aggregates their report coefficients, removing queries beyond ordinary caching while preserving the fully scored result. For a fixed response bank and an otherwise unrestricted scalar scorer, we characterize necessary and sufficient query sets for exact recovery of sample means, either alone or jointly with ordinary sample covariances. On controlled updates, CAFA removes 55.8% and 90.1% of the scoring inputs remaining after caching for Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct and SmolLM2-1.7B-Instruct, respectively, averaged over four generation repetitions. Across three online group relative policy optimization (GRPO) trajectories, Independent Star sampling with CAFA achieves 46.1-51.3% lower recorded generation-plus-feedback cost than independent autoregressive sampling with caching at a common empirical precision threshold (RMS MCSE $\leq 0.04$). This is a post hoc comparison of completed runs on a fixed budget grid. All 504 evaluated report cells reproduce the fully scored means and covariances to numerical precision. We provide a modular implementation supporting existing response banks, versioned caches and external scorers.

papers.title: Provenance-Isolated Epistemic Quorums: Execution-Bound Evidence Certification and Plausible-World Safety Gating in Agentic Control Planes
papers.abstract:
Agreement among large language models is not physical evidence for mutating production infrastructure. Because generative models share pretraining priors and conform to peer rationales during deliberation, voting ensembles correlate errors instead of providing independent fault tolerance; yet attaching rigid deterministic checks to unconstrained agent outputs paralyzes incident remediation. We present Provenance-Isolated Epistemic Quorums (PIEQ), an execution-bound certification layer that keeps every language model strictly outside the trusted computing base. PIEQ unifies assumption-based truth maintenance, physical provenance isolation, control-theoretic plausible-world safety shielding, and linearizable concurrency governance around three distinct obligations: certifying diagnostic preconditions from disjoint physical failure domains, gating candidate mutations across all unrefuted fault worlds while falling back to read-only diagnostic probes under ambiguity, and binding admission certificates to target execution through snapshot barriers, revision checks, authorization freshness, trusted temporal-precondition policies, and capability-tiered enforcement.
  Across formal guarantees, automated etcd fault suites, frozen software benchmarks, and live language-model runs, PIEQ achieves zero within-assumption unsafe admissions and zero false-precondition commits, converting occasional agent proof omissions into recoverable false blocks rather than unsafe actions. On a physical PostgreSQL/Patroni cluster, PIEQ gates supervised failovers alongside Patroni and etcd's native split-brain protection and enforces a full Tier E2 contract inside a single serializable PostgreSQL transaction for bounded capacity reservations. All benchmarks are author-labeled, live model snapshots are unpinned, and Tier E2 physical failover promotion as well as multi-host hardware fault isolation remain open work.

papers.title: Robust decision-dependent information discovery is harder than robust optimization
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider a four-stage variant of robust optimization with cost uncertainty described by the budget uncertainty polytope, known as decision-dependent information discovery (DDID). In this problem, the decision maker first queries a subset of the cost coefficients. Then, the adversary responds by revealing worst-case values for the queried elements, after which the decision maker chooses a feasible solution while facing the remaining uncertainty on the unqueried costs. Our contribution is twofold. On the negative side, we prove that, the DDID is NP-complete even when the underlying nominal problem is the 2-selection problem, for which only a polynomial number of feasible solutions exist. This contrasts with the min-max robust counterpart with budget uncertainty, known to be not harder than the nominal problem. On the positive side, we prove that the more general $p$-selection problem can be solved in polynomial time under the additional assumption that all deviations are equal.

papers.title: Monte Carlo Tree Search for Classifier Chains
papers.abstract: Multi-label classification continues to be relevant to a variety of modern tasks. Among other challenges, modern data sets are increasingly large with respect to the number of labels, and these labels may be noisy or missing in the training sets. Label-wise scores and ranking-based metrics have been popular, but optimising exact multi-label evaluation (where a predicted set of labels should match the true set exactly) is particularly relevant for many domains, e.g., in medicine; alongside some measure of confidence. This requires an estimation of joint probability across labels (a model of label dependence; conditioned on each input instance). A family of methods known as probabilistic classifier chains provides such inference. However, these existing varieties either do not scale to a large number of labels or do so by approximating joint via marginal distributions in a way that compromises the estimation of uncertainty for exact match accuracy. We overcome this issue by proposing TSCC; leveraging a Monte Carlo Tree Search methodology to enhance chain inference via an efficient balance between the exploration of label space and the exploration of promising label-set predictions. Results are promising both in terms of predictive and computational performance.

authors.name: Jesse Read
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Robust Measurements of the Cosmic Microwave Background Lensing Power Spectrum in the Presence of Anisotropic Cosmic Birefringence
papers.abstract: Achieving the scientific potential of upcoming high-sensitivity cosmic microwave background (CMB) polarization surveys requires lensing analyses that are robust to unmodeled distortions of the polarization field. One such possible distortion is anisotropic cosmic birefringence, a direction-dependent rotation of the linear polarization plane that may arise from parity-violating physics such as axion-like fields. We quantify the impact of both modeled and unmodeled anisotropic birefringence on the CMB lensing measurement in the Marginal Unbiased Score Expansion (MUSE) framework. Considering noise levels expected for current and future CMB surveys, we find that neglecting birefringence produces a positive bias in the lensing bandpowers that increases towards small angular scales. For a scale-invariant birefringence power spectrum $L(L+1)C_L^{\alpha\alpha}/2\pi=10^{-5}\,{\rm rad}^2$, the positive fractional bias can reach $(10.1\pm1.1)\%$ of the lensing power at $1375<L<2000$. Jointly estimating lensing and birefringence in the MUSE framework recovers the input lensing bandpowers and birefringence amplitude without detectable bias across all tested configurations. The joint MUSE estimator also reduces the scatter of the recovered birefringence amplitude by factors of $1.6\pm0.2$ to $2.4\pm0.3$ relative to a joint quadratic estimator, with the largest gains in the highest signal-to-noise configurations. These results indicate that a joint-field reconstruction with MUSE can recover unbiased estimates of the lensing and birefringence power spectra while still improving precision relative to quadratic estimators.

papers.title: EnSurv: Deep Generative Survival Modeling with Application to Kidney Graft Outcomes
papers.abstract: Kidney transplantation is the optimal treatment for life-threatening end-stage renal disease, providing significant survival advantages over dialysis. Given the severe shortage of donor organs, accurately predicting the time to premature graft failure is an essential clinical task for optimizing organ allocation and tailoring individualized immunosuppressive therapies. This study is motivated by a comprehensive United Network of Organ Sharing (UNOS) dataset containing 243,443 kidney transplant records with complex multi-region structures and high right-censoring rates. We propose EnSurv (survival engression), a deep generative survival framework designed to capture complex, non-linear clinical covariate interactions for modeling time to graft failure. Within a pre-additive noise model (pre-ANM) family, EnSurv optimizes an energy score augmented with pooled Kaplan-Meier tail completion to handle right-censoring. We identify the pooled-completion target of the objective, establish consistency for its best approximation within the pre-ANM family, and give conditions and error bounds for its relation to true conditional graft survival. EnSurv also provides global explainability through summaries of fitted feature weights and incorporates domain constraints through established clinical directions using a soft gradient penalty. Extensive simulation experiments were conducted to evaluate the performance of the proposed method in comparison with existing methods. Application to the UNOS cohort demonstrates that EnSurv effectively models individual and region-level effects, consistently outperforming baselines across evaluation metrics encompassing discrimination, calibration, and accuracy.

papers.title: Tweezing microparticles by tightly focused optical skyrmionic fields
papers.abstract: The concept of skyrmions, once translated to the optical domain, provides a topological framework to investigate structured light-matter interactions. However, their practical use for the manipulation of material systems remains barely explored. Here, we experimentally demonstrate trapping and tunable orbital motion of dielectric microparticles in tightly focused skyrmionic polarization textures prepared using a compact spin-orbit optical element. We explore the tweezing capabilities at fixed topology either by varying the relative weights of the orthogonally polarized components or by switching between skyrmion and bimeron polarization textures. Vectorial focusing and optical-force calculations qualitatively reproduce the experimental observations. These results motivate extending skyrmionic light to the manipulation of micro-objects, including birefringent and chiral samples.

authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: VIDE : Training-Free Video Anomaly Detection via Visual Intrinsic Distribution Estimation
papers.abstract: In embedding-based video anomaly detection (VAD), normal clips can have high similarity to anomalous descriptions, an anomaly bias that leads to false positives. Methods such as PRISM mitigate this bias by measuring deviations from a normality reference along anomaly directions. Both the normality reference and the anomaly directions are derived from text and shared across videos, although normal activity and the appearance of anomalies vary across scenes. The resulting scores are also sensitive to prompt selection. To address these limitations, we propose Visual Intrinsic Distribution Estimation (VIDE), a training-free framework that adapts text-derived scoring to each test video using frozen clip embeddings. VIDE estimates normal scene content from clips with low initial anomaly scores and uses this estimate to partially correct the textual reference. It then rescales category responses, penalizes clips with strong responses across categories, and refines the anomaly directions using high-scoring clips. VIDE averages scores across prompt views to reduce sensitivity to prompt selection and fuses scores from two frozen encoders. With both encoders, VIDE improves AUC over the best PRISM result by $1.5$, $1.9$, and $3.5$ points on UCF-Crime, XD-Violence, and MSAD, respectively, and AP by $6.5$ points on XD-Violence and $9.3$ points on MSAD. VIDE yields the highest AUC among the compared training-free methods on all three benchmarks and the highest reported AUC among all compared methods on XD-Violence and MSAD. Our code is included in the supplementary material and will be made publicly available.

papers.title: A sharp polygonal Finsler-Hadwiger inequality
papers.abstract:
For every simple $n$-gon of area $A$ with side lengths $a_1,\ldots,a_n$, we prove \[
  \sum_{i=1}^n a_i^2 \ge 4\tan\frac{\pi}{n}\,A
  +c_n\sum_{i<j}(a_i-a_j)^2,
  \qquad
  c_n=1-\frac{\tan(\pi/n)}{\tan(\pi/(n-1))}, \] with the convention $c_3=1$, so that the case $n=3$ is exactly the Finsler-Hadwiger inequality. The coefficient $c_n$ cannot be improved, and equality holds only for regular polygons. The extremal configurations are far from the regular $n$-gon: the constant is approached by cyclic polygons in which one side shrinks to zero while the others become the sides of a regular $(n-1)$-gon (a doubled segment when $n=3$). The proof combines the classical fact that cyclic polygons maximize area for given side lengths with a two variable minimization using the half central angles. We also compute the larger optimal coefficient for nearly regular polygons, and show that the best constant in the joint stability estimate for side lengths and vertex radii grows like $n^2$.

authors.name: Beniamin Bogosel
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Sulfur chemistry in temperate N$_2$-dominated exoplanetary atmospheres investigated through experimental simulations: Volatile characterization
papers.abstract: Aims. This study addresses through an experimental approach an understudied aspect of sulfur atmospheric chemistry which is the coupled and complex reactivity existing between sulfur, carbon, and nitrogen elements. Experimental simulations have been used to better characterize the volatile products resulting from the coupling between these three elements and discuss the potential observability of such species. Sulfur chemistry appears as a source of diversified signatures which need to be characterized for the current and the future exploration of exoplanetary atmospheres. Methods. SO$_2$ and H$_2$S reactivity was explored experimentally in plasma discharges using mixtures of either pure N$_2$ or composed of N$_2$ and CH$_4$. The volatile species produced in such conditions were analyzed and quantified by in situ mass spectrometry. Results. SO$_2$ reactivity in the presence of N$_2$ alone or combined with methane led to the detection of six sulfur species: H$_2$S, NHSO, S$_2$O, CS$_2$, OCS, and CH$_3$SH. Under the same conditions, the reactivity of H$_2$S resulted in the observation of CS$_2$, CS, and CH$_3$SH. The detection of these species highlights the need to establish a consistent photochemical network describing this sulfur chemistry. Furthermore, the study addresses the detectability of these sulfur compounds via transit spectroscopy. Among them, OCS and CS$_2$, exhibit several detectable bands in the mid-infrared, and constitute promising targets to probe sulfur active chemistry with space- telescopes. In contrast, the detection of the other sulfur volatiles observed appears more challenging at low spectral resolution.

papers.title: Seldon TFM family: Seldon-Mini, Seldon and Seldon+
papers.abstract: We introduce Seldon, a family of tabular foundation models. Our classifier Seldon+ ranks first among 15 models on TabBench, our benchmark of 124 classification datasets, and on its variant with missing values. In our own runs of public benchmarks, it also ranks first on BeyondArena IID classification and TabBench-Bio, and second on TabArena classification. The open-weight models Seldon-Mini (27M parameters) and Seldon (213M parameters) both lie on the TabArena Pareto front of Elo against inference time: no entry is both more accurate and faster. On TabArena, Seldon ranks fourth and Seldon-Mini seventh among 109 leaderboard entries, and on the IID track of BeyondArena, Seldon ranks second among 42 entries. Seldon-Mini and Seldon handle both classification and regression, use an architecture similar to those of Kumo-Tabular, TabFM and TabPFN-3.5, and are trained on synthetic tables only.

papers.title: Energy and Performance Characterization of UxNBs: Toward AI-Driven Non-Terrestrial Open RAN Control
papers.abstract: UAV-mounted base stations (UxNBs) can provide ondemand 5G coverage, but their limited onboard energy makes power consumption the main operational constraint. AI-driven Open RAN controllers are a promising solution, yet they are trained almost exclusively on analytical models and simulations, since no public dataset captures the real energy behavior of a flying 5G base station (BS). As a first step toward closing this gap, we present a UAV testbed hosting a 5G picocell that supports a 20 MHz carrier and up to 100 Mbps throughput. The testbed measures BS system metrics, including power consumption, CPU load, and temperature, alongside UAV flight telemetry and detailed per-layer vRAN processing metrics. To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration that jointly exposes the energy and RAN behavior of a flying 5G BS, providing the real measurements needed to train and validate energy-aware AI controllers.

papers.title: Linear convergence of evolution strategies to local minima by coupling with quadratic models
papers.abstract: Among derivative-free optimization methods, evolution strategies have emerged as competitive algorithms for multimodal, noisy or ill-conditioned problems in small and moderate dimensions. Theoretical guarantees have long been scarce, but a series of recent works established their convergence on certain classes of objective functions. A successful approach normalizes the states of the algorithm into a Markov chain and proves that this chain converges to a stationary distribution. It has yielded the linear convergence of several evolution strategies, including the state-of-the-art CMA-ES. Yet this approach requires the objective function to be scaling-invariant, hence unimodal, since otherwise the normalized process is not a Markov chain. We propose a methodology to prove linear convergence on a much larger class of functions, including smooth multimodal functions. Started close enough to a local minimum with a nondegenerate Hessian and with a small enough step size, the ($\mu$/$\mu$w, $\lambda$)-ES with stepsize adaptation converges linearly to this minimum with high probability, at the rate of its quadratic model, and the probability of failure vanishes when the initial step size and the initial distance to the minimum tend to zero. The proof views the normalized process as an adaptive chain and couples it, with high probability, with the Markov chain associated with the quadratic model.

authors.name: Armand Gissler
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: When Exact Token Importance Is Not Enough: Limits of Top-K Selection in LLM Attention
papers.abstract: Long-context language models often retain only a limited set of past token positions for an attention query. A common strategy scores positions individually and keeps the highest-ranked K. Yet attention weights are renormalized over the chosen set: two individually important positions need not form the best pair. We ask whether independent ranking suffices even when each importance score measures the exact downstream change in next-token predictions caused by deleting that position alone. It does not. A four-position construction makes the ranked pair incur 133.2 times the Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence of the optimal pair, and a parametric family proves that this multiplicative gap is unbounded. An exact exchange identity and preference reversals for every K >= 2 explain the interaction. In exhaustive frozen-model audits of SmolLM2, Gemma, and Qwen, exact-singleton Top-4 leaves at least 10% relative improvement within a fully enumerated 24-position candidate pool in 55/60, 49/60, and 60/60 cases, respectively. SwapCert, a same-budget one-swap audit, detects 157/164 such cases and returns directly checkable improving supports. A KL-margin certificate relates support fidelity to next-token stability; larger-budget, multi-layer cached-decoding experiments measure predictive fidelity at K = 128 and 256. These results establish joint support quality as an essential object of analysis for sparse attention and motivate downstream-aware support selection under inference constraints.

papers.title: A note on slicing
papers.abstract: We give a short proof of Bourgain's slicing theorem with the explicit bound $L_K\leq\sqrt{5/\pi}$ for every convex body $K$. The argument combines the strong thin-shell inequality obtained from the moment-measure method of Chen and Klartag with an entropy estimate along Eldan's stochastic localization. The proof uses neither $M$-ellipsoid theory nor the reverse Santal\'o inequality.

authors.name: Joseph Lehec
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: On local embeddability into $C^*(\F_\infty)$
papers.abstract: We study local embeddability of $C^*$-algebras into $C^*(\F_\infty)$ as an analogue of QWEP in the LLP/WEP picture. We characterize this property by an analog of CP-stability, an approximation property for finite-dimensional operator systems. We show that local embeddability, together with an amenable trace, implies a tracial local lifting property. Combining this observation with the cohomological obstructions of Ioana, Spaas and Wiersma, we prove that the full group $C^*$-algebra $C^*(\SL_3(\Z))$ does not locally embed into $C^*(\F_\infty)$. We obtain the same conclusion for the full $C^*$-algebras of two hyperlinear groups constructed by Thom. To our knowledge, the only previously known obstruction to local embeddability into $C^*(\F_\infty)$ was due to Junge and Pisier.

authors.name: Jean Roydor
authors.institution: Institut de Mathématiques de Jussieu-Paris Rive Gauche

papers.title: Magnetoelectric response to a N\'eel domain wall in spin-orbit coupled superconducting films: Spontaneous currents, vortex pinning, and vortex-antivortex nucleation
papers.abstract: We study the superconducting response induced by a N\'eel domain wall in a thin superconducting film proximity-coupled to a ferromagnetic layer in the presence of interfacial Rashba spin-orbit coupling. The combined action of the magnetic texture and broken inversion symmetry generates a magnetoelectric coupling that induces spontaneous equilibrium currents. To establish the basic response to a continuously rotating magnetic texture, we first consider a periodic harmonic cycloid as an analytically tractable reference problem. Near Tc, this reference problem illustrates how the magnetoelectric coupling modifies the superconducting order parameter, while below Tc it provides a simple setting for describing the phase response, Pearl screening, and the interaction with a vortex. We then turn to the main problem of this work, a single N\'eel domain wall, and derive analytical expressions for its equilibrium phase profile, spontaneous current, magnetic field, and vortex-wall interaction energy.We show that the N\'eel wall acts as an extended magnetoelectric source and produces a vorticity-selective pinning landscape controlled by the competition between the wall width and the effective screening length. We further demonstrate that sufficiently strong magnetoelectric coupling can render a bound vortex-antivortex pair energetically favorable relative to the vortex-free state, even in the absence of an applied magnetic field. Our results provide an analytical framework for understanding magnetoelectric vortex pinning and vortex-antivortex nucleation by N\'eel domain walls in spin-orbit coupled superconducting films.

papers.title: Latent Class Mixed Model Variational Autoencoders for Scalable Phenotyping of Health Trajectories
papers.abstract: Clustering longitudinal health trajectories requires handling high-dimensional measurements, irregular visit times, and subject-level heterogeneity while retaining clinically interpretable structure. Existing methods address this only partially: latent-class mixed models yield an interpretable, covariate-driven partition but do not scale past a handful of markers, while deep time-series clustering scales at the cost of that structure and generally requires a common time grid. We introduce the Latent Class Mixed Model Variational Autoencoder (LCMM-VAE), a deep generative model whose latent prior is a mixture of class-specific linear mixed models, so that each subject's latent trajectory decomposes into its class mean trajectory and a subject-specific deviation. We derive a variational EM algorithm whose class responsibilities, random effects and mixed-model parameters are updated in closed form, and provide identifiability guarantees under stated conditions. Experiments on simulated and real longitudinal cohorts show that LCMM-VAE returns a partition, a reconstruction of incomplete trajectories and interpretable class-level dynamics at once, while remaining competitive with classical and deep baselines.

authors.name: Michel Coste
authors.institution: Institut National de Recherche pour l'Agriculture, l'Alimentation et l'Environnement

papers.title: Phoneme-identity depth profiles do not reliably predict LoRA placement for dysarthric ASR
papers.abstract:
Parameter-efficient adaptation of a speech foundation model to dysarthric speech requires a rarely justified choice: which encoder layers to adapt. A recently proposed strategy is to probe the encoder, find where phonetic information becomes most decodable, and put the adapters there. We test that inference across two ASR models (Qwen3-ASR, Whisper-small) and two dysarthric corpora (Mandarin CDSD, English UASpeech), holding recipe and seed discipline constant.
  The inference fails. Measured under one pipeline rather than inherited from published figures, all four phoneme-error curves minimise between 83% and 92% of relative depth, each model's minimising layer moving no further between corpora than between probe seeds. The best adaptation band is not similarly constant: none of three natural mappings from the curve to a band -- steepest improvement, lowest band-mean error, or knee location -- recovers the best tested configuration. We do not claim no statistic of the curve could work, only that these three do not.
  Placement still matters, but is model- and corpus-specific. On CDSD the models disagree -- Qwen3-ASR prefers its upper third (29.88% CER, three-seed mean), Whisper-small all-block LoRA (53.56%) -- while on UASpeech neither favours the upper band. At three seeds, upper-versus-all is resolved (-1.31 pp, CI [-2.16, -0.25]) but upper-versus-middle is not (-0.83 pp, CI [-2.06, +1.86]). The two models' preferences differ as a directly tested interaction (-4.71 pp, CI [-6.17, -2.89]); we designate this the primary claim, and record that the designation was made post hoc. On Qwen3-ASR x UASpeech, adapting near the input is reliably worse than not adapting at all (+9.90 pp CER). We recommend choosing the band by a short adaptation sweep on the model and corpus in hand, not by reading it off a probe.

papers.title: High-order polynomial corrections for embedded curved boundaries in discontinuous Galerkin methods for hyperbolic systems: from staircase instabilities to a gap method
papers.abstract: High order polynomial corrections, which impose the boundary conditions on an embedded boundary by modifying the polynomial of the surrogate boundary cells, give accurate and robust discretizations of elliptic problems on unfitted meshes. We show that, used out of the box in discontinuous Galerkin discretizations of hyperbolic systems on Cartesian meshes, the shifted boundary and minimization-based (ROD) corrections become unstable, with eigenvalues of positive real part that no restriction of the time step can remove. Linear advection, whose operator is block triangular, is the least affected case: a tilted straight boundary makes every correction unstable with the geometry-normal map, while the face-orthogonal map, which likely gives a one-dimensional character to the boundary condition with tensor-product bases, keeps the 1D stability up to one polynomial degree less. The slip wall of the linear acoustic system is much more critical: all the corrections are unstable already on a tilted straight wall, and an energy balance shows that the cause is the misalignment, in direction and in position, between the faces of the staircase and the wall. Since the origin of the instability is geometric, we act on the surrogate boundary itself, and develop the gap paradigm for discontinuous Galerkin discretizations of hyperbolic systems: each boundary cell is extended, by extrapolating its polynomial without new degrees of freedom, up to the segments joining the projections of its vertices on the wall, where the boundary condition is imposed, and neighbouring extended cells exchange information through the numerical fluxes used on the interior interfaces. Numerical experiments confirm the energy stability of the gap method on a straight wall and show high order convergence on curved walls, in configurations where the classical corrections applied on the staircase diverge.

authors.name: Mirco Ciallella
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Breaking Routing And Inter-device Dependencies in Mixture-of-Experts
papers.abstract: As Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models scale, Expert Parallelism (EP) becomes increasingly important for distributing experts across devices. However, the resulting token dispatch and combine operations can become a major bottleneck during inference. Overlapping these communication phases with computation is constrained by the sequential dependencies of standard MoE architectures. We introduce BRAID-MoE, an architecture that pairs laddered residual connections with early routing to relax these dependencies. Laddered residuals enable each expert combine to be deferred to the following block, while early routing computes the next routing decision from the pre-combine residual, with experts still receiving the updated post-combine hidden state. This creates an extended communication window in which the preceding combine and next dispatch can execute back-to-back on a dedicated communication stream, overlapping attention computation. On Qwen3-shaped MoEs with 0.4B-A0.1B and 2.5B-A0.5B parameters, BRAID closely matches sequential training at matched compute, with validation-loss increases of only 1% and 0.5%, respectively. We further demonstrate that existing MoE checkpoints can be adapted to BRAID with limited additional training, largely recovering their original accuracy. On a converted Qwen3-30B-A3B model, BRAID achieves speedups of up to 1.29$\times$ in prefill and 1.37$\times$ in decode, and at least 1.12$\times$ across diverse workloads and EP configurations on one or two four-H100 nodes. It outperforms competing overlap strategies in all tested settings, with the strongest gains when communication is a major latency bottleneck and its duration approaches the available computation window. These results demonstrate that early routing enables more effective communication-computation overlap in MoE inference at a modest cost in model quality.

authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: The one-velocity Baer--Nunziato system as a weak limit of solutions to a compressible two-fluid system
papers.abstract: We study how a macroscopic mixture arises from two compressible fluids that share a velocity but occupy disjoint regions. We fix the initial density profiles and the common initial velocity, and let the partition between the fluids oscillate on increasingly fine scales. The fluids remain segregated as they evolve, but in the weak limit the phase indicator becomes a volume fraction that may lie strictly between zero and one. For independent adiabatic exponents $\gamma^\pm\geq9/5$, we prove that the sequence of segregated solutions converges to a global weak solution of the viscous one-velocity Baer--Nunziato system in three space dimensions. The mixture pressure is the volume-weighted average of the two phase pressures, while their difference drives the evolution of the volume fraction along the flow and contributes to dissipation in the macroscopic energy inequality.

authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Recursive estimation of the Oja median and related simplex medians
papers.abstract: We study the recursive estimation of multivariate location functionals defined by minimizing the expected volume of a random simplex. This framework encompasses both the spatial median and the affine-equivariant Oja median. We introduce a sliding-window stochastic gradient algorithm and its averaged version, and establish their strong consistency and asymptotic normality. We further show that the sliding-window approach offers a favorable trade-off between statistical accuracy and computational cost compared with a naive disjoint-block stochastic gradient algorithm and offline methods, with the statistical comparison based on asymptotic covariances. Numerical experiments illustrate the computational advantages of the proposed procedures and their finite-sample accuracy.

authors.name: Guillaume Salle
authors.institution: Institut National de Recherche pour l'Agriculture, l'Alimentation et l'Environnement

papers.title: Twisted Poincar\'e series at zero on surfaces
papers.abstract: Let $(\Sigma,g)$ be a closed, connected, oriented, Riemannian Anosov surface. We show that there exists an open subset $\mathcal V_g$ of the space of finite-dimensional irreducible representations of the fundamental group of $\Sigma$, whose complement has complex codimension at least one, such that the following holds: for all $x,y\in \Sigma$, $\rho \in \mathcal{V}_g$, the meromorphic extension of the twisted Poincar\'e series $s \mapsto \eta_{g,\rho,x,y}(s)$ vanishes at $s=0$. We also give examples of non-trivial representations whose Poincar\'e series does not vanish at zero. In addition, we describe the structure of twisted resonant states at zero for these examples and show that they admit non-trivial Jordan blocks.

authors.name: Thibault Lefeuvre
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Text Is Just Another Shot in Vision-Language Models: Simple Probes on Frozen Encoders Do It
papers.abstract: Few-shot adaptation of vision-language models has produced increasingly elaborate methods built on CLIP and on one shared principle: the zero-shot text classifier is the anchor, and labeled images only correct it. We argue that this principle reflects CLIP's visual features rather than a property of the task. We provide a simple Bayesian interpretation, in which a class name is worth exactly kappa = sigma^2 / tau^2 labeled images, the ratio between the visual spread of a class and the misalignment of its name. The Bayes classifier of this model counts text as kappa more samples. With modern frozen encoders, few-shot adaptation then reduces to a well-regularised convex probe. Specifically, we introduce TASP, a simple convex logistic regression on frozen features that incorporates class-name embeddings as weighted training examples and as a regularization prior. On the standard 11-dataset benchmark, TASP with frozen PE-Core-L features achieves 87.1% accuracy at 1 shot and 91.4% at 16 shots, outperforming state-of-the-art few-shot vision-language adaptation methods by 4.6 to 11.0 percentage points. While stronger representations explain much of this improvement, controlled comparisons on matched features show that existing frozen-encoder adaptation methods do not materially improve on this probe. We further find that the weight assigned to text matters more than how it is incorporated, and that combining self-supervised visual features with vision-language representations is most beneficial for weaker visual encoders. Together, these findings suggest that progress in few-shot vision-language adaptation depends more on representation quality and the appropriate use of text supervision than on increasingly complex adaptation mechanisms.

papers.title: Testing Expansion without Connectivity via Return Probabilities
papers.abstract:
We study whether every connected component of a bounded-degree graph is an edge expander, given access to its neighbor lists. Dinur and Goldreich give a tester using $\mathrm{poly}(1/\varepsilon)n^\alpha$ queries for every fixed $\alpha>2/3$. We obtain \[
  \widetilde O_{d,c,\beta}\!\left(\frac{n^{1/2+\beta}}{\varepsilon}+\frac{\sqrt n}{\varepsilon^4}\right) \] queries for every fixed $0<\beta\le1$. The tester accepts graphs whose components have edge expansion at least $c$ and rejects graphs $\varepsilon$-far from having edge expansion $\Omega(\beta c^2/d)$ in every component, each with probability at least $2/3$. No structural promise is imposed on the input.
  The tester compares pairwise collision probabilities at two walk lengths and starts further walks at vertices where sampled endpoints coincide. These additional samples control the contribution of vertices with larger return probabilities. We show that the resulting conditions force the longer walk to be nearly uniform on an induced expander with few edges leaving it. We also prove an $\Omega(\sqrt{n/\log n})$ lower bound for Cayley graphs at infinitely many input sizes.

authors.name: Nikolas Melissaris
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Temporal Inhomogeneous Random Graphs
papers.abstract: Motivated by the study of time-dependent propagation processes in inhomogeneous populations, we extend Burova, Lugosi and Perarnau's results on the temporal stochastic block model to graphon-based random graphs with a continuous and strictly positive kernel. We consider such a graph in the regime where connection probabilities are of the order of $\log n/n$, and equip its edges with a uniformly random ordering, interpreted as timestamps. We study the size of reachable sets via increasing paths (that is, paths whose edge timestamps are strictly increasing). We establish tight first-order asymptotics for the size of the reachable set from a fixed vertex, and also determine the first-order asymptotics of the lengths of the longest and shortest increasing paths with one or two fixed endpoints.

papers.title: Exact solution of the Bose-Fermi mixture along the unnesting line
papers.abstract: A one-dimensional model of a Bose-Fermi mixture with contact repulsions is exactly solvable via nested Bethe ansatz. That formal solution is here simplified along a special line where the Bethe-ansatz equations can be unnested. The model solution is expressed in terms of the known solutions for the Lieb-Liniger model and the Yang-Gaudin model of attractive spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ fermions in the balanced case. We find explicit analytical results for the ground-state energy, the velocities of excitations, and the Drude weights at weak and strong interactions. At weak interactions, the special line corresponds to the parameter values where the isolated systems of free fermions and weakly interacting bosons have equal velocities.

papers.title: Anomalous front propagation in many-body quantum transport with memory-dependent resetting
papers.abstract: We introduce an exactly solvable framework for non-Markovian quantum many-body dynamics based on stochastic resetting with memory. Applicable to arbitrary time-independent Hamiltonians, including interacting systems, our framework provides an exact representation of the dynamics with memory in terms of the corresponding reset-free evolution, which can be accessed either analytically or numerically. We demonstrate the power of this approach by studying domain-wall melting in a one-dimensional chain of noninteracting fermions, obtaining exact analytical results for the density profile, the local structure of the front edge, the extreme-value statistics of the rightmost fermion, and the integrated current. Remarkably, memory transforms ballistic transport into logarithmically slow propagation without arresting spreading. While the macroscopic density profile retains its original scaling function, the front edge broadens as $\sqrt{\ln t}$ rather than $t^{1/3}$ at late times and develops a qualitatively different edge structure. Furthermore, the extreme-value statistics change from Tracy--Widom to Gaussian, while both the mean and variance of the integrated current grow logarithmically in time. Our predictions are in excellent agreement with numerical simulations. These results reveal how memory can fundamentally alter quantum many-body transport and its fluctuations.

papers.title: RFW-W: Scaling Physical Asset Universes for Generative Embodied Simulation
papers.abstract: Scaling embodied simulation requires diverse objects with executable physical representations. We present RFW-W, a physical asset universe connecting rigid, articulated, and deformable asset sources to task-conditioned scene composition. Its reported inventories comprise 1,010,386 asset records: 524,611 rigid assets in 1,212 categories (RFW-R), 402,410 articulated assets in 531 categories (RFW-A), and 83,365 jointly verified deformables in 485 categories (RFW-S). These taxonomies contribute 2,228 dataset--category entries. RFW-R couples category-guided generation with collision geometry, composed physical properties, and interaction annotations; RFW-A uses reusable agent-authored procedural generators with explicit part and joint structure; RFW-S uses structure-aware simulation representations, calibration, and independent testing. A common interface preserves physical requirements specific to each asset type for retrieval and scene assembly. Quantitative evaluations demonstrate that RFW-R provides broader asset coverage and stronger scene-fulfillment capabilities than existing datasets. Across five RoboTwin tasks, using 100 demonstrations per task for each asset source, policies trained on RFW-R achieve macro success rates of 71.2% in clean settings and 41.8% under randomization, exceeding the strongest baseline by 15.8 and 10.6 percentage points, respectively. RFW-W provides a scalable and unified asset foundation for generating physically grounded, task-conditioned embodied worlds.

papers.title: Quantitative $p$-Wasserstein bounds for empirical measures on manifolds: Expectation and concentration
papers.abstract: We derive quantitative bounds in expectation and concentration for the $p$-Wasserstein distance between the empirical measure of independent samples and their common law on metric measure spaces satisfying the measure contraction property $\MCP(K,n)$, with $K\le0$. Our results extend the expectation estimates of Boissard--Le Gouic (Theorem 1.1 in Ann. Inst. Henri Poincar\'e Probab. Stat. 50 (2014), no. 2, 539--563) and the concentration estimates of Bolley--Guillin--Villani (Theorem 2.1 in Probab. Theory Relat. Fields 137 (2007), 541--593). In spaces with exponential volume growth, suitable exponential moment assumptions allow us to recover the Euclidean rate $N^{-1/n}$ in expectation when $n>2p$. As an application, we obtain uniform-in-time concentration estimates for the empirical measure of McKean--Vlasov interacting particle systems on complete Riemannian manifolds with Ricci curvature bounded below by combining comparison theory and parallel coupling to a noninteracting proxy system.

authors.name: Jonathan Junne
authors.institution: Centre National de la Recherche Scientifique

papers.title: Who decides the norms in TCS? Analysing the composition of the STOC 2027 committees and of the Simons Institute "AI+TCS" working group
papers.abstract: A working group organised by the Simons Institute released a report last September containing recommendations aiming to increase the usage of LLMs in theoretical computer science (TCS), including introducing them for communication and evaluation. Most of these recommendations were enacted by the STOC 2027 programme committee and the ACM SIGACT executive committee (as the steering committee of STOC). The composition of the Simons Institute working group is analysed along two axes: country of affiliation, and ties with industry (i.e. affiliated with or funded by). The results show an overwhelming representation of researchers from US institutions and private companies, and a large over-representation of researchers with ties to AI/Big Tech companies (in the present or the recent past). The composition of the STOC 2027 and 2026 programme committees is analysed in terms of country of affiliation. The results show a large over-representation in 2027 of researchers from US institutions/companies, and large under-representation of researchers from EU and Asian institutions, as compared to 2026. The composition of the ACM SIGACT extended executive committee is analysed along the same two axes as the Simons Institute working group: country and industrial ties. The results show the same overwhelming representation of researchers from US institutions/companies, and a large representation of researchers with ties to AI/Big Tech companies.

papers.title: Evolutionary constraints on protein fold diversity
papers.abstract: Arrangements of secondary structures in proteins yield a wide variety of possible topologies, yet the protein folds observed in nature are limited in their diversity. Is the number of protein folds limited by biophysical constraints or by evolutionary contingency? In recent years, the development of new methods for protein structure prediction and comparison, molecular design, and the rapid progress of cryo-electron microscopy revealed new insights into the protein fold space. Here, we present recent findings demonstrating that natural proteins adopt only a small fraction of all possible folds and discuss how evolutionary processes limit the diversity of evolving protein folds.

papers.title: SOTS: Signature-based Optimal Transport Selection
papers.abstract: Training data selection for machine learning models is a critical bottleneck in industrial applications where expert annotation is costly and time-consuming. Existing coreset selection methods for time series either ignore temporal structure entirely or cannot handle variable-length, irregularly sampled, multi-channel signals, the setting most common in industrial monitoring and testing. We introduce SOTS (Signature-based Optimal Transport Selection), an unsupervised coreset selection framework for irregular multivariate time series (IMTS) classification. Each sample is mapped to a truncated path signature, capturing the joint geometric structure of its channels, and the coreset is selected by greedily minimizing the Sliced Wasserstein distance between the empirical signature distributions of the candidate subset and the full dataset, a criterion for which we establish a convergence guarantee for random coresets. We validate SOTS on a real-world, highly imbalanced industrial I&C testing dataset, where SOTS-Greedy exceeds 95% of full-dataset accuracy using only 30% of the training data, outperforming standard coreset baselines at most budgets. This advantage generalizes to public UEA regular multivariate time series benchmarks specifically when class-discriminative information is purely geometric.

papers.intro:
Not every machine learning problem is a big-data problem. Large language models are trained on trillions of tokens with correspondingly large compute budgets, but many industrial, medical, and financial applications rely on task-specific models trained on far smaller datasets, and often with modest compute. When data is scarce or expensive to label, the question shifts from how much data to collect to which data is worth collecting: not every point in a dataset contributes equally to a downstream task, and identifying the informative ones from the redundant or uninformative ones becomes central rather than incidental. Simple filtering heuristics, removing exact duplicates or points that clearly fall outside the task’s scope, rarely shrink a dataset by much, precisely because they do not reason about task relevance. Conversely, discarding points that are inconvenient, for instance those with missing values that are hard to impute, can remove information the task actually depends on. Formalizing what makes a subset of data representative of a learning task, rather than simply small, is the coreset selection problem. In this paper we study coreset selection for classification: we assume a downstream classifier is fixed, but do not yet know which instances to feed it for best performance. This setting is particularly relevant when data arrives unlabeled: selecting the most informative instances before labeling, rather than after, directly reduces the labeling effort required. In our motivating industrial setting, for example, a single test report can flag tens of thousands of discrepancies for a verification engineer to manually review; selecting a few hundred of the most representative ones for labeling, rather than the full report, would save a considerable amount of time and ensure better labeling of data.

We focus specifically on irregular multivariate time series (IMTS), the most common form of time-indexed data in the industrial settings that motivate this work. Multivariate time series arise whenever several sensors jointly measure a system over time, and are ubiquitous across domains, from clinical monitoring to industrial process control. In many industrial contexts, however, the channels of a multivariate series are not recorded synchronously: sensors sample at different rates, drop out for periods of time, or are only active over different intervals, so that no single, shared timestamp grid exists across channels. This is not an edge case; it is close to the default in real deployments. In our own application, comparing an oracle and a simulated signal to detect false positives in nuclear Instrumentation and Control (I&C) software testing [28], the two compared signals are independently sampled and routinely differ in rate, producing exactly this kind of irregularity.

The literature on IMTS classification is comparatively limited, and coreset selection specifically for IMTS is scarcer still. On the classification side, recent architectures such as GRU-D [40], SEFT [35], and adapted Transformer variants [34, 35] handle irregularity by encoding missingness directly, typically via masking indicators or continuous time embeddings, rather than by imputing to a regular grid first. On the coreset side, the closest prior work we are aware of is [41], who construct coresets with provable size guarantees for time series clustering under a parametric Gaussian mixture model with autocorrelation. Their setting differs from ours in three respects: it targets clustering rather than classification, it assumes regularly time-indexed panel data rather than irregular, asynchronously sampled channels, and its notion of similarity is defined by the parametric generative model rather than by any geometric property of the observed trajectories. Closer in spirit to our approach, [42] use the sliced Wasserstein distance directly for unsupervised training data selection in an industrial setting, filtering points whose removal would most reduce the empirical distributional distance to the rest of the dataset. Their method targets outlier filtering on raw, fixed-dimensional features, however, and does not address either the irregularity of multivariate time series or a representation capturing their geometric structure; the underlying intuition, that a sliced-Wasserstein criterion can guide data selection in industrial settings, is one we share, but apply to a different problem, through a different representation and with a different algorithm.
