papers.title: SPAR: Self-Referenced World-Model Rewards for Physical Alignment in Video Generation
papers.abstract: Generating videos with physically plausible dynamics remains challenging despite advances in visual quality. Latent world models offer predictive signals for evaluating physical plausibility, but higher agreement between predicted and observed features may reflect easier-to-predict scene content rather than more plausible dynamics. We propose \textbf{S}elf-Referenced \textbf{P}hysical \textbf{A}lignment \textbf{R}ewards (\textbf{SPAR}), a framework that uses world-model predictions for inference-time physical alignment. SPAR compares each video's prediction error with that of static clips constructed by repeating its own frames, providing a content-matched reference for evaluating generated dynamics. To account for the uneven spatial and temporal distribution of physical interactions, we introduce a unified \textbf{spatiotemporal reward refinement} strategy. \textbf{Spatial refinement} emphasizes localized prediction discrepancies, while \textbf{temporal refinement} moderates brief error peaks and supplements prediction errors with agreement between predicted and observed feature changes. Evaluations across multiple benchmarks demonstrate that SPAR improves the physical plausibility of both \textbf{text-to-video generation} and \textbf{image-to-video continuation}, bringing generated dynamics into closer alignment with the physical regularities governing real-world events. Additional results and resources are available at https://gavin-jy.github.io/spar-page/

papers.title: Predict Backbone, Graft Dynamics: A Decoupled Paradigm for Time Series Forecasting
papers.abstract: Modern long-term forecasters are typically optimized for point-wise accuracy, which rewards dominant low-frequency backbones but often suppresses high-utility local dynamics such as abrupt variations, transient surges, and turning points. We propose Predict Backbone, Graft Dynamics, a decoupled forecasting paradigm that separates stable structural prediction from grounded dynamic restoration. We instantiate it as GRAFT, where a base forecaster predicts the reliable trajectory backbone, and a dedicated grafting path restores historically recurrent dynamics through retrieval-based evidence, phase-aware release, channel-wise control, and restoration-cooperative optimization. Unlike generic post-hoc revision methods that correct residual errors, GRAFT formulates the second stage as grounded dynamic grafting, where historical response evidence is calibrated into transferable dynamics and selectively grafted onto the backbone under phase-, channel-, and confidence-aware constraints. Across the full evaluation grid of seven benchmarks, two metrics, four horizons, and six backbones, GRAFT improves over the corresponding backbone in 87% of all comparisons, with average MSE/MAE reductions of 4.6%/3.9%. Dynamic-window analyses show that GRAFT restores local dynamics while preserving the stable backbone structure. These results suggest a new principle for high-utility forecasting: predict the backbone, then graft the dynamics.

papers.title: Query-Sample Tradeoffs for Revenue Maximization
papers.abstract:
We introduce and study the full query-sample tradeoff for revenue maximization with a single buyer whose value follows an unknown distribution. A learner may adaptively combine value samples, which reveal full buyer values, with pricing queries, which reveal only whether a fresh buyer accepts a selected price. The goal is to learn a price that achieves a $(1-\varepsilon)$-multiplicative approximation to optimal revenue with high probability. We ask when, and by how much, reducing the sample budget increases the number of pricing queries required.
  We establish tight tradeoff bounds for monotone-hazard-rate (MHR), regular, and quasi-monotone-hazard-rate (quasi-MHR) distributions, and almost tight bounds for quasi-regular distributions. Our results reveal sharply different benefits from combining the two information sources. Quasi-MHR distributions admit a smooth intermediate tradeoff: additional samples can reduce the query requirement by polynomial factors. For MHR and regular distributions, however, a sufficiently small constant fraction of the sample-only requirement still leaves the learner facing the full asymptotic query cost attainable with one sample. Our upper bounds are achieved by algorithms that collect all value samples before making queries, while our lower bounds hold even under arbitrary adaptive interleaving of the two forms of access. Along the way, we also fully characterize the sample-only and single-sample query complexities for all four families, eliminating the extra logarithmic dependence on $1/\varepsilon$ in the literature.

papers.title: RoboHarness-RL: Agentic Reinforcement Learning for VLM-Based Robot Manipulation
papers.abstract: Agentic harnesses enable frontier vision-language models (VLMs) to manipulate robots through perception, planning, and control tools, yet achieving comparable performance with compact open-weight VLMs remains challenging. We present RoboHarness-RL, an agentic reinforcement learning framework for improving VLM-based robot manipulation through tool calls. Starting from supervised fine-tuning on successful teacher demonstrations, the VLM further improves through multi-turn reinforcement learning with task-outcome rewards, without relying on vision-language-action models or world action models. To support efficient multi-turn training, we develop LiteHarness, which uses hierarchical memory to keep interaction contexts compact while preserving task performance. With Qwen3.5-9B, RL raises success from 31.2% to 44.0% on RoboTwin 2.0 and from 57.8% to 73.3% on LIBERO-Pro; these gains extend to randomized RoboTwin scenes unseen during training (26.4% to 38.0%). Behavioral analysis further shows that RL reduces repetitive-call rates by up to $4\times$, shortens successful executions, and improves recovery from negative feedback. Project page: https://aim-uofa.github.io/RoboHarness-RL/

papers.title: BodyWeave: Native Body-Conditioned 3D Garment Generation
papers.abstract: Generating 3D garments for digital characters requires preserving a reference design while adapting the garment to the target body's shape and pose. Sewing-pattern methods can struggle to reproduce unfamiliar designs and fine details, while image-to-3D generators offer rich shape priors but typically lack explicit 3D body context. We present \textbf{BodyWeave}, a framework that unifies garment generation and fitting through native 3D body conditioning. Building on 3D generative priors, BodyWeave uses the body as a spatial reference throughout geometry generation: a \textbf{Global Body Adapter} guides garment placement and extent in the shared coordinate frame, while \textbf{Local Body Attention} guides surface refinement using nearby body geometry. A \textbf{Surface Penetration Loss} supervises decoded surfaces to reduce body intersections, and the resulting geometry conditions material synthesis to produce garments with physically based rendering attributes. To support learning across designs and wearers, we construct \textbf{GarmentWeave3D} with 293K aligned garment--body observations, including 114K same-design cross-body pairs. Evaluations on out-of-domain \textbf{Artist-Created Garments} demonstrate high geometric fidelity and low body penetration. Cross-body evaluations demonstrate accurate adaptation to new wearers with consistent garment--body spacing, while appearance comparisons show faithful fabric reproduction. Additional results and resources are available at https://gavin-jy.github.io/bodyweave-page/

authors.institution: Louisiana State University Health Sciences Center Shreveport

authors.institution: Affiliated Hospital of North Sichuan Medical College

papers.title: DeCo-Attention: Decompose to Compensate for Low-Precision Attention
papers.abstract: Self-attention over tens of thousands of tokens dominates the generation time of video diffusion transformers, because its cost grows quadratically with sequence length. The FP4 matrix products of modern GPUs can speed up attention, but the 4-bit rounding of the queries Q and the keys K introduces large errors. We show that the exponential in softmax amplifies the error of their product QK, which therefore dominates the attention error. We propose DeCo-Attention, a co-design of algorithm and system for low-precision attention. DeCo-Attention is training-free and compensates the rounding error of Q and K along a few principal directions found by a per-head eigendecomposition. The lightweight compensation terms are appended to Q and K as extra channels, so the FP4 matrix product corrects its own rounding error while it computes the attention scores. Once the products run in FP4, the softmax bounds the kernel, and we optimize the softmax so that the gain of FP4 computation translates into realized speedup. With QK in FP4, we implement DeCo-Attention with the rest of attention in FP8 on GB300 and VR200 and in FP4 on RTX PRO 6000. On Wan2.2, these kernels run 2.13x, 2.49x, and 2.82x faster than BF16 attention, and the whole generation runs 1.55x, 1.68x, and 1.80x faster. On four video generation models, the FP8 configuration achieves LPIPS comparable to prior 8-bit QK methods, and the fully FP4 configuration lower LPIPS than prior fully 4-bit kernels.

authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Mengdi Wang
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: EffectWAM: Learning Action-Grounded Effects for Robot Manipulation
papers.abstract: World-action models connect visual prediction with executable robot control. We present EffectWAM, which develops this connection through three complementary components: Effect, camera positional encoding (CaPE), and Action Grounding. Effect represents visual change as the difference between independently encoded future observations and a shared current-observation anchor. CaPE conditions endpoint pooling on relative camera pose when reliable extrinsics are available, while sharing the same learned parameters with pose-free pooling for uncalibrated trajectories. Action Grounding trains the visual representation to retain measured changes in end-effector pose and gripper state. An exponential moving average of the observation encoder supplies Effect targets. A shared generation expert learns to jointly predict Effect and an executable action chunk through flow matching, and reuses the sampled pair to generate future video on demand. This allows the controller to execute actions without waiting for video synthesis. We train on more than 20,000 hours of heterogeneous embodied data, excluding unused chain-of-thought data, and accommodate dataset-specific joint, end-effector, and hand-pose representations. Our evaluation uses the Small (8B) configuration on all five benchmarks and additionally evaluates the Large (26B) configuration on RoboDojo. Experiments examine closed-loop manipulation across complementary benchmarks, and comparisons across multiple baseline policies show consistent improvements from Action Grounding.

papers.title: More Powerful, Less Verifiable? Mitigating Hard-to-Verify Hallucinations in MLLM's Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) strengthens model capabilities through feedback from humans and environments. However, emerging evidence suggests that reward optimization can produce outputs whose errors are harder for humans to detect. To address this issue, we construct ITHV (the Image-Text Hallucination Verifiability Dataset), comprising 2,728 visually grounded instances that distinguish between obvious hallucinations, which humans readily detect, and elusive hallucinations, which humans struggle to identify. We then propose DAPO-V, an extension of DAPO that maximizes correctness subject to a budget on verifiability-aware risk. Specifically, DAPO-V combines a verifiability-aware reward with adaptive dual control, where larger penalties are assigned to incorrect responses on questions with lower human verification accuracy. An adaptive multiplier further adjusts the penalty strength according to risk-budget violations. Across three MLLM base models, DAPO-V improves overall accuracy while substantially improving accuracy on elusive hallucination questions by 5.78--9.72 percentage points over accuracy-only DAPO. We further test DAPO-V with a blinded human study, which shows that hallucinations are more readily detected in DAPO-V than those of the base model.

papers.title: Automated Smoke Testing for Multi-ending Game Quests via Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Modern game quests are increasingly trending toward high freedom and multiple endings, making their design and testing more complex. Smoke testing in games aims to rapidly validate quest functionality, but existing automated testing approaches face critical limitations when handling quests with branching narratives, and multiple possible endings. These challenges result in insufficient exploration of endings, redundant action sequences, and prohibitively high interaction costs. To address these challenges, we propose EndWeaver, an automated smoke testing framework specifically designed for multi-ending game tasks. EndWeaver leverages LLMs to interpret quest descriptions and game environments, generating high-level methods to guide global exploration, complemented by the generated primitive task sequences for fine-grained planning. By combining this multi-level planning structure with the dynamic construction of state-transition graphs, EndWeaver ensures comprehensive coverage of all possible endings and enables efficient testing. We evaluated EndWeaver on four game environments---Mini RPG, Overcooked Plus, Minecraft, and PySC2 against baseline methods. In all environments, EndWeaver achieved stable quest completion with high reliability, significantly outperforming the baselines. In terms of testing cost, EndWeaver required only a few thousand steps, while baseline methods required millions of steps, all while ensuring comprehensive coverage of all possible quest endings. Ablation studies further demonstrated the critical contributions of each framework component, validating the effectiveness and robustness of our approach.

papers.title: Ego2Real: Learning Bimanual Dexterous Manipulation from Egocentric Visuo-Tactile Demonstrations
papers.abstract: Learning dexterous manipulation from egocentric human demonstrations offers a scalable path toward robot skill acquisition. Vision alone, however, provides limited information about physical contacts and the demonstrator's force intent, leading to ambiguities in interpreting hand-object interactions. Capturing human touch via tactile sensing is therefore crucial for reliable human-to-robot dexterous skill transfer. We present Ego2Real, a framework that leverages egocentric demonstrations and tactile gloves to transfer bimanual dexterous manipulation skills to robotic hands. Ego2Real incorporates tactile supervision at two complementary stages: (1) tactile-guided hand-object interaction reconstruction, which uses measured tactile signals to refine hand poses and contact geometry; and (2) contact-informed reinforcement learning, which translates human contact patterns into robotic contact rewards. By combining refined motion references with physical contact rewards during training, Ego2Real guides anthropomorphic robotic hands to emulate demonstrated contact behaviors while adapting to their own morphology and actuation. Experiments show that incorporating tactile supervision into both reconstruction and policy learning yields higher manipulation success rates, underscoring the importance of enriching egocentric demonstrations with tactile observations to improve their quality and transferability.

authors.name: Ange Bao
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory Fluid Power and Mechatronic Systems

papers.title: Let The Pixels Through: Rethinking Long Skip Connections for Scalable Pixel Diffusion
papers.abstract: Training pixel diffusion models remains less straightforward, owing to the ad hoc training recipes and architecture designs, along with the sensitivity to hyper-parameter choices. We show that strong denoisers can be built by refining existing pixel-native designs from the literature. Specifically, we revisit the long skip connection in U-Net and find that the optimization benefit commonly attributed to it is not necessary for its denoising benefit. We further find that the conventional linear combination of features from the skip and main backbone is inadequate for regimes of various noise levels. Motivated by these observations, we introduce two core modifications. First, we adopt asymmetric long skips, which propagate fine-grained information from input embeddings to decoder layers. Second, we introduce adaGLU, a SwiGLU-like MLP block, in decoder layers to adaptively filter information from the embeddings before being added to main-branch features. The above designs give a simple pixel diffusion transformer architecture. When trained from scratch, it scales smoothly from small-scale baselines up to 1.6B parameters, achieving 1.62 and 1.70 FID on ImageNet-256 and -512, respectively. Besides, it natively supports multimodal inputs, such as text and images, yielding competitive performance in text-to-image generation. We release our codes at https://github.com/AMAP-ML/PiT

papers.title: SoccerNarrate: Event-Grounded Streaming Soccer Commentary with Macro-Window Preference Alignment
papers.abstract: Existing clip-based soccer commentary models often produce delayed, repeated, or poorly synchronized narration on untrimmed full-match videos. Recent streaming video-language models make low-latency full-match narration feasible, but they often favor general descriptions rather than professional, event-grounded soccer commentary. They may describe nearby actions while failing to mention key events such as goals, cards, substitutions, and offsides correctly and on time. In this paper, we present SoccerNarrate to bridge low-latency streaming narration with event-grounded professional soccer commentary across data, training, and evaluation. First, we construct SoccerNarrate-Data, a large-scale time-anchored dataset with word-level ASR alignment, quality filtering, and entity calibration. Second, we perform macro-window preference alignment (MWPA), which aligns the model with complete event-level commentary semantics by comparing causal multi-step rollouts from the same streaming prefix while keeping second-level inference unchanged. We further use event-mismatched human commentaries as counterfactual negatives to emphasize event semantics over commentary style. Third, we introduce SoccerNarrate-Eval, an event-centric benchmark based on temporally constrained event entailment. Full-match experiments show that SoccerNarrate improves event coverage and event-aligned precision over strong offline and streaming baselines. Code and models are released at https://github.com/MCG-NJU/SoccerNarrate.

papers.title: Making Evaluation Explicit Is Not Enough: Supervising the Evaluation Process in Generative Reward Models
papers.abstract: Generative reward models (GRMs) make language-model evaluation more explicit by generating critiques, rubrics, or intermediate analyses before predicting a final preference. However, explicit evaluation does not necessarily imply a reliable evaluation process: under outcome-only supervision, a model may reach the correct final preference while producing weak or unsupported intermediate judgments, turning the evaluation into a post-hoc rationalization. We introduce STEP-GRM, a framework that directly supervises the intermediate evaluation process of rubric-based GRMs. In addition to conventional preference supervision, STEP-GRM provides structural guidance for rubric construction and local supervision for criterion-level judgments, encouraging the model to learn not only the correct final preference but also a more reliable process for reaching it. Extensive experiments show that STEP-GRM achieves strong performance on standard reward-modeling benchmarks while improving the consistency and correctness of intermediate evaluations. Moreover, reward signals produced by STEP-GRM lead to better downstream policy optimization, demonstrating that more reliable evaluation processes can translate into practical gains beyond reward-model accuracy.

papers.title: RightDiff: Learning Generative Reward Models to Judge by the Right Differences
papers.abstract: Generative reward models typically rely on generic query-level rubrics or unconstrained rationales, overlooking the fact that pairwise preference is driven by response-specific differences. Moreover, optimizing solely for outcome correctness encourages models to exploit superficial shortcuts such as verbosity and formatting, triggering rationale drift. To address this, we propose RightDiff, which structures pairwise evaluation into an evidence-grounded evaluation trajectory executed in a single autoregressive generation. RightDiff explicitly discovers contrastive differences between candidates, categorizes them into material or immaterial factors, and induces pair-specific rubrics before final adjudication. To train this process without post-hoc rationalization, we synthesize demonstration data via response-isolated prompts and optimize the reward model with a difference-alignment reward regularized by budget-constrained one-to-one matching and multiplicative gating. RightDiff achieves state-of-the-art preference modeling performance on RewardBench and RM-Bench, surpassing all open-source reward models and leading proprietary LLM judges. Downstream, it provides reliable supervision for direct preference optimization on Arena-Hard and AlpacaEval while effectively resisting length shortcuts.

papers.title: MediaStormBench-CameraLog: Can Multimodal Models Identify a Camera's Log Curve?
papers.abstract: MediaStormBench is a multimodal benchmark for real-world film and television production, with each subset drawn from MediaStorm's day-to-day work. We release its first subset, MediaStormBench-CameraLog (CameraLogBench), on a common foundational task in footage ingest and initial color grading: identifying the Log curve of a clip without metadata. Cameras record Log footage by compressing a wide range of scene light into code values with a vendor-defined logarithmic curve, and color can be restored correctly only once that curve is known. The curve, however, is recorded only in file metadata, easily lost in transcoding and team hand-offs. A colorist then has to try candidate curves one by one against a waveform scope, and a wrong choice shifts the tones and colors of the whole clip. Recovering the curve from the image alone is challenging, because vendor curves cluster tightly in code value and are coupled with unknown exposure. CameraLogBench is built on professionally shot footage and tests whether multimodal models can identify the curve, with a probe that removes the correct option to expose guessing from priors. Because every candidate curve is strictly defined by a published vendor formula, we derive four controls from one implementation of these formulas: graded negatives, synthetic frames of identical scenes, in-context specification digests, and a training-free formula baseline, which together decouple semantic priors from photometric measurement. Across 11 models, real-footage accuracy barely exceeds always guessing the most frequent curve; when the correct option is removed, models almost never abstain, revealing heavy reliance on scene and brand priors. Supplying the vendor specification sharply improves recognition on calibrated charts but hardly helps on natural images without a photometric reference, exposing a gap between reading a specification and measuring pixels.

papers.title: A User-Item Aware Encoding Framework for Short Video
papers.abstract: Traditional encoding methods from the Professional Generated Content (PGC) era face significant challenges due to two unique characteristics of user-generated short videos: massive daily uploads (reaching hundreds of millions) and heterogeneous content-consumer relationships (varying video quality and diverse consumer contexts). To address these challenges, we propose UIAE (User-Item Aware Encoding), a novel multiple bitrate ladder group encoding method comprising three key components: 1) Establishing user-item relationships via rule-based or DNN-based models; 2) Developing local optimization models maximizing Quality of Experience (QoE) for sub-populations based on contextual consumption patterns; 3) Deriving globally optimal encoding strategies through hierarchical model integration. Experimental results demonstrate that the UIAE framework adaptively adjusts encoding outcomes for distinct user groups with varying context profiles, ensuring optimal QoE for end viewers. We have deployed the UIAE method into the online pipeline, handling tens of millions of video transcoding tasks daily.

papers.title: OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval
papers.abstract: Multimodal retrieval must match dense pages, fine-grained entities, ordered video, and agent tools and memory. Single-vector embeddings lose local evidence, cross-encoders reread every recalled item online, and uncompressed late interaction is too large to serve. We present OmniEVIE, a 4.5B multi-vector embedding model covering text, images, visual documents, video, and tools with one compressed index and a three-stage retriever. Each record stores at most 128 int8 vectors of dimension 64 (9,472 bytes, or 8.82 GiB per million records), providing a mean vector, 1-bit signs, and int8 multi-vectors for coarse, middle, and final search while localizing each hit to a page region or video interval. Training, merging, indexing, and retrieval are co-designed: all tasks share one retrieval format, a three-grade evidence check removes false negatives, dynamic sampling follows the baseline-teacher gap, candidates are compressed with ST-HAC during training to match the index, stage-wise and specialist models are merged by parameter block, and a saliency gate with a noise floor refines query scoring. Trained on public datasets, OmniEVIE scores 60.68 (full d=2048 sequence) and 60.06 (K128 x d64 int8 index) on MMEB-V3 (190 tasks), 77.96 on MMEB-V2 (78 tasks), and 62.96 on ViDoRe V3 (48 tasks). On 1M and 5M records, a single-thread query takes 54.2 ms and 120.2 ms (11.1x and 25.3x faster than exact 4096-d single-vector search; 236x and 532x faster than full int8 MaxSim). Video is encoded directly from frames without a parsing model: on QVHighlights (1,083 queries), the peak falls inside the labeled segment for 78.0% of queries and the returned span (18% of video length) intersects it for 94.3% vs. 44.9% random. Weights and code: https://huggingface.co/tencent/OmniEVIE-4B and https://github.com/Tencent/OmniEVIE.

papers.title: Roboclock: A Unified Benchmark for Time-Aware Robotic Intelligence
papers.abstract: Time is a fundamental dimension of robotic intelligence: a robot may fail despite physically correct actions if it acts outside a valid time window, responds too slowly to an event, or fails to meet required throughput. Yet existing robotic benchmarks primarily emphasize spatial correctness and logical task completion, largely overlooking the temporal constraints of real-world applications. We present RoboClock, a unified benchmark for time-aware robotic manipulation featuring 60 tasks across five application domains. Mirroring these failure modes, RoboClock structures tasks around three types of temporal constraints: Temporal Window, Event-Reactive, and Throughput. Furthermore, RoboClock incorporates a Latency-Aligned evaluation protocol that continuously advances environment time during model inference and control-interface delays, paired with time-sensitive metrics. Evaluating over 30 methods, we find that the best-performing approach is the trained VLA, yet it achieves only 8.3% temporal success even on Easy-level tasks, with persistent challenges in generalization and transfer. These findings reveal fundamental limitations in current robotic systems and highlight the need to jointly optimize physical competence, temporal reasoning, and execution latency.

authors.name: Zhijing Wu
authors.institution: Southwest University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Convergence and error analysis of problem-independent machine learning (PIML) with linear completeness
papers.abstract: Problem-independent machine learning (PIML) is an effective computational approach that combines the finite element method with machine learning. PIML uses neural networks to learn the mapping from material distributions or element geometries to the numerical shape functions of substructures. This approach avoids repeated computation while preserving the conformity of the underlying finite element discretization, thereby significantly improving the efficiency of substructure-based finite element analysis. However, existing studies on PIML have primarily focused on numerical accuracy and computational efficiency, while rigorous theoretical analyses of its approximation errors are still limited. In this paper, we establish an error analysis framework for PIML from a classical finite element perspective, in which the numerical error is bounded in terms of the finite element discretization error and the network generalization error. Our analysis shows that, when only rigid-body displacement invariance is enforced, the resulting error estimate contains a learning-induced term that does not necessarily decrease under mesh refinement. To ensure convergence, we propose an improved PIML scheme with linear completeness. By using linear displacement field constraints to reconstruct the corresponding columns of the transition matrix, we ensure that the resulting numerical shape-function space contains the space of linear polynomials. We derive error estimates and establish convergence results of the improved scheme in the H1 and L2 norms. Numerical experiments verify the theoretical results and demonstrate that the improved PIML achieves optimal convergence rates, good generalization performance, and numerical stability.

authors.name: Chong-Jun Li
authors.institution: Changchun University of Science and Technology

papers.title: GOLD-SLAM: Gaussian-splatting Omnidirectional LiDAR-Depth SLAM
papers.abstract: Panoramic cameras capture nearly the entire spherical field of view in a single frame. However, the mismatch between this panoramic coverage and the field of view of LiDAR poses a substantial challenge for panoramic Gaussian splatting SLAM that relies on LiDAR depth priors. We introduce GOLD-SLAM, a Gaussian-splatting Omnidirectional LiDAR-Depth SLAM system that combines high-quality rendering with accurate geometric reconstruction. It performs tracking and mapping in the spherical domain and uses tracked visual features in regions without LiDAR coverage to improve pose estimation. To address insufficient coverage of newly observed surfaces and floating artifacts during incremental mapping, we introduce Depth-Aware Map Extension and Pruning (DAEP). To enable broader evaluation, we collect a new dataset, WHOLE, using a UAV platform across Weak-geometry, High-dynamic, Omnidirectional, Low-light, and Easy scenarios. Extensive experiments on public benchmarks and WHOLE demonstrate competitive rendering quality and improved geometric accuracy relative to perspective systems. Compared with existing panoramic baselines, GOLD-SLAM improves mean PSNR by 5.56-9.10 dB and reduces mean Depth-L1 by 71.9-83.9%. To assess deployment feasibility on resource-constrained platforms such as UAVs, we evaluate an embedded configuration of GOLD-SLAM on a Jetson Orin NX (16 GB), demonstrating online operation at the cost of reconstruction quality.

authors.name: Yufan Chen
authors.institution: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Get the Next Moment Right: Short-Term Event Planning for Physically Plausible Video Generation
papers.abstract: Video generation models synthesize realistic imagery yet still struggle to produce physically plausible evolution. Existing methods guide generation with a motion trajectory predicted for the entire clip in advance, so prediction errors accumulate and degrade later frames. We propose STEP(Short-Term Event Planning), a training-free closed-loop framework that guides generation one short clip at a time. Each round consists of four steps: grounding measures the scene state from the latest frames, event planning predicts the next physical event and renders it into a control clip, latent-guided generation produces the next short clip under this control, and verification checks whether the event occurs and resamples the clip if it does not. Because each round is grounded in the frames actually generated, control relies only on reliable short-range predictions. STEP improves the physical plausibility of three frozen generators on Physics-IQ Verified and PhyGenBench, and can be applied to new generators without training.

papers.title: On the Importance of Hidden-State Refinement in Masked Diffusion Language Models
papers.abstract: Masked diffusion language models (MDLMs) generate text by iteratively denoising masked or corrupted token sequences, allowing token predictions to condition on bidirectional context and update multiple positions in parallel. While each denoising step produces a rich layer-wise hidden-state trajectory, prior work typically focuses only on token-level information and discards these continuous hidden states, leaving their refinement dynamics underexplored. In this work, we analyze hidden-state dynamics in MDLMs and find clear evidence of layer-wise and cross-step refinement: smooth evolution across adjacent layers, greater predictive power in deeper layers, gradual degradation under transformer block removal, and strong final-state alignment across consecutive denoising steps. Motivated by these observations, we propose Cross-Step Recurrent Refinement (CSRR), a mechanism that carries hidden-state information across denoising steps to enhance generation. Extensive experiments show that CSRR improves text generation quality, highlighting the critical role of continuous hidden-state refinement in MDLMs. Project page: https://zhongzero.github.io/Recurrent-DLLM/

authors.name: Hourong Li
authors.institution: Rutgers, The State University of New Jersey

papers.title: OmniPersist: Persistent Dynamic World Modeling via Coupled Panoramic Evolution
papers.abstract: Action-conditioned world models play a vital role in robotics and autonomous driving, yet existing video diffusion models struggle to maintain dynamic object persistence. When the camera turns away and returns, out-of-view moving entities fail to evolve plausibly in latent space, often mutating or vanishing entirely due to bounded perspective views. To resolve this issue, we propose OmniPersist, a unified framework that couples perspective video generation with panoramic evolution within a single-stage diffusion model, without relying on auxiliary models or initial panoramic inputs. To maintain efficiency, we model the panoramic stream at a lower frame rate, bridging both views across space and time via Geometric Anchoring (GeoAnch) for spatial correspondence and Temporal Compensation (TemComp) for temporal aggregation. OmniPersist is agnostic to camera-control architectures, supporting both latent-level and attention-level conditioning. Extensive experiments on a newly constructed dynamic benchmark across image-to-video and video continuation tasks demonstrate consistent gains in visual quality, camera controllability, revisit consistency, and dynamic persistence.

authors.name: Wenxi Liu
authors.institution: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

papers.title: RecurSciBench: Benchmarking Recursive Self-Improvement in Data-Driven Scientific Research
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based agents are advancing the automation of data-driven scientific research. Recent advances in recursive self-improvement (RSI) offer the potential for these agents to continuously improve through experience, but evaluating transfer across scientific tasks requires executable, scientifically verifiable tasks and independent assessment of self-improvement gains. We introduce RecurSciBench, a scalable benchmark for evaluating RSI in data-driven scientific research. Its RecurSciPipe framework automatically constructs scientific modeling and data analysis tasks from raw datasets, with execution-based verification and scientific validity checks. RecurSciBench spans four scientific domains, multiple data modalities, and varied scientific objectives. We evaluate four RSI systems by comparing their initial and evolved states on independent tasks after evolution on source tasks, covering within-type, cross-type, and cross-domain transfer. Experiments show that the benefits of self-improvement vary across agent systems and scientific domains. Positive overall gains can coexist with regressions on individual tasks. Experience can transfer across task types and benefit other domains even without measurable gains in the source domain.

authors.name: Jingbo Zhou
authors.institution: Xi'an University of Science and Technology

papers.title: GeoSurge: Geometry-Grounded Multimodal Reasoning for Auditable Liver Resection Planning
papers.abstract: Surgical resection planning centers on generating executable resection surfaces from anatomical evidence and operative constraints. Medical multimodal foundation models enable anatomical understanding, and segmentation models predict resection regions, but neither translates these capabilities into explicitly constrained, executable resection surfaces. We present GeoSurge, an anatomy-grounded framework that combines mask-derived metrics with structure-aware point-cloud tokens to generate executable, editable resection surfaces. To make resection geometry learnable and editable, GeoSurge maps actions to parametric geometry through a surface-action grammar. Using this grammar, anatomy-oriented and tumor-centered templates generate candidates, which are filtered by hard constraints and semantic deduplication. Training supervision is then derived from candidate-expert geometric agreement and independently recomputed feasibility metrics. At inference, the reasoner uses patient evidence and surgical requirements to select or revise an action, which an independent geometry engine subsequently materializes and verifies. GeoSurge achieves the best overall scores on DeepTumour Liver and CRLM-QA, improving the constraint satisfaction rate from 73% to 100% on CRLM and from 56% to 99% on GeoSurge-Bench.

authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: TokenMatte: Unlocking T2V Diffusion Priors for Pixel-Native Video Matting
papers.abstract: High-resolution video matting requires accurate recovery of continuous alpha values, including fine hair, soft boundaries, and motion blur, yet dense alpha supervision remains scarce. Pretrained text-to-video diffusion transformers (DiTs) offer rich spatio-temporal priors, whereas existing generative video matting approaches typically route alpha predictions through RGB-trained VAE latents, which can attenuate fine details and introduce additional decoding overhead. We present TokenMatte, which adapts a pretrained video DiT into a single-pass, auxiliary-free RGB-to-alpha predictor with a pixel-native output interface. At its core is a single shared linear readout that maps each spatio-temporal token directly to its corresponding ($t \times p \times p$) block of alpha pixels, predicting spatial details and temporal variations within the same local video block. Tiling these blocks produces the full-resolution alpha sequence without a convolutional decoder or learned upsampling. The predicted alpha is supervised directly in pixel space, while the ground-truth alpha never enters the VAE, eliminating target-side alpha encoding and output-side VAE decoding. Leveraging the pretrained video prior, TokenMatte is trained using only existing public matting datasets, without additional data curation or auxiliary inputs at inference. Compared with a matched latent-output baseline, our pixel-native interface improves matting accuracy while achieving a 1.51$\times$ inference speedup. TokenMatte establishes a new auxiliary-free state of the art on VideoMatte, YouTubeMatte, and V-HIM60.

authors.name: Shilong Liu
authors.institution: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Cif-query bridging for audio-native asr transfer to visual speech recognition
papers.abstract: Audio-native automatic speech recognition (ASR) models provide strong speech-language priors, but their compact acoustic interfaces are mismatched with long, frame-level visual features. We propose CIF-Query Bridge, a lightweight connection from a Paraformer visual speech recognition (VSR) encoder to Qwen3-ASR. The existing visual continuous integrate-and-fire (CIF) predictor produces an input-dependent number of token-rate queries; a two-layer cross-attention bridge refines them against the complete frame sequence, and a linear adapter feeds the pretrained ASR projector and decoder. This design preserves access to uncompressed visual context while avoiding direct autoregressive processing of hundreds of video frames. On CMLR, the complete visual-only transfer system achieves 7.97% character error rate, compared with 11.78% for native Paraformer under the same test split and scoring protocol---a 3.81-point absolute and 32.3% relative reduction. Controlled ablations characterize bridge depth, projector initialization, adapter capacity, and CTC supervision. The results show that CIF-derived adaptive queries provide a compact interface for transferring audio-native ASR capability to VSR.

authors.name: Dongliang Xie
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

authors.name: Wanpeng Xie
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: A Hybrid Analytical-Neural Residual Surrogate for Fast Radio Propagation Prediction over Irregular Terrain
papers.abstract: Fast prediction of radio-wave propagation over irregular terrain is important for coverage analysis in mountainous environments, where many terrain and antenna configurations must be evaluated repeatedly. High-fidelity split-step parabolic equation (SSPE) solvers can capture terrain-induced shadowing and interference, but their computational cost is high for repeated planning studies. Learning-based surrogates reduce this cost, but direct field regression asks the network to learn both analytically tractable propagation trends and terrain-dependent residual structure. This paper proposes a hybrid analytical-neural residual surrogate that separates these two parts. A deterministic analytical baseline represents free-space spreading, antenna directivity, modified knife-edge diffraction, and terrain-aware specular reflection, while a compact coarse-to-fine neural network predicts the residual field. The network uses baseline-derived guidance channels, anisotropic convolutions, and feature-wise antenna conditioning to match the directional structure of terrain propagation fields. On synthetic SSPE data at 1.0 GHz, the proposed model achieves an MAE of 2.1061 dB, compared with 3.3955 dB for a standard U-Net and 3.2560 dB for a reproduced physics-guided CNN, while reducing the average inference time to 11.30 ms per sample. A zero-shot test at 1.8 GHz gives an MAE of 2.8692 dB without retraining, and a case study on the measured Hjorringvej terrain profile shows that the prediction remains consistent with the SSPE reference and follows the measured path-loss trend.

authors.name: Hao Qin
authors.institution: Tianjin Medical University Cancer Institute and Hospital

papers.title: A degree-sum condition for paths through prescribed vertices
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a graph of order $n$ and let $S\subseteq V(G)$. Denote by $\kappa(S)$ the minimum size of a vertex set separating two vertices of $S$, and by $\sigma_p(S)$ the minimum degree sum over all independent sets of $p$ vertices in $S$. We prove that if $\kappa(S)\ge k\ge2$ and $\sigma_p(S)\ge n+(p-1)^2$ for every integer $p\ge k$, then any two distinct vertices of $S$ are joined by a path containing all vertices of $S$. This gives a path version of Ota's theorem on cycles containing a prescribed set of vertices. As an application, we prove a conjecture of Faudree, Faudree, Gould, Jacobson and Magnant: for $k\ge3$, every $k$-connected graph $G$ of order $n$ satisfying $\delta(G)>(n+k^2-2k)/k$ and $\delta(G)\ge\alpha(G)+k-2$ is hamiltonian-connected.

authors.name: Kun Cheng
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: Beyond Fixed-Context Likelihood: Zero-Shot AI-Generated Text Detection via Context Perturbation Discrepancy
papers.abstract: The same increase in token log probability from earlier context can be typical at one position and unusually large at another. We introduce Context Perturbation Discrepancy (CPD), a zero-shot detector that measures this gain relative to what a single pretrained language model expects. Keeping the passage fixed, CPD scores each observed token under its full prefix and under a short window of recent tokens. Under the full-prefix distribution, the expected gain equals the KL divergence from that distribution to the restricted-prefix distribution. CPD subtracts this expectation from each observed gain and scales the sum of the signed deviations by its analytical reference standard deviation. On unedited human and AI texts from GEN, DetectRL-X, and HART, subtracting the expected gain raises AUROC by 32.78-35.81 percentage points at the same variance scale. CPD outperforms seven zero-shot baselines, averaging 94.80% AUROC and 79.60% recall at a 5% false-positive rate. On original and edited HART passages, the same scores separate texts more clearly by draft origin than by the benchmark's final-expression labels (89.15% versus 65.50% AUROC). Code is available at https://github.com/BUPT-tyf/CPD.

papers.title: NABLA: A Noise-Adaptive Blockwise Left-Right Preconditioning Algorithm for Stochastic Optimization
papers.abstract: We propose NABLA, a noise-adaptive blockwise left-right preconditioning algorithm for mini-batch stochastic nonconvex optimization. NABLA combines an exponential moving average of stochastic gradients with block-diagonal row and column preconditioners constructed from matrix-valued second-moment statistics. Unlike conventional matrix-preconditioned methods that use fixed decay parameters, NABLA adjusts the second-moment averaging coefficient through a closed-loop feedback rule determined by the cumulative stochastic-gradient energy and its running average. The first-moment coefficient remains fixed, allowing the trajectory-dependent adaptation to act directly on the structured preconditioners. The resulting method is horizon-free, requires no prior knowledge of the noise level, and automatically adjusts the memory of its second-moment estimators to the observed optimization dynamics. Under standard lower boundedness, smoothness, unbiasedness, bounded-variance, and spectral-boundedness assumptions, we establish uniform stability and variation bounds for the time-varying block preconditioners and control their interaction with momentum estimation and parameter updates. These results yield the noise-adaptive stationarity guarantee $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(T^{-1/2}+\sigma^{1/2}T^{-1/4})$, which automatically reduces to the nearly deterministic $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(T^{-1/2})$ rate when the stochastic-gradient noise vanishes. NABLA therefore provides a principled approach to combining closed-loop trajectory feedback with memory-efficient structured matrix preconditioning.

papers.title: MSRGF: Multi-Source Reconstruction with Reference-Guided Fusion for Incomplete Multimodal Sentiment Analysis
papers.abstract: Incomplete multimodal sentiment analysis (MSA) predicts sentiment from textual, acoustic, and visual features when some observations are missing. Existing reconstruction methods estimate missing features from available modalities and combine the resulting information for sentiment prediction. However, different available modalities can produce distinct estimates of the same modality, while direct fusion often leaves the relationships among these estimates underused. We propose MSRGF (Multi-Source Reconstruction with Reference-Guided Fusion), which retains separate estimates and exploits their relationships during fusion. Specifically, MSRGF comprises three components: (1) Source-Wise Reconstruction (SWR), which uses modality-specific queries and a shared generator to produce a separate estimate of each modality from every available modality; (2) Reference-Guided Fusion (RGF), which uses relationships among estimates and available observations to construct a weighted reference, selectively refines it using their differences, and incorporates observed features when available; and (3) Global Context Modulation (GCM), which uses global context to adjust modality summaries for sentiment prediction. Extensive experiments on three datasets show that MSRGF outperforms existing methods, achieving average accuracy improvements of 1.9% on MOSEI under random within-modality missingness, 0.6% under random whole-modality missingness and 1.3% under fixed whole-modality missingness.

papers.title: GRAPE-Bench: When Vision Degrades, Does Video Reasoning Hold?
papers.abstract: Despite strong performance on standard benchmarks, video reasoning models remain vulnerable to visual degradation, raising concerns about their reliability in safety-critical scenarios. Existing benchmarks address this concern in part by simulating visual degradation or probing model reasoning with challenging questions, leaving open how well models handle naturally degraded video and whether they can make the simpler judgments that matter for safe driving. To this end, we introduce GRAPE-Bench, which jointly evaluates video reasoning across visual degradation conditions and question difficulty. It combines a synthetic set spanning twelve corruption types across daily-life and driving videos with real-world footage of driving at night or in rain, snow, or fog. Each video is paired with three progressively challenging questions, from fundamental judgments with potential safety implications to demanding reasoning stress tests. Across open-weight and frontier models, we observe ranking reversals between synthetic and real-world conditions and level-specific weaknesses obscured by overall accuracy. Synthetic-data fine-tuning improves Qwen3.5-9B's real-world accuracy from 76.7% to 81.1%, while clean-privileged on-policy distillation reaches 80.4% in a separate reasoning-enabled setting. Through preference steering, we further demonstrate continuous control over a frozen model's trade-off between safety-relevant judgments and challenging reasoning, with little change in overall accuracy. Together, GRAPE-Bench provides a unified testbed for evaluating, improving, and controlling video reasoning under degraded visual conditions.

papers.title: Prismatic construction of crystalline deformation rings up to p-power torsion
papers.abstract: We study the deformation of Galois representations which are etale realizations of finitely generated prismatic F-crystals and show the deformation functor is pro-represented by a complete Noetherian local ring whose Z_p-flat quotient coincides with Kisin's crystalline deformation ring. As a consequence, we obtain a universal prismatic F-crystal with coefficients in Kisin's crystalline deformation ring.

papers.title: Draft Calibration for Speculative Decoding: Accelerating LLM Serving by Matching Draft and Target Distributions
papers.abstract: Speculative decoding accelerates large language model (LLM) inference by employing a lightweight draft model to propose draft tokens and allowing the target model to verify the new tokens in parallel to improve inference-time compute utilization. The speedup relies on the acceptance probability of draft tokens in target verification, which is directly related to the gap $\|p-q\|_1$ between the target distribution $p$ and the draft distribution $q$. In this paper, we study draft calibration of speculative decoding to improve the speedup of speculative decoding, where we employ post-hoc methods to calibrate the draft distribution to mitigate the distribution gap. We observe that though current community open-source draft models may learn the top candidate token correctly, they are generally underconfident compared to the target model, suggesting a consistent distribution mismatch. To mitigate the effect of this mismatch on the acceptance rate of the draft models, we try various post-hoc calibration methods, including standard temperature scaling and token-wise calibration. Our results suggest that a standard temperature scaling applied to the draft distribution improves the acceptance length by up to approximately 10\% with almost no additional cost across different tasks. Throughput analysis further verifies that this improvement in serving efficiency. Analysis of more general calibration methods reveals further potential room for improvement.

papers.title: DiaCap: Jointly Learning Who Speaks When for Audiovisual Dialogue Captioning
papers.abstract: We present DiaCap, an audiovisual LLM for comprehensive dialogue captioning, which produces the transcript, timestamps, and a visual description of the speaker for every utterance in a video. Considering that utterance timing and audiovisual diarization are tightly coupled, DiaCap unifies the tasks in a single model, trained in two complementary stages. First, we train DiaCap on 225K curated clips, using synthetic captions that densely label every utterance in detail. Second, we further refine the model via reinforcement learning on 2.9K human-corrected clips, using fine-grained feedback that directly evaluates utterance timing, speaker grouping, and speaker binding. On DiaDemBench, which we extend with utterance-level timestamps and subtitle redaction, both DiaCap with off-the-shelf transcripts and its end-to-end variant DiaCap-E2E achieve strong results. Specifically, DiaCap performs on par with Gemini 4 Argon in audiovisual diarization while clearly outperforming it in timestamp accuracy (76.59 vs. 42.76 TIME). It also maintains strong diarization on multilingual and minute-long videos, and transfers to audiovisual question answering.

papers.title: Partial Self-Similar Fractal Interpolation Functions and Surfaces
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study a class of fractal interpolation functions with partial self-similarity. We first study fractal interpolation surfaces defined on rectangular domains, analyze the stability and sensitivity of the proposed construction to parameter perturbations. In addition, we investigate the partial $\alpha$-fractal function in both the univariate and bivariate cases, as well as the invariant measure in the univariate setting whose support is the graph of the fractal interpolation function. Further, under suitable additional conditions, we derive bounds for the box-counting dimension of the graph of the univariate PFIF. The results presented in this paper are backed up by illustrative examples.

papers.title: When Is Product Decoding of ECOC MAP-Consistent? Pair Structure and the n-vs-Rest Codes
papers.abstract: Error-Correcting Output Codes (ECOC) combine binary classifiers by the sum decoder, which totals probabilities, or the product decoder, which totals log-likelihoods. In the noiseless setting, where the binary classifiers output the true posteriors, we ask on which code matrices each decoder always agrees with the Bayes-optimal (MAP) class. For the sum decoder the answer is known: the code must be equidistant (James and Hastie, 1998). We answer the question for the product decoder. Two classes are compared through the votes of the columns on which they differ: the sum decoder decides by their sample mean, the product decoder by an M-estimator with influence function artanh, and each vote is the MAP margin plus a bias determined by the other classes alone. Our main theorem states that the product decoder is MAP-consistent if and only if, for every class pair, the columns on which the two classes differ are matched with the columns obtained by swapping the two classes (or their complements), and equivalently if and only if the code is a union of n-vs-Rest codes. Efficient equidistant codes are therefore excluded: Hadamard codes ($M\ge 8$), which meet the Plotkin bound with $M-1$ columns, have no such pairs, and for the Sylvester type the reversal margin can be at least a constant 0.0182 independent of $M$. All theorems are machine-checked in Lean 4. On six real datasets with estimated probabilities, the product decoder is slightly more accurate when each column is calibrated, and the sum decoder is better when the calibration error differs across columns; in either case the decoders disagree only near ties.

papers.title: The Reliability Function of Error-Correcting Output Codes with Noisy Binary Classifiers
papers.abstract: Error-correcting output coding (ECOC) builds a multi-class classifier from binary classifiers. We study the excess error rate of ECOC over the Bayes (MAP) classifier when each binary classifier outputs a posterior estimate whose log-odds is corrupted by Gaussian noise. Recasting decoding as a test over a Gaussian channel, we derive an upper bound from the union and Chernoff bounds and a lower bound from the nearest competing category and the Mills ratio. The bounds show that a large Hamming distance is both necessary and sufficient for reducing the excess error rate. The excess error rate stays bounded away from zero, by a constant that depends on the two largest posteriors and the noise level but not on the number of categories $M$, whenever the distance between the code words of the two most probable categories is bounded; for equidistant codes this distance is $d_{\min}$. Conversely, it is at most $M-1$ times a factor that is exponentially small in the minimum distance $d_{\min}$, and it vanishes whenever $\kappa\,d_{\min}-\ln(M-1)\to\infty$ for an explicit $\kappa$ (for general codes, under a posterior condition). For $n$-vs-rest codes with $n\geq2$, the upper and lower exponents coincide asymptotically, which determines the reliability function of ECOC in closed form. The results extend to correlated Gaussian noise with the Hamming distance replaced by an effective distance; when noise is shared at the level of categories, the effective distance stays bounded and the excess error rate does not vanish for any code. All theorems are machine-checked in Lean 4. In a semi-synthetic setting, the measured decay agrees with the predicted exponent. On ResNet-50 features of CIFAR-10/100 and ImageNet-1k, the excess error over a log-likelihood decoding reference decreases with $d_{\min}$ and, for larger $M$, levels off at a moderate distance, while codes with $d_{\min}=1$ degrade as $M$ grows.

papers.title: A steady-state genetic algorithm with multi-ratio seeding and pair exchange for the quadratic knapsack problem
papers.abstract: The quadratic knapsack problem (QKP) seeks a subset of items of maximum total linear and pairwise profit whose total weight does not exceed a given capacity. Most QKP heuristics rank items by a profit-to-weight ratio. We show on benchmark instances that this ranking can steer the search away from the best known solutions, and that on an almost full knapsack a local optimum can be separated from a better solution by an exchange where every single swap loses profit. We propose SSGA-P, a steady-state genetic algorithm with pair exchange that addresses both effects. Its initial population contains greedy solutions built with a grid of exponents between 0.5 and 3 applied to the item weights, and its pair exchange move combines an improving swap violating the capacity with a second swap or removal that restores feasibility. Incremental contribution vectors keep the method practical up to 10{,}000 items. SSGA-P finds optimal solutions in every run on the 100 classical instances and reaches all best known values in 99.8\% of the runs on the 80 instances with 1000 and 2000 items and in 99.75\% on the 40 instances with 5000 and 6000 items, significantly above the 87.7\% of the iterated hyperplane exploration algorithm, improving one best known value. On the 144 Large-QKP instances of Hochbaum et al. (2025), with the same 120-second limit, it improves 20 best known values and matches the other 124. An ablation study shows that the multi-ratio seeding and the pair exchange account for most of this performance.

papers.title: Vx: A Programming Language for Scalable, Maintainable and Secure Systems
papers.abstract: A program for a modern machine runs on several kinds of chips. Its memory spaces, links and capacities are invisible to the compilers of today. So a host that reads device memory, a working set that does not fit, or a data race shows up only when the program runs. Vx is a systems programming language that puts these facts in the program text. A machine is a source file of declarations. A value's type says which memory it lives in. Apart from one stated exception, a function's signature is the whole contract that its callers see. A flag lists the code and the facts that the compiler trusts without a proof. This report is a tour of the language at one commit. It describes six design principles, the core language, and the features that serve three qualities. Vx is scalable because one program text runs across machines, cores and GPU threads. With an option, the compiler also checks its function bodies in parallel. It is maintainable because a signature is the contract of a function and most diagnostics have codes. The output of the parallel compiler does not depend on the number of threads. It is secure because safe code has ownership, borrow, race and placement checks, and in safe code, a file or a socket of the standard library opens only with a right. For every feature, the report gives its status and the evidence for it. It also lists where the implementation does not yet meet the design.

papers.title: LookAnything: A Foundation Model for Holistic Gaze Following
papers.abstract: Human gaze provides a rich window into attention and intent, making its understanding essential for applications ranging from social signal analysis to human-robot interaction. Existing methods typically employ highly customized architectures relying on auxiliary inputs like head crops or depth maps, causing cascading errors and inference overhead. Trained on single domains and confined to isolated gaze following with heatmap outputs, they lack flexibility and generalization for diverse interactive scenarios. To bridge this gap, we present LookAnything, a foundation model that unifies diverse gaze-centric tasks for holistic gaze following. Benefiting from large-scale multi-task and cross-domain training, LookAnything flexibly adapts to various settings, generating diverse outputs (points, boxes, heatmaps, and language) and supporting broad gaze-centric localization, description, and reasoning. At its core, we introduce learnable gaze-prior queries to promote gaze-aware representation learning, eliminating the need for auxiliary external inputs. To facilitate this paradigm, we construct HoliGaze, a comprehensive corpus and benchmark comprising 311K question-answer pairs across 5 capability dimensions and 9 distinct tasks. Experiments demonstrate that LookAnything consistently outperforms 33 leading vision-language models on holistic gaze following, while remaining highly competitive with dedicated specialists across 5 conventional target detection benchmarks. Evaluation on unseen datasets and deployment on a real robot further validate its strong out-of-domain generalization and flexible adaptation in real-world scenarios.

papers.title: ROVO: Robust Rotation-Only Visual Odometry for UAVs at Low and Moderate Altitudes
papers.abstract: Image noise can confound rotation and translation estimates in monocular visual navigation for unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) at low and moderate altitudes, where even small perturbations may cause large errors in translation direction. Inspired by angular cues in long-range visual perception, we propose rotation-only visual odometry (ROVO) for monocular aerial imagery. ROVO estimates pairwise rotations from matched images, robustly averages them over overlapping windows, and aligns consecutive windows through shared frames. By retaining only orientation in the trajectory state, it prevents uncertain landmark depth from propagating to later estimates. In trajectory simulation, sliding-window ROVO achieved a mean orientation error just 10.7% as large as that of the conventional SLAM baseline. On real flight data, ROVO achieved rotation accuracy comparable to ORB-SLAM3 and DPVO under the original Bell412 settings. With a narrower FoV or at higher flight altitude, ROVO reduced relative rotation RMSE by 19.7--69.4% compared with the next-best method in each comparison. Code and simulation tools are available at https://github.com/sssxxxkkkk/ROVO.

papers.title: Constraints on Finsler cosmology from observational data
papers.abstract: We investigate current constraints and conditional detectability of Finslerian {\Lambda}CDM (F{\Lambda}CDM) cosmology using supernova, cosmic chronometer (CC), and baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) data. We adopt PantheonPlus SH0ES, CC and BAO data with a free acoustic scale. Supplementary tests with DES supernovae and PantheonPlus without SH0ES absolute calibra?tion verify result robustness. We compare F{\Lambda}CDM model against {\Lambda}CDM and wCDM and find that F{\Lambda}CDM improves the fit compared to {\Lambda}CDM, but the degree of fit is not superior to that of the wCDM model with the same number of parameters. We find that the background variations introduced by F{\Lambda}CDM can be absorbed to some extent by {\Lambda}CDM through adjusting its own parameters. We then use parametric bootstrap calibration and Monte Carlo power estimation to assess the detection power of residual background deviation that {\Lambda}CDM cannot absorb. We find no statistically significant ev?idence for a residual background deviation in the main data configuration. For an injection background fixed at the maximum likelihood estimate, the conditional detection power is relatively low. We examine the sensitivity of the detection power of this signal to the injected background. We find that the detection power of this deviation is significantly dependent on the injection context.

papers.title: Shuttle: Dependency-Attributed Workflow Evolution for Smart Contract Auditing
papers.abstract: In LLM-based smart contract auditing, detection quality depends on both model capability and workflow design. While coding agents can revise workflows from execution feedback, unconstrained rewrites rarely yield stable gains. Cross-function vulnerabilities require multi-step state tracking and boundary reasoning that coarse pipelines miss. End-to-end outcomes hide which step lost a clue, so direct rewrites regress existing hits or discard valid edits under coarse aggregate scoring. Repeatedly iterating on a small project set also adds case-specific heuristics that bloat prompts and hurt generalization. We present Shuttle, a constrained workflow-evolution system, and LucidScan, the auditing framework it evolves. Shuttle centers on provenance-graph attribution: it expands each run into an instance-level dependency graph, locates the node where a clue was lost via forward search, and traces existing hits backward into a protected set. After evaluating a merged batch, Shuttle drops dragging edits via a node-level provenance ledger, falling back to cache-reusing local re-runs only when early-round edits overlap on the same node. For localized bottlenecks, Shuttle generates edits under task decomposition, progressive refinement, and generality blind review. On 10 training projects, Shuttle evolves LucidScan from $G_0$ (28.7% per-project average C/H/M recall) to $G_8$ (82.1%). On 13 held-out validation projects under the same model, average recall rises from 28.6% ($G_0$) to 70.3% ($G_8$), above Pashov and Codex Security. In an anonymized live public audit contest with 896 researchers (Nov. 2026), the evolved scanner tied for #1 in High-severity recall (6/8, 75.0%), ranked #2 in scored H/M clusters (34/72, 47.2%) with 92.9% validity (78/84), and finished #3 overall.

papers.title: ActiveBridge: Scaling Active Prior for Robots through Egocentric Perception-Interaction Modeling
papers.abstract: Robotics foundation models are now widely used for manipulation, and egocentric videos offer rich data for scaling. However, existing methods overlook the human active priors captured in egocentric videos, which limits performance in unstructured scenes. They act on given observations instead of actively seeking information as humans do. We propose ActiveBridge, a training framework that learns these human active priors and transfers them to robots through world-action modeling. We design a robot that actively controls its viewpoint through head actions to acquire the visual information needed for manipulation using a single head camera, without wrist cameras. During human training, an instruction-conditioned model jointly predicts future egocentric videos and synchronized head-wrist action trajectories, with head actions providing explicit supervision for active perception. Experiments show that ActiveBridge outperforms baselines on active manipulation tasks, while ablations demonstrate the benefit of joint head-wrist action supervision.

papers.title: CoverMem: Coverage-Constrained Visual Memory for Budgeted Embodied Question Answering
papers.abstract: Episodic-memory embodied question answering enables agents to answer questions based on previously recorded visual observations of the surrounding scenes. However, growing observation histories, varying observation quality across viewpoints, and limited computational resources make it challenging to construct and maintain compact visual memories while retrieving sufficient evidence for question answering. To address these challenges, we introduce CoverMem, which incorporates three key components: (1) a coverage-constrained memory construction method that selects a compact set of informative full frames satisfying object-quality and representative-scene coverage requirements; (2) a coverage-preserving incremental maintenance strategy that locally reselects only the affected frames to satisfy updated coverage requirements as observations arrive; and (3) a budgeted complementary frame selection method that balances question relevance, additional support for question requirements, and redundancy with selected frames within a fixed budget. Experimental results on three benchmarks covering diverse environments and question types demonstrate that CoverMem improves question-answering performance under limited visual budgets.

papers.title: Spanning cyclability of split graphs
papers.abstract: For a positive integer $k$, a graph $G$ is called $k$-spanning cyclable (resp. $k$-edge spanning cyclable) if, given any $k$ distinct vertices $v_1, v_2, \ldots, v_k$ (resp. $k$ independent edges $e_1, e_2, \ldots, e_k$) of $G$, there exist $k$ vertex-disjoint cycles $C_1, C_2, \ldots, C_k$ in $G$ such that $v_i \in V(C_i)$ (resp. $e_i \in E(C_i)$) for each $i$ and $V(C_1) \cup \cdots \cup V(C_k) = V(G)$. In particular, the notion of 1-spanning cyclable coincides with the existence of a Hamiltonian cycle, and a Hamilton-connected graph is necessarily 1-edge spanning cyclable. For a positive integer $r \ge 3$, a graph $G$ is $K_{1,r}$-free if $G$ does not have an induced subgraph isomorphic to $K_{1,r}$, and $K_{1,4} + e$ denotes the graph obtained by adding an edge $e$ between two nonadjacent vertices of $K_{1,4}$. There are several interesting conjectures and sparse results relative to these conjectures on Hamiltonian properties of $K_{1,r}$-free split graphs, whose vertex set can be partitioned into a maximum clique $W$ and an independent set $J$. In this paper, we extend some of these results by proving the following: (1) every $(k+1)$-connected $K_{1,3}$-free split graph of order at least $4k-1$ is $k$-spanning cyclable for $k \ge 1$; in particular, every 2-connected $K_{1,3}$-free split graph of order at least 3 is Hamiltonian; (2) every $2k$-connected $K_{1,3}$-free split graph is $k$-edge spanning cyclable for $k \ge 2$; (3) every $(k+1)$-connected $\{K_{1,4}, K_{1,4}+e\}$-free split graph with $|W| \ge |J| \ge 3k+5$ is $k$-spanning cyclable for $k \ge 1$; in particular, every 2-connected $\{K_{1,4}, K_{1,4}+e\}$-free split graph with $|W| \ge |J| \ge 8$ is Hamiltonian; (4) every $2k$-connected $\{K_{1,4}, K_{1,4}+e\}$-free split graph with order at least $4k+9$ is $k$-edge spanning cyclable for $k \ge 2$.

papers.title: EEG-World: Context-Conditioned Dynamics of the Watching Brain
papers.abstract: Brain encoding models predict neural responses from audiovisual input, but typically overlook how ongoing brain activity shapes an individual's response. We introduce EEG-World, a recurrent world model that forecasts 10 seconds of EEG band-power dynamics from 6 seconds of preceding EEG and the subsequent audiovisual stimulus. Pretrained on continuous EEG, EEG-World learns shared neural dynamics and adapts to unseen individuals through lightweight subject-specific readouts. Using 2,584 hours of EEG from 78 participants, we show that nonlinear recurrent forecasting surpasses strong history-aware linear baselines at scale. EEG-World achieves a forecasting correlation of 0.261 versus 0.233 for the strongest history-and-video linear model, with a 3.3-second forecasting-horizon advantage. Its learned dynamics transfer to unseen participants, outperforming the linear baseline in 23 of 24 individuals after calibration. While ongoing EEG history accounts for most predictive performance, controlled stimulus analyses reveal an additional video-dependent component. This component also enables evaluation of visual representations, with V-JEPA 2 improving clip-locked prediction by 35% over combined CLIP and DINOv2 features. Our results demonstrate the value of transferable neural dynamics for individual EEG forecasting and highlight the importance of separating state-driven from stimulus-driven predictability.

papers.title: Verified two-sided bounds for the inf-sup constant of the divergence on planar polygons
papers.abstract: The inf-sup constant $\beta(\Omega)$ of the divergence governs the stability of the Stokes problem. For polygons, analytic lower bounds are far from the true value, and numerical methods either bound $\beta$ from above or require spectral-gap and mesh-fineness hypotheses that cannot presently be checked. We propose a method that produces verified lower bounds without any such hypothesis. It rests on the Friedrichs formulation of $\beta$ in the Bergman space and on a multiplier identity that controls the non-compact corner contribution pointwise, with the sharp corner constant; the remaining compact part is bounded by a finite matrix inequality that is checked in exact and ball arithmetic. We prove that the bounds converge to $\beta$. Together with enclosed Rayleigh quotients of explicit trial functions (and, for the square, the bottom $\frac12-\frac1\pi$ of the essential spectrum) this yields two-sided enclosures, e.g.\ $0.426245\le\beta\le0.426252$ for the square and $0.303973\le\beta\le0.304078$ for the L-shaped domain. For a square with a square hole, which is neither simply connected nor star-shaped, we obtain $0.154596\le\beta\le0.154781$. For the rectangles $(0,1)\times(0,r)$ we enclose $\beta$ for eight aspect ratios and prove for the five ratios $r\in\{\frac14,\frac38,\frac12,\frac9{16},\frac58\}$ that $\beta^2$ is an isolated eigenvalue below the essential spectrum; the last two lie beyond the range covered by the explicit bound of Costabel, Crouzeix, Dauge and Lafranche. As an application, the certified values give guaranteed a posteriori bounds for Taylor--Hood approximations of the Stokes equations, including the doubly connected domain, for which, to our knowledge, no explicit lower bound for $\beta$ had been available.

papers.title: Continuum model for disconnection structures of hetero-interfaces
papers.abstract: Hetero-interfaces, as planar defects between dissimilar materials, accommodate the lattice misfit through networks of line defects of disconnections (a combination of structural ledges/step and dislocation characters). We develop a continuum model that predicts the hetero-interface structures, including disconnection networks, the interface inclination and misorientation angles. The model is based on the interfacial energy minimization with respect to all possible disconnection modes, subject to the interface structure constraint of the generalized Frank-Bilby equation that describes the lattice correspondence across the interface including both dislocation and step characters of disconnections and the inclination and misorientation angles. Numerical simulations are performed to determine the equilibrium configurations of three different types of hetero-interfaces: the $\alpha$/$\beta$ (orthorhombic/monoclinic) interface in ZrO$_2$, $\alpha$/$\beta$ hetero-interfaces in Ti and Au/Pd (001) twist-misfit interfaces. Comparisons with experiments, atomistic simulations and theoretical predictions show that our continuum model provides excellent predictions of the hetero-interface structures including disconnection networks and inclination, misorientation angles. Furthermore, systematic analysis reveals the functional dependence of hetero-interface structural properties on inclination and misorientation angles.

authors.name: Dongsong Tao
authors.institution: Jiangsu University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Sample-Efficient In-Context Adaptation via Sleep
papers.abstract: The ability to learn and generalize from limited experience, or sample efficiency, is a cornerstone of intelligence. How can we build language models that turn a few user interactions, a few snippets of unfamiliar code, or a handful of experimental results provided in context into knowledge that generalizes? Prior work has found that sleep, a process where the model performs $N$ recurrent forward passes to refine its representations of a chunk of context, can improve long-context reasoning (specifically, within SSM-attention hybrid models). We study whether this method also improves in-context adaptation on general, non-synthetic tasks for transformer language models. To this end, we pre-train language models up to 1.2B-parameters on up to 100B tokens with sleep mechanisms. Notably, longer sleep (i.e., using a larger number of recurrent forward passes $N$) enables the model to learn faster in-context on multiple few-shot algorithmic, question-answering tasks, while also achieving lower next-token prediction loss on out-of-distribution evaluations.
