papers.title: SGD with Large Learning Rates: General Analysis & Improved Rates
papers.abstract: Stochastic Gradient Descent lies at the core of modern machine learning. However its classical analysis typically restricts the stepsize to be below a curvature-dependent stability threshold. Recent developments in deterministic optimization have challenged this paradigm, showing that suitably chosen large stepsizes can not only preserve convergence, but also accelerate Gradient Descent (GD). Whether this phenomenon persists in the presence of stochastic gradient noise has remained an open question (Wu et al., 2024). In this work, we answer this question affirmatively for the cross-entropy loss with linear predictors and two-layer neural networks, establishing an accelerated $\mathcal{O}(T^{-2})$ convergence rate. At the core of our analysis is a fine-grained characterization of the stochastic large-stepsize dynamics. This sharper control of the trajectory further yields tight convergence guarantees within the stable regime, improving existing bounds even in the deterministic setting. Taken together, our results show that the acceleration mechanism induced by large stepsizes survives stochasticity and extends beyond linear models. Numerical experiments demonstrate the benefits of large learning rates in practice.

papers.title: Analytic properties of Boolean-Narayana numbers
papers.abstract: Very recently, B\'ona introduced the Boolean-Narayana numbers BoNa(n,k) as the number of 0-1-trees on n+1 vertices with k right edges. We prove the total positivity of the Boolean-Narayana triangle by providing an explicit matrix factorization, and construct a planar digraph for this triangle. We give two combinatorial interpretations of the gamma-coefficients of the Boolean-Narayana polynomials. We also show the strong q-log-convexity of the Boolean-Narayana polynomials and the asymptotic normality of the Boolean-Narayana numbers. A bijection between 0-1-trees and colored Motzkin paths is constructed, presenting an alternative interpretation of the Boolean-Narayana numbers.

papers.title: Quantization-Induced Performance Degradation in Segment Routing: A Concentration Inequality Analysis
papers.abstract: In segment routing (SR), splitting ratios must be quantized to respect practical hardware precision constraints. Yet no existing work has established an upper bound on the performance degradation caused by such quantization. In this work, we propose source-agnostic systematic rounding, which allows flows sharing a destination to share the same policy, thereby reducing memory consumption, and which approximates the target splitting ratios by a set of power-of-two terms so as to respect the hardware precision limit. We explicitly analyze the consequence of quantizing splitting ratios to integer multiples of 1/64 by a probability-theoretic argument based on concentration inequalities, and we derive an upper bound on the resulting performance degradation. We validate our analysis with extensive experiments on real-world network topologies and flow statistics.

authors.name: Kai Wang
authors.institution: Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania

papers.title: Leveraging Persistent Field-of-View and Multipath Segment Routing for Traffic Engineering in LEO Satellite Constellations
papers.abstract: The emergence of low earth orbit (LEO) satellite constellations poses fundamental challenges for traditional rout- ing paradigms due to high node mobility, frequent topology changes, and constrained on-board resources. This paper pro- poses a segment routing (SR) framework that offloads route computation and control signaling from resource-constrained LEO switches to more powerful medium earth orbit (MEO) con- trollers. We first establish sufficient conditions for the persistence of user-to-satellite and LEO-to-MEO field-of-view (FoV) con- nectivity throughout a virtual topology (VT) snapshot interval, enabling handover-free operation. Leveraging this persistence, we formulate the MEO control domain partitioning problem as a mixed-integer linear program (MILP) to minimize control over- head while assigning disjoint segment routing domains (SRDs) to MEO controllers. Within each SRD, we develop a multipath SR- based traffic engineering (SR-TE) formulation that splits traffic among four minimum-hop-count path types to minimize maxi- mum link utilization. We solve this linear program (LP) using a distributed primal-dual hybrid gradient (PDHG) approach that preserves SRD-level privacy and requires only AllReduce communication. Simulations on the Starlink/GPS combination demonstrate our approach reduces maximum link utilization by more than 13.09%, 11.84%, and 12.50%, respectively, com- pared to traditional minimum hop count routing (MHCR) and traffic-oblivious load-balancing methods for Starlink, Kuiper, and OneWeb.

authors.name: Kai Wang
authors.institution: Hospital of the University of Pennsylvania

papers.title: Irrationality and differential equations: the work of Calegari, Dimitrov, and Tang
papers.abstract: Beautiful recent work of Calegari, Dimitrov, and Tang has given new methods for proving irrationality of certain arithmetically interesting constants, notably $L(2, \chi_{-3})$, building on ideas of Siegel, Andr\'e, Bost-Charles, and others. This note is meant to explain some of this work for the 2027 JMM Current Events Bulletin, and to situate it in context of some results and conjectures in arithmetic and algebraic geometry.

papers.title: Probabilistic index models for hierarchical survival outcomes
papers.abstract: In clinical trials, prioritized composite outcomes allow treatment comparisons to reflect the clinical importance of fatal and nonfatal events. Probabilistic index models relate these comparisons to covariates, but censoring can leave a comparison unresolved. We develop three weighted estimating equations at a prespecified restriction time, with logit, probit, and identity links. Complete history weighting requires both restricted histories to be observed. Resolved comparison weighting also retains comparisons determined before both histories are complete. Conditional tie weighting further uses an observed lower-priority event when higher-priority ties remain uncertain, weighting its regression residual by their conditional probability under a joint model of observed event histories. The construction accommodates a fixed number of nonfatal components and parametric or semiparametric joint models. Under their respective nuisance-model assumptions, the three equations target the same full data regression parameter. We establish consistency and asymptotic normality and derive sandwich estimators accounting for overlapping pairs and nuisance estimation. Across 27 simulation configurations, conditional tie weighting had smaller empirical variance than the other two methods, with reductions ranging from 5.1 to 59.0 percent relative to resolved comparison weighting. An HF-ACTION analysis of death and first hospitalization illustrates the additional observed information used by conditional tie weighting. Conditional tie weighting yielded smaller estimated variances, and the treatment effect intervals from all three methods included zero.

authors.name: Xi Fang
authors.institution: Central South University of Forestry and Technology

papers.title: A Calculus for Borrowability
papers.abstract: Borrowing grants temporary shared or exclusive access to a linear resource without transferring ownership. However, capturing borrowing in a type system poses two challenges: a lender, the reference a borrow was taken from, should remain a first-class value that can be moved, and regain its permission when a non-lexical borrow ends. We propose borrowability, an index on reference types that tracks how access permissions are lent across lifetimes while separating them from the owner's obligation to release the resource. A lender is then an ordinary value whose borrowability records its remaining access permissions and the lifetimes of its active borrows, recovering borrowed permissions in place when those lifetimes end. We formalize borrowability in the calculus $\lambda^{bo\rho}$, mechanize its semantic type soundness and memory safety proofs in Rocq using Iris, and show that our design rules out all 24 in-scope soundness issues reported against the Rust compiler.

papers.title: PORTA: Systematic Discovery of Vulnerabilities in Identity Brokers
papers.abstract: Identity brokers such as Keycloak, Vault, and Dex translate authentication proofs from an upstream identity provider into sessions for downstream services. Due to their central role in authentication and trust mediation, a single vulnerability in a broker compromises every downstream service behind it. In fact, recent incidents have demonstrated that even widely adopted platforms are not immune to such issues, highlighting the critical need for systematic analysis. To build such an analysis, this work first defines invariants for broker operation. These invariants are not completely covered by existing authentication specifications, primarily because brokers are unique in their duality, i.e., acting simultaneously as a relying party and an identity provider. The invariants capture the properties that identity brokers must uphold throughout their workflows, as all 60 previous CVEs we consider violate at least one invariant. Within these workflows, we further define high-level action categories. Equipped with this information, our automated tool PORTA leverages a large language model (LLM) to generate API invocation sequences corresponding to the high-level action categories, and oracle assertions aligned with the specified invariants. PORTA identifies 33 previously unreported security vulnerabilities in seven popular open-source brokers. We study these novel vulnerabilities and trace them to eight recurring patterns. We responsibly disclosed all discovered vulnerabilities: 29 have been confirmed, 14 patched, and 19 assigned CVE numbers, with 10 CVEs rated as critical.

papers.title: Lost on Campus: Evaluating Embodied Spatial Reasoning of Vision-Language Models in the Wild
papers.abstract: Embodied Spatial Reasoning (ESR) is central to deploying Vision-Language Models (VLMs) in real-world embodied tasks, yet remains inadequately evaluated. Existing benchmarks primarily assess spatial reasoning in static images or synthetic indoor environments, where semantic shortcuts often suffice, making it difficult to faithfully evaluate spatial reasoning capabilities in the wild. In light of this, we present Lost on Campus, a benchmark for evaluating ESR in large-scale real-world outdoor 3D environments reconstructed by 3D Gaussian Splatting. Our benchmark introduces a unified reasoning-action evaluation framework that seamlessly integrates diagnostic QA for isolated reasoning with closed-loop interactive navigation for active reasoning under multimodal instructions. To enable fine-grained diagnosis, we evaluate six capability aspects of ESR: action grounding, spatial foresight, metric awareness, goal-directed planning, ego-allocentric localization, and spatio-temporal consistency. Extensive experiments reveal that: (i) Compared to indoor settings, real-world outdoor environments impose substantially higher demands on spatial reasoning, where existing models exhibit poor performance; (ii) VLMs still struggle with fine-grained visual alignment, with failures in spatial foresight and ego-allocentric localization emerging as primary bottlenecks; (iii) Improving multimodal interaction capabilities and long-term spatial reasoning is crucial for advancing embodied intelligence. These findings highlight that faithful evaluation of ESR demands benchmarks tightly coupling perception, reasoning and action within realistic and continuous environments.

authors.name: Yutao Tang
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: AdProducer: Towards Agentic Advertising Video Generation
papers.abstract: Recent advances in video generation have made automated advertising production increasingly feasible. However, an effective advertisement must faithfully represent the product and communicate its selling points through compelling visual storytelling, which requires more than visual synthesis: it calls for deeper product understanding and strategic decisions about how to present product value. Crucially, product research and creative design are closely intertwined, as the information gathered about a product determines which features can be faithfully demonstrated and how they should be presented. In this paper, we introduce AdProducer, the first end-to-end agentic framework for advertising video creation, transforming concise creative briefs into finished advertisements. Our multimodal agent autonomously researches products through web and image search and translates its findings into selling-point-driven storyboards that guide a frozen video generator. To achieve this, we develop a dedicated data construction pipeline that yields two training datasets, AdProducer-SFT and AdProducer-RL, and train the agent through supervised fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning with joint optimization of storyboard- and video-level rewards. We further introduce AdCreation-Bench, comprising 305 advertising briefs across eight domains, with two complementary metrics: PG-Score for product correctness and creative execution, and Ad-Score for overall advertising effectiveness assessed by an independent judge. Experiments demonstrate that AdProducer improves the PG-Score of MiniMax H3 from 17.3 to 51.3 and generalizes to Veo 3.1 without additional training, improving its score from 28.0 to 35.9, with consistent gains in Ad-Score, VideoScore2, and human evaluations. Code, models, and data are released.

authors.name: Chaoyang Wang
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

papers.title: See the Answer, Learn to Embed: Learning Universal Multimodal Embeddings from Hindsight
papers.abstract: Universal Multimodal Embedding (UME) models map heterogeneous multimodal inputs into a shared embedding space, where pairwise similarity supports diverse downstream tasks. Recent reasoning-driven UME approaches use intermediate reasoning to generate additional context for embedding, but often incur extra computation at inference. In this paper, we explore the matched candidate (i.e., the paired target) as an alternative source of context, asking whether a model can "see the answer" during training and "learn to embed" without it at inference. However, direct conditioning on this privileged context can introduce candidate-specific information unavailable from the query alone or cause the candidate-conditioned query representation to collapse toward the candidate embedding. To address this, we introduce Hindsight-Enhanced Multimodal Embeddings (HEME), which learns query-grounded hindsight representations from such candidate context. HEME first trains a hindsight teacher with a hindsight attention mask, mismatched-candidate conditioning, and query-token alignment to limit excessive reliance on the candidate. It then freezes the teacher and distills its hindsight representation and similarity distribution into a standalone student embedder. At inference, the student independently encodes queries and candidates without candidate conditioning or the hindsight teacher. Experiments on MMEB-V2 and the agent and text tasks of MMEB-V3 demonstrate the effectiveness of HEME and show that it enables more efficient inference than explicit reasoning-driven methods.

authors.name: Yoonki Cho
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

authors.name: Taegeun Yang
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

authors.name: Jinhwan Seo
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Residual Guidance for Real-Time Interactive Video Generation
papers.abstract: Real-time interactive video generation allows users to change the prompt during generation to steer the evolving video. However, existing streaming models, which generate videos chunk by chunk, often keep following the previous prompt after a switch. We trace this failure to context inertia, where the previous chunk acts as a strong prior that suppresses the new prompt. Furthermore, we find that this inertia persists even when the cache retains only the previous chunk, yet discarding the context breaks visual continuity, which limits approaches that edit the cache. Rather than editing the cache, we propose Residual Guidance (RG), a simple, training-free method that counteracts context inertia with a correction measured outside the cache. Specifically, RG denoises the re-noised previous chunk once under the new prompt without the cache and adds the resulting residual to the early denoising steps of the next chunk, where its content is largely decided and the new prompt is most suppressed. Across settings ranging from a single switch to long multi-switch generation, RG substantially improves prompt switching capability on existing streaming models, including those with dedicated switching mechanisms, while largely retaining visual quality. As it requires no training or per-model tuning and adds only one forward pass per chunk, RG can be easily integrated into existing real-time video generation pipelines.

authors.name: Kyeong-Hwan Moon
authors.institution: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology

papers.title: Tempering and few-shot calibration of pathology foundation models improve digital biomarker reproducibility across slide scanners
papers.abstract: Pathology foundation models underpin a growing number of histology-based cancer biomarkers, but sensitivity to slide scanner-specific image signatures degrades cross-center reliability and reproducibility. We developed a foundation model fine-tuning method that improved consistency in head-and-neck cancer human papillomavirus (HPV) prediction, colorectal cancer microsatellite instability (MSI) identification, prostate cancer grading and breast cancer phenotyping. This tempering method decreased cross-scanner prediction differences by 67.5% for HPV (95% CI 59.0-73.9%), 69.3% for MSI (95% CI 51.9-76.5%) and 63.4%-81.2% for breast signatures. Cross-scanner prostate grade agreement rose from 42.5% to 92.7%. Under full scanner-HPV confounding during training, AUROC fell from 0.80 to 0.68 with original model features but only from 0.86 to 0.84 with tempering. Unlike post hoc feature calibration, tempering used only public data yet matched or exceeded on-site calibration. These findings support tempering to reduce scanner dependence of pathology foundation models.

authors.name: Alexander T Pearson
authors.institution: University of Chicago Medicine Comprehensive Cancer Center

papers.title: Gaps between zeros of Epstein zeta-functions of binary quadratic forms on the critical line
papers.abstract: We prove that for every integral binary quadratic form $Q$ whose discriminant is, up to sign, not a perfect square, the Epstein zeta-function of $Q$ has a zero $\frac12+i\gamma$ with $|\gamma-T|\le T^{2/5+\epsilon}$ for all large $T$. For indefinite $Q$, that is, for zeta-functions of ideal classes of real quadratic orders, this is the first exponent below the classical barrier $1/2$. For positive definite $Q$ it improves the exponents $5/11$ of Jutila and Srinivas and $3/7$ of the authors, and for discriminant $-4m^2$ with $m$ odd we obtain $1/3$. A main ingredient, of independent interest, is an explicit Voronoi summation formula with additive twists to every modulus for the representation numbers of an indefinite binary form. The resulting dual sums are treated by a two-dimensional Weyl differencing, controlled by an exact formula for the Hessian determinant of the differenced phase.

authors.name: Srinivas Kotyada
authors.institution: Indian Institute of Science Education and Research, Tirupati

papers.title: Reliability of Language-Model Judges for Quantitative Scientific Question Answering: Evidence from Perovskite Photovoltaics
papers.abstract: Evaluating retrieval-augmented language models increasingly relies on automated model judges, yet their reliability on quantitative scientific synthesis remains largely unmeasured. Here, we evaluate automated grading on a quantitative benchmark for perovskite photovoltaics, where all 755 ground-truth answers are deterministically computed from 45,441 experimental device records. We evaluate a frontier judge (Claude Opus 5.5) alongside two local open-weight judges (Qwen3-14B and Qwen3-8B) across 4,530 free-text answers from six retrieval architectures under three regimes: reference-augmented (with the computed key), evidence-augmented (with retrieved passages and query logs), and unassisted (question and answer alone). Equipped with the reference key, Claude Opus reproduces ground truth near-perfectly (Cohen's $\kappa = 0.982 \pm 0.003$) and preserves exact architectural rankings ($\tau = 1.00$). Withholding the reference causes evaluation fidelity to collapse: frontier agreement drops to $\kappa = 0.557 \pm 0.022$, and providing retrieved literature passages yields virtually no improvement ($\kappa = 0.576 \pm 0.024$). Without reference keys, local judges degrade to near-random agreement ($\kappa = 0.087$ and $0.112$), inverting the leaderboard to rank a hallucinating closed-book baseline first ($\tau \le 0.20$). Furthermore, SQL-augmented generations induce severe evaluative blind spots: absent a reference, the frontier judge accepts 46.6% of erroneous SQL answers, overestimating architecture accuracy as 66.4% against its true 52.6%. These findings demonstrate that model-based evaluation in the physical sciences cannot rely on unstructured text inspection; rigorous benchmarking requires reference ground truth precomputed from structured measurement records.

papers.title: EvoMisty: Building, Optimizing, and Evolving Capabilities on a Social Robot
papers.abstract: Social robots face diverse and changing tasks in companionship and education. LLM-based methods can generate task programs, but they still rely on manually developed control interfaces and predefined capabilities. They also lack a general mechanism to optimize completed tasks based on user-specified metrics and reuse performance improvements across tasks.We present EvoMisty, a plugin-based framework that enables coding agents to build and continually improve robot capabilities. EvoMisty builds a control program from official documentation and verifies candidate capabilities on a physical robot. Verified capabilities are stored in an atomic capability library and combined with existing skills to solve tasks. After task completion, EvoMisty can collect execution data, measure user-specified metrics, and iteratively improve task programs. It then distills reusable skills from final solutions into a skill library for future tasks.We evaluate EvoMisty on a physical Misty II robot using Claude Code and Codex. The two agents construct 109 and 107 verified atomic capabilities, respectively. Both complete all 28 AutoMisty benchmark tasks and seven additional tasks beyond AutoMisty's capabilities. Optimization improves all seven evaluated metrics across five tasks. For example, dialogue response latency decreases by 52% and 71%, respectively. Reusing skills from one optimized dialogue task reduces latency by 33% to 72% in three other dialogue tasks without further optimization. All code and experimental videos will be publicly released through the webpage: https://wangxiaoshawn.github.io/projects/evomisty/index.html

papers.title: Electrical Degradation of Vertical $\beta$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ Schottky Barrier Diodes Under Au-Ion Irradiation to a Fluence of $1.3 \times 10^7$ cm$^{-2}$
papers.abstract: The electrical degradation and time-dependent current behavior of vertical $\beta$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ Schottky barrier diodes (SBDs) subjected to energetic Au-ion irradiation were systematically investigated. Two successive irradiation exposures were conducted under a constant reverse bias of $-100$ V to evaluate the effects of heavy-ion irradiation on device performance and transient current response. Following irradiation, the devices exhibited degraded forward conduction, increased specific on-resistance, enhanced reverse leakage current, and reduced apparent carrier concentration. During irradiation, pronounced increases in leakage current and transient current spikes were observed. Following each beam termination, the leakage current exhibited an initial rapid decay followed by a slower relaxation process. Single-exponential fitting identified distinct fast and slow relaxation components, while a double-exponential model provided a more comprehensive description of the overall current decay. After the second irradiation exposure, the characteristic time constants of the fast and slow relaxation processes increased from 33.50 to 40.64 s and from 190.35 to 282.29 s, respectively, indicating prolonged recovery dynamics under repeated irradiation. A charge-trapping-based model is proposed to explain the irradiation-induced current enhancement and subsequent fast and slow relaxation processes through modulation and gradual recovery of the effective Schottky tunneling barrier. These findings provide insights into the relationship between heavy-ion-induced electrical degradation and time-dependent current relaxation in $\beta$-Ga$_2$O$_3$ SBDs.

papers.title: GUI-WEdit and GUI-SkillEvo: Gradient-Free Adaptation of Small GUI Agents
papers.abstract: Small graphical user interface (GUI) agents can execute desktop workflows, but repeated local errors and fragile procedural decisions limit their reliability. We present GUI-WEdit-4B and GUI-SkillEvo-2B, two gradient-free adaptations of GUI-Owl-1.5 backbones. For the 4B model, we use trajectory feedback to construct guarded, closed-form updates to a late multilayer perceptron (MLP), retaining successful states as protection constraints. The final checkpoint changes 23,739,095 parameter values, or 0.535\% of the 4,437,815,808-parameter backbone, within one weight tensor. For the 2B model, an assistant iteratively proposes and refines procedural skills while the model weights remain fixed. On the 361-task OSWorld subset excluding Google Drive tasks, the frozen systems obtain final aggregate scores of 48.02\% and 45.47\%, respectively.

papers.title: Score-Based Diffusion for Hypergraph Signals in the t-Spectral Domain
papers.abstract: We introduce the first score-based generative model for signals on a fixed hypergraph, formulated in the spectral domain of t-product hypergraph signal processing (t-HGSP). The naive tensor heat semigroup is ill-posed, since after palindromic symmetrization the spectral slices of the Laplacian tensor are no longer positive semidefinite. A per-mode frequency shift repairs it, yielding a forward Ornstein-Uhlenbeck diffusion that decouples per (eigenmode, slice) pair with closed-form marginals, exact score targets, and an exactly isotropic stationary law. A lightweight slice-conditioned denoiser is trained on the resulting real spectral grid. Sampling combines its score on data-active modes with the closed-form score elsewhere, which proves essential for stability at scale. A closed cosine-form observation operator turns missing-node recovery into linear-Gaussian guidance with stabilized posterior sampling. On hypergraphs of up to 500 nodes, our model beats a clique-expansion baseline by margins growing from $2\times$ to $27\times$ in covariance error, matches the graph-spectral statistics of the data better than the graph-basis model itself, and reaches the finite-sample estimation floor on data rotated off the t-spectral axes. Posterior sampling reduces missing-node NMSE to 0.28-0.64 (classical baselines 0.87-1.1) at conservative coverage, and cuts the framework's own denoising baseline by up to $3.6\times$.

papers.title: Off-axis performance characterization of hard X-ray optics for the FOXSI-4 and FOXSI-5 sounding rocket missions
papers.abstract: FOXSI-4 and FOXSI-5 are Japan--U.S. joint sounding rocket missions investigating particle acceleration and plasma heating in solar flares. We developed soft and hard X-ray optics for both missions and characterized the off-axis response of the hard X-ray optics. Imaging performance was measured at SPring-8 BL29XUL, and effective areas at NASA/GSFC. With increasing off-axis angle, focused images became elongated and the large-angle component of the point spread function increased. The Half Power Diameter (HPD) remained below 20 arcsec up to 7.5 arcmin, increasing to approximately 50 arcsec at 15 arcmin. A Wolter-I optics model reproduced the off-axis HPD dependence within approximately 20%, with residuals likely associated with azimuthal variations in mirror figure errors. On-axis effective areas were 41.3 +/- 1.9 mm^2 at 6.4 keV and 32.3 +/- 1.6 mm^2 at 10 keV, decreasing by 20% and 30%, respectively, at 5 arcmin. Incorporating an empirical correction for geometric effects and X-ray reflectivity reproduced measured effective areas within 20% over 1.0--12.5 keV up to 5 arcmin. At larger off-axis angles, deviations at lower energies suggest increasing stray-light contributions. These measurements provide off-axis response data for constructing response functions for FOXSI-4 and FOXSI-5 analyses.

papers.title: Exact Collision Gradients for Ellipsoids in Differentiable Simulation
papers.abstract: Differentiable simulation enables gradient-based optimization in learning and control problems involving collisions, but its gradients are least reliable at the moment of impact, when the velocities jump. A fixed-step simulator detects a collision only after the bodies overlap, and some differentiable simulators correct for this with a linear estimate of the time of impact. In this paper, we study impacts between ellipsoids. We show that the gradient error of this estimate grows with the obliqueness of the collision, the curvature at contact, and the time step, and that ignoring spin adds a further error. Subsequently, we find the time of impact with continuous collision detection on the Perram Wertheim contact function and differentiate through the touching condition rather than the search. This gives exact gradients at any step size. We demonstrate our method on an optimal control problem and a system identification problem. In both, exact gradients recover the optimal control and the true parameters, while the linear estimate does not, even when it accounts for spin.

papers.title: Delegent: A Multi-Agent Harness That Reduces Cost without Sacrificing Performance
papers.abstract: Agents built on frontier language models are expensive. At every step, the frontier model re-reads its entire context and executes every subtask regardless of its difficulty. This paper explores the simple thesis that much of this cost can be removed by delegating easy subtasks to a small language model, or SLM, that runs on hardware one already owns. To test it, we build Delegent, a simple and effective agent harness built on Claude Code, in which the frontier model stays in charge of every task but hands focused subtasks, such as investigating code, running tests, and searching a corpus, to SLM subagents. Existing approaches such as cascades and model routers usually choose which model executes the entire task, whereas in Delegent, the frontier model always leads the execution and delegates easy subtasks to the SLM. No router or model is trained, so either model can be swapped freely. With the help of a 27B FP8 SLM, Delegent reduces the frontier cost of long-horizon coding by 67% and of agentic search by 59%, with no loss in task performance, and even a 2B SLM that fits on a laptop reduces the coding cost by 66%. The savings grow with the legwork that the frontier model would otherwise do itself, and a short instruction, which leaves the main coding tasks to the frontier model, accounts for most of the saving and keeps the 2B SLM from losing tasks. Code: https://github.com/castorini/delegent

papers.title: Transferable, Time-Parallel Graph Dynamics via Space-Time Factorization
papers.abstract: Time-parallel neural operators (FNO and successors) have transformed PDE surrogates on regular grids. Mesh-based operators (MeshGraphNets, Transolver) extend operator learning to irregular geometries, but jointly learning across diverse topologies while retaining non-recurrent temporal evaluation remains challenging. We propose space-time factorization: partition the model into local temporal operators (learned, graph-independent) and a spatial mixer that propagates information across nodes without graph-dependent learned parameters. This structural condition lets the same parameters run on unseen graphs; non-recurrent instances also admit time-parallel evaluation. Accurate zero-shot transfer further depends on controlling three information leaks (graph-dependent weights, graph-specific features, and graph-correlated training distributions) and on suitable task physics and training coverage. The protocol applies to two distinct spatial-mixer families, fixed-spectral and learned-attention. We validate the principle in three domains. For floodwave propagation in river networks, a 27K-parameter model trained on the Yangtze transfers zero-shot to the Mississippi with median NSE 0.998 in boundary-conditioned operational evaluation, training 5.5x faster than a stabilized recurrent baseline. On cross-geometry Navier-Stokes, the three-seed SepFNO mean relative vorticity error on five unseen targets falls by about 28% from 5 to 12 training geometries, with a consistent single-run SepTransolver trend. On cross-city traffic forecasting, zero-shot transfer reaches within 12.9% of an oracle trained on the target city. Across settings, cross-geometry error decreases with both the number of training geometries and their relatedness to the test, at a rate depending on the spatial mixer. This opens the path to pooled-data, foundation-style models for graph dynamics on irregular topologies.

papers.title: One Step, Four Clocks: How GUI Agents Fall Out of Step
papers.abstract: GUI agents can choose correct actions yet fail as interfaces change during deliberation. Latency alone cannot explain these failures because actions may become invalid at different interaction stages. We model four events: environment change, observation availability, decision commitment, and action receipt (EODA). We introduce ChronotopeGym to study these failures under Paused, Replay, and Live execution. Across five tasks, agents can fail in Live despite succeeding when responses remain valid, even when actions meet deadlines. On Moving Balloon, updating a pending click raises success from 0% to 100% without changing response time. Our accelerator-resident GUI controller, Chronotope, maintains compact interaction history and selectively keeps, updates, or redecides pending actions. Compared with Agent S3, Chronotope reduces median end-to-end latency by 85.5% for a 27B model, expanding its performance envelope to 100% Live success at an 8-second deadline versus 0%. Chronotope enables real-time GUI control through compact interaction history, knowing when to preserve, revise, or replace actions, and an overall efficient architectural design that obviates verbose reflection, reasoning, and grounding calls.

papers.title: Universal spectrum of weakly coupled quantum critical Ising chains
papers.abstract: We study the spectrum of arrays of critical transverse field Ising chains perturbed by a weak inter-chain coupling in the scaling limit, using an exact diagonalization algorithm based on Hamiltonian truncation. As the number of chains is made large, we confirm the existence of excitations below the two particle continuum that can be identified with the celebrated Zamalodchikov $E_8$ theory with small corrections. In addition, we find a distinct $\psi$-particle, with mass $M_\mathrm{\psi}$ which is not contained in the $E_8$ theory. Its ratio to the lowest $E_8$ mass ($M_1$) is a universal number, which we have computed numerically to be $M_\mathrm{\psi}/M_1 = 1.819\cdots$ for a one dimensional array of critical chains. We present evidence that this new state fundamentally involves excitations on neighboring chains, explaining why it has no analogue in the single chain problem. Interestingly the $M_\mathrm{\psi}$ mass has a characteristic scaling dependence on detuning from the critical point that is qualitatively distinct from the $E_8$ masses, which can help identify it in spectroscopic experiments on easy-axis magnetic chain materials.

papers.title: Reading Decisions Before Spans: Efficient Generative Verification
papers.abstract: A developer checking an assistant's report may need only an alarm that a claim is unsupported. A generative verifier, however, can continue decoding to quote and classify the errors. We study how much of that output is needed to recover its decision. In a frozen 2B span verifier, the choice between an empty error list and its first object precedes all localization. Native8 stops generation at this branch. The preceding seven syntax tokens are fixed, so Prefill1 supplies them as input and generates only the unrestricted branch token, using the same native instruction. On 2,015 code-agent TEST responses, Prefill1 reduces eager resident service by 84.84% relative to full generation, with released-reference F1 of 83.43 versus 83.41. It saves 31.98% over Native8 even though their logical token totals are identical. Under default compiled execution, the extra saving is 6.74-26.73% on the complete workload, with small decision changes. Controlled evidence interventions and first-location decoding establish what these shorter readouts retain and what requires further generation.

authors.name: Yanbin Gong
authors.institution: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Topological Anderson Superconductor in Landau Levels
papers.abstract: There is much interest in two-dimensional superconductors with odd integer values of the Bogoliubov-de Gennes (BdG) Chern number $C_{\rm BdG}$, often termed topological superconductors, as these are predicted to harbor Majorana zero modes. Because a magnetic field produces Landau levels (LL) with nonzero Chern numbers, it is natural to ask if a conventional two-dimensional superconductor of spinful fermions with Rashba spin-orbit coupling can be driven topological by application of a magnetic field. Self-consistent solutions of the BdG equations for an on-site attractive interaction produce a phase diagram consisting almost everywhere of superconducting states with even integer values of $C_{\rm BdG}$, transitioning from one value to another as parameters such as the chemical potential are varied. We predict that introducing Anderson-type on-site disorder, which broadens as well as mixes LLs, produces, in the transition region, states wherein topological superconductivity percolates. This topological Anderson superconducting state provides another example where disorder can produce topologically nontrivial states.

papers.title: Lexical Tone and Word Order Matter in Translation: Prosodic Correspondence Across Languages
papers.abstract: Prosody conveys emphasis, emotion, and intent, yet its correspondence across translation remains underexplored, especially when languages differ in lexical tone and word order. To our knowledge, we present the first systematic word-level analysis of prosodic correspondence in translated speech spanning tonal and non-tonal Asian languages, with comparisons to European-language findings and explicit analyses of lexical tone and word reordering. Building on prior evidence of fine-grained prosody correspondence in European-language pairs, we investigate how these linguistic factors relate to word-level pitch and energy correspondence between English and five languages: Mandarin Chinese, Thai, and Vietnamese, which have lexical tone, and Japanese and Korean as additional comparisons. Correspondence is generally lower than previously reported European-language estimates. Adjusting for lexical tone increases pitch correspondence for English-Mandarin Chinese, English-Thai, and English-Vietnamese. However, English-Japanese and English-Korean also exhibit lower correspondence than the European-language estimates, indicating that tonal status alone does not explain the observed pattern. Greater word reordering is associated with weaker local correspondence even under semantic alignment, suggesting that semantic alignment does not fully account for differences in prosodic organization. These findings characterize the limits of fine-grained acoustic correspondence across translation and motivate prosody modeling that accounts for lexical pitch constraints and the structural context of translated content.

papers.title: Characterizing Datasets to Anticipate Unsupervised Domain Adaptation Performance for Radiographic Pneumonia Detection
papers.abstract:
Deep learning models for pneumonia detection from chest radiographs exhibit degraded accuracy when applied across institutions, which motivates Unsupervised Domain Adaptation (UDA). We observe that UDA performance depends on the properties of both the source and target datasets, and that performance gains are asymmetric with respect to dataset pairs. We investigate which structural properties of chest X-ray datasets are the most important predictors of UDA performance, and whether they can be measured before adaptation is attempted.
  Five chest radiograph datasets were characterized by the class separability of their features, obtained from one forward pass of a frozen DenseNet-121 and summarized by the Silhouette Score, with the Fisher Ratio as a supporting measure. All twenty directed source-target pairs were adapted with a Domain-Adversarial Neural Network (DANN), while direct transfer without adaptation was also evaluated. Seven published transferability estimators were computed on the same representation for comparison.
  We found that adaptation performance depended on both endpoints in opposite directions. More separable target datasets attained higher AUC scores ($r=0.934$, $p=0.042$), whereas more separable sources produced lower AUC scores ($r=-0.922$, $p=0.017$). The signed difference in separability tracked the signed difference in AUC between the two directions of a pair ($r=-0.932$, $p=0.017$) and identified the better direction in 10 of 10 pairs ($p=0.001$). The proposed descriptor was comparable to the best published estimators on target evaluation.
  Source and target datasets play opposite structural roles in adaptation: higher class separability makes a dataset easier as a test set but not as a training source. This framework can guide dataset selection for adaptation in low-resource settings without running full experiments.

papers.title: SpecEngineeringBench: Evaluating Coding Agents as Autonomous Specification Engineers
papers.abstract: Autonomous specification engineering requires coding agents to translate functional requirements into executable tests and use the results to discover and validate defects. However, existing benchmarks evaluate coding agents on explicitly specified test generation tasks, commonly providing an issue description, a designated test entry point, or files to inspect, leaving the ability to determine what to test and where to investigate insufficiently evaluated. Relying on such clues bypasses the challenge of mapping requirements to implementations and proactively uncovering unknown defects. We propose SpecEngineeringBench, comprising 100 instances from 78 open-source Python repositories across 16 application categories, with multiple recorded defects in each instance. Two independent tasks evaluate complementary capabilities: generating test suites and discovering defects through execution analysis. The evaluation combines test validity, defect detection, and coverage with localization precision and recall. Across seven frontier coding agents, results reveal that test validity and coverage decouple from defect exposure: agents achieve a 91.47% Head Pass Rate and 80.48% Change-focused Coverage alongside a 26.36% Fail-to-Pass Rate, while localization recall drops from 78.11% at the file level to 51.29% at the function level. Autonomous test generation improves file, function, and hunk localization recall by 4.99, 2.77, and 2.69 percentage points over relying solely on existing repository test suites.

authors.name: Ge Zhang
authors.institution: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

papers.title: EvoSearch: Self-Evolving Active Perception for Wide-Area Geospatial Search
papers.abstract: Geospatial search is fundamental to resource surveys and environmental monitoring, requiring the discovery of relevant evidence across large geographic areas and multiple spatial scales. Existing active perception methods adaptively select observation locations and scales to improve search efficiency, yet their search trajectories become increasingly long and costly as the search area expands. A key limitation is that final-answer correctness alone provides little guidance on which observations to retain and when to stop, hindering efficient wide-area search. To address this challenge, we propose EvoSearch, a self-evolving active perception framework that co-evolves the perception policy and exploration program to compress search trajectories while preserving answer quality. Specifically, quality-cost comparisons between completed branches from shared evidence train the policy to acquire useful observations, avoid redundant ones, and stop when sufficient evidence is available. Execution feedback from the updated policy then guides exploration-program revision, adapting experience generation to the policy's changing observation needs. We further introduce GeoSearchBench, a benchmark for evaluating search quality and visual processing efficiency through relational search and region search. Experiments demonstrate that EvoSearch shortens search trajectories and substantially reduces visual processing while maintaining overall search quality, supporting scalable active perception for wide-area geospatial search.

authors.name: Zhenghao Xie
authors.institution: Macau University of Science and Technology

papers.title: A Classification of Trees Without Unique Subgraphs
papers.abstract: We study trees without unique subgraphs, in both the induced and non-induced settings. Graphs without unique induced subgraphs, called anchor-free graphs, form a natural candidate class for counterexamples to the Graph Reconstruction Conjecture, but their structure remains poorly understood. We develop a framework for studying anchor-free graphs based on a covering lemma that characterizes anchor-freeness via induced subgraph coverings of vertices. Using this framework, we prove that a tree is anchor-free if and only if it is a path with one less vertex than a prime. We also introduce the related notion of unique-subgraph-freeness, which acts as an edge-based analogue of anchor-freeness. We show that the line graph of every unique-subgraph-free graph is anchor-free and obtain a complete classification of unique-subgraph-free trees as either prime paths, stars, or extended stars. Together, these results provide a classification of trees without unique subgraphs and suggest a general approach for extending the theory beyond trees.

authors.name: Andrew Searns
authors.institution: Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory

papers.title: Not Just Any Example: Security Requirements and Fix Patterns for Guiding LLM Vulnerability Repair
papers.abstract: Software vulnerabilities leave systems open to attack, and their remediation is often delayed. Large language models (LLMs) have advanced automated patch generation, yet passing functionality tests does not ensure that a patch enforces the security requirement the vulnerability violated. Existing vulnerability repair techniques rely on curated patterns or templates with limited coverage, leaving unclear which repair strategies carry over across vulnerabilities and how they can steer LLMs. We present a large-scale empirical study that relates recurring fix patterns to the security impacts of vulnerabilities and examines how this knowledge can guide LLM-based repair. Building on a manual study of security patches, we cluster 3,816 security patches from 348 open-source repositories and analyze the edits and their context to derive concrete fix patterns, ranging from local safeguards to coordinated changes across multiple locations. We define 12 security impact classes by the security requirements that vulnerabilities violate and map them to repair categories and fix patterns, revealing characteristic repairs, alternative strategies within a class, and patterns shared across classes. We then use these patterns and impact-pattern associations to select repair examples for four LLMs on repair tasks of varying complexity. Guided example selection raises the four-model mean pass@3 from 37.9% under zero-shot prompting to up to 49.2%, whereas randomly selected examples reach only 36.9%. Our findings connect vulnerability characterization with patch generation and support organizing repair knowledge around security requirements.

authors.name: Xinda Wang
authors.institution: China University of Mining and Technology - Beijing

papers.title: Generalized Tate--Nakayama duality for complexes of tori over local function fields
papers.abstract: We define the cohomology set $H^{1}(\mathcal{E}, Z \to T \to U)$ for a complex $Z \to T \to U$ with $T$, $U$ tori over a local function field $F$ and $Z$ a finite subgroup of $T$, where $\mathcal{E}$ is the gerbe from [Dil23]. We follow the method of [Kal26] and prove that the Tate--Nakayama isomorphism [Dil23, Theorem 4.10] for $H^{1}(\mathcal{E}, Z \to T)$ extends to $H^{1}(\mathcal{E}, Z \to T \to U)$, which lets one generalize Kaletha's parametrization [Kal21] of supercuspidal $L$-packets to local function fields.

papers.title: RVLM-X: Towards a Universal VLM Harness
papers.abstract: Harnesses for vision-language models (VLMs) have grown with the models' capabilities, notably for images far larger than those seen in training, where downscaling loses small details. Most of them wrap the VLM in a fixed procedure, such as a zoom tree, that decides in advance where it looks and how the evidence is combined. These procedures make up for the weaknesses of older models by keeping them on a task-specific path, but with frontier models that reliably plan and use tools, they can lower accuracy. We propose RVLM-X, a task-generalizable recursive VLM harness that runs unchanged across photographs, charts and maps. Following the recursive inference of Recursive Language Models, the VLM programmatically controls its own visual context in a code REPL that holds the full-resolution image and calls itself recursively on regions that it chooses. With a cost-efficient frontier model as the base of every method, RVLM-X is more accurate than a single call on all 7 public benchmarks and has the highest pooled accuracy. Because existing benchmarks mostly test whether a model finds one small detail, we also introduce MapGenBench, procedurally generated maps whose questions combine fine-detail perception with multi-step reasoning. There, RVLM-X answers 71.4% of held-out questions against 55.5% for the strongest baseline. Overall, our findings suggest that as VLMs plan and use tools more reliably, letting the model write its own visual search works better than fixing one in advance.

papers.title: On Euclidean Diameter in Dynamic Streams
papers.abstract:
We give a streaming algorithm for maintaining the diameter of a high-dimensional Euclidean point set under arbitrary insertions and deletions that achieves update time polylogarithmic in the number of points and polynomial in the dimension. For every fixed $c>\sqrt3$, there is an $\epsilon_c > 0$ such that our one-pass algorithm uses $\tilde O(N^{1-\epsilon_c}\poly(d))$ space, has worst-case update time $\poly(d,\log N)$, and maintains a factor-$c$ pair witness.
  On the hardness side, we prove that every constant-factor approximation requires polynomial memory even on short dynamic streams: a factor-$c$ approximation needs $N^{\Omega(1/(c^2\log(c+1)))}$ space on streams of at most $2N-1$ updates.
  Our upper bound combines a geometric hull, Gaussian hashing through successively smaller caps, and local and global rebuilding schedules. Every update changes only one leaf of the hash hierarchy, while the answer is maintained through small variance certificates. The lower bound is based on a communication complexity argument. Together, these results separate the polynomial memory regime from the time needed to process an update.

papers.title: LIBRA: Runtime Co-Tuning of Batch Size and Parallelism for Time-Efficient LLM Training
papers.abstract: Training large language models (LLMs) requires choosing both a batch size and a parallel configuration. Existing systems make these decisions in isolation, tuning parallelism for throughput and batch size for convergence, but neither objective alone determines training efficiency. We present LIBRA, a lightweight runtime framework that co-tunes batch size and parallel configuration to minimize end-to-end time. LIBRA treats throughput and convergence as two noisy objectives and searches their joint space using parallel noisy expected hypervolume improvement (qNEHVI). To make this runtime search efficient, we propose hierarchical pruning, which removes infeasible and low-throughput parallel configurations through system-level performance estimation and then narrows batch-size candidates through critical-batch-size-aware convergence monitoring. We further design acquisition-guided parallel evaluation (AGPE), which evaluates surviving candidates concurrently across GPU groups in order of their acquisition values. On clusters of up to 256 GPUs, LIBRA reduces time-to-convergence by 31.1% on average over state-of-the-art methods, while runtime tuning accounts for only 0.3-3.5% of overall time.

papers.title: FigmaEval: A Benchmark for Evaluating AI Agents in Professional UI Design
papers.abstract: Recent advances in AI agents have enabled autonomous UI design using professional tools such as Figma, yet evaluating their design capabilities remains challenging due to the open-ended nature of design tasks and the absence of unique ground truths. We introduce FigmaEval, a benchmark for evaluating AI agents on professional UI design tasks, comprising 84 tasks and 783 screens derived from real-world Figma design files. FigmaEval adopts a constrained-specification, open-solution paradigm, standardizing task requirements and design resources while allowing agents to independently determine layouts, visual hierarchies, component composition, and visual presentation. To assess design quality beyond reference similarity, we develop 22 expert-grounded evaluation rubrics across six dimensions and introduce a human evaluation arena where professional designers compare agent-generated designs through blinded pairwise judgments. Evaluating eleven models under a unified Figma agent setup, we find substantial agreement between rubric-based assessments and human preferences, alongside distinct differences in design practices and quality--efficiency trade-offs. FigmaEval provides a framework for systematically assessing professional UI design capabilities and understanding the strengths and limitations of current AI agents.

authors.name: Xinya Liu
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Lewei Lu
authors.institution: Chengdu College of University of Electronic Science And Technology of China

papers.title: VenusOCR2.0: Towards Efficient and Effective Document Parsing
papers.abstract: We present VenusOCR2.0, a compact 1B-parameter vision-language recognizer designed for both high-accuracy and high-throughput document parsing across text, tables, and formulas. To continuously improve recognition quality without self-training collapse, we build a bounded recursive self-improvement (RSI) data engine where the model acts strictly as a weakness probe, while external multi-expert medoid consensus, VLM visual verification, and factorized synthesis supply reliable supervision across pretraining, curated SFT, and RLVR. VenusOCR2.0 couples a dynamic-resolution SigLIP2 encoder and 2x2 spatial token merging with a Qwen3-0.6B decoder, adopting compact atomic OTSL tokens to shorten table sequences and reduce structural errors. To further eliminate the autoregressive decoding bottleneck, we introduce PTPv2, a lightweight ($\sim$67M) decoupled parallel draft module that combines frozen multi-layer verifier conditioning, a standalone learned mask, and block-causal all-position next-token prediction. On OmniDocBenchv1.6, VenusOCR2.0 achieves an overall score of 96.45 and a state-of-the-art 98.57 formula CDM, substantially outperforming massive general-purpose VLMs such as Gemini-3-Pro (92.91) and Qwen3-VL-235B (89.78). Deployed in vLLM on a single H20 GPU, PTPv2 delivers a 2.96x single-request speedup and up to 2.36x higher batched throughput while guaranteeing lossless, token-for-token equivalence with standard autoregressive decoding.

authors.name: Lei Li
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Qingbin Liu
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Mineral Processing

papers.title: Adaptive ghost Gutzwiller dynamics of Hubbard model quenches across coupling strengths over extended times
papers.abstract: Following the real-time dynamics of correlated electrons to extended times, at all interaction strengths, remains an open challenge. We address it with an adaptive time-dependent ghost Gutzwiller approximation (td-gGA). The method extends the Gutzwiller approximation by auxiliary ghost orbitals. It adds more of them whenever the correlations that build up during the dynamics exceed a threshold. This is computationally far more efficient than keeping their number fixed. As a demonstration we take the interaction quench of the half-filled Hubbard model on the Bethe lattice. For this paradigmatic problem, numerically exact nonequilibrium dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) serves as the reference. A previous td-gGA study with a fixed set of 6 ghost orbitals per spin largely reproduced the available DMFT data. It lacked, however, an error estimate that would support predictions beyond them. With up to 16 ghost orbitals per spin, adaptive td-gGA agrees with DMFT wherever DMFT data are available, from the weak-coupling prethermal regime to the strong-coupling collapse-and-revival regime. At strong coupling it remains converged up to three and a half times as long as the DMFT data. Near the crossover between the two regimes, the system relaxes to thermal values that agree with DMFT. Resolving the dynamics in the number of ghost orbitals shows how the sharp dynamical transition of the Gutzwiller approximation turns into this smooth crossover. In the extended time window at strong coupling, we observe that the oscillation frequency is renormalized as predicted by our second-order strong-coupling expansion. With its built-in error estimate, adaptive td-gGA offers a systematically improvable route to the extended-time dynamics of driven and multi-orbital correlated systems, especially when combined with tensor-network or quantum solvers for the embedding problem.

papers.title: Bit-Flip Attacks on Quantized Neural Networks without Knowledge of Model Parameters
papers.abstract: We show that quantization asymmetry concentrates bit-flip vulnerability in small tensors retained at high precision. CoarseHammer targets these tensors and accepts flips at any bit, without parameter values, gradients, or data. It remains effective under continued fine-tuning. Under ideal placement, CoarseHammer reaches chance accuracy in at least 81.5% of runs on each of ten evaluated models, including four large language models, with median successful runs requiring at most 24 flips. On simulated DRAM with 0.01 flippable bits per million, it outperforms three prior attacks on every evaluated convolutional network, succeeding in up to 83.6% of runs while they never succeed. On a real system, CoarseHammer steers heap-allocated tensors onto vulnerable frames despite address space layout randomization, without accessing the model file. With 16 templated frames, median accuracy reaches chance for all four language models and approximately chance for four convolutional networks.

papers.title: Sparse Poison, Strong Hijack: Efficient Trajectory-Level Backdoors in Vision-Language-Action Models with Only 1\% Poisoning
papers.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models advance robotic manipulation, but their reliance on demonstrations exposes them to backdoor threats. Among these threats, trajectory-level targeted backdoors are particularly challenging and may pose greater safety risks than behavior-disrupting attacks: rather than merely causing task failures or local action deviations, they must sustain closed-loop redirection to complete an attacker-specified multi-step task. To reliably induce such behaviors, existing methods typically rely on high poisoning rates to obtain sufficient target-trajectory supervision. However, high poisoning rates may compromise clean-task performance, whereas low rates leave target-trajectory supervision scarce and backdoor learning vulnerable to interference from dominant clean-task updates. To resolve this trade-off at low poisoning rates, we propose a two-stage co-optimization framework guided by vision, language, and action. Stage I freezes the policy and uses differentiable rendering and multimodal supervision to optimize a 3D trigger's texture, translation, and scale, strengthening trigger-target associations from limited poisoned demonstrations. Building on the optimized trigger, Stage II applies source-selective dual-LoRA adaptation to decouple clean and backdoor updates and mitigate their interference, followed by learned column-wise calibration and analytic fusion into a unified policy. Experiments on OpenVLA, OpenVLA-OFT, $\pi_0$, and $\pi_{0.5}$ across four LIBERO suites show consistent gains over all evaluated attack baselines. With only 1% poisoned data, our method achieves 86.4% target success and 95.2% clean-task success on OpenVLA-OFT in LIBERO-Spatial. Real-robot trials also demonstrate trajectory-level hijacking.

authors.name: Jiawei Chen
authors.institution: Chongqing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: Sharp Rigidity of Hyperbolic $p$-Barycenters
papers.abstract: We study the hyperbolic $p$-barycenters $C_p$, $0\le p\le\infty$, of $n$ points $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_n$ in the hyperbolic plane. For $0<p<\infty$, $C_p$ minimizes the sum of the $p$th powers of the hyperbolic cosines of the distances to the points. At the endpoints, $C_0$ minimizes the product of these cosines and $C_\infty$ their maximum. The center map $p\mapsto C_p$ is real analytic at every finite parameter. A point $P$ is the center for every parameter exactly when, at each positive distance from $P$, the unit directions to the points at that distance sum to zero. If the map is nonconstant, the equation $C_p=P$ has at most $n-2$ solutions in $[0,\infty]$ for each $P$, and at most $\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor$ when the points lie on a geodesic. Finite solutions are counted with multiplicity, and the endpoint contributes one if $C_\infty=P$. Each bound is attained in arbitrarily small disks, with prescribed finite parameters and multiplicities, and with or without the endpoint. The proofs use exponential sums over distance shells, a variation-diminishing property of the radial-weight kernel, and the Hobby--Rice theorem. For the upper-half-plane roots of a totally complex real binary form, $C_0$ is Julia's zero and $C_1$ is the hyperbolic zero. Their coincidence forces the center map to be constant in degrees at most six, but counterexamples exist in every even degree at least eight. We obtain the same bounds on the number of distinct parameters for Riemannian $L^q$ centers, the minimizers of $\sum_i d(P,\alpha_i)^q$ on Hadamard manifolds for $1<q<\infty$.

papers.title: Multi-Scale Temporal Structure of the Conti Ransomware Communication Network
papers.abstract: Communication networks provide a means of inferring broader organisational structure from accumulated local interactions. Cybercriminal organisations are particularly vulnerable to such inference, despite their secretive nature, because their distributed operation necessitates coordination through centralised digital communication infrastructure. The public leak of the Conti ransomware organisation's internal communications provides a rare longitudinal record of this coordination. Yet common approaches to analysing such longitudinal records aggregate interactions into a static network or model the communication process as stationary, both assuming a temporal homogeneity rarely tested for criminal organisations. Here we show substantial temporal heterogeneity at each scale examined in the Conti record, and demonstrate that much of it can be accounted for through appropriate, diagnostically guided choices of event representation and observation period. Collapsing rapid message bursts into conversational episodes brings communication timing closer to a constant-intensity reference and clarifies longer-timescale structure, which resolves into a sequence of distinct communication regimes, including a major transition following a coordinated platform migration. Even so, within these regimes heterogeneity persists, most evident in churn among peripheral participants, while highly active actors remain consistently observable. Together, these findings motivate explicit consideration of multi-scale temporal dynamics in the analysis, modelling and longitudinal monitoring of cybercriminal networks.

papers.title: Agentic Systems Need Multi-Run Evaluation: A Study of Retrieval and Response Variability in a Deployed Enterprise RAG System
papers.abstract: Previous RAG systems have mostly been evaluated in a single-run setting, and with the advent of agentic RAG, systems are still often evaluated the same way. However, agentic RAG systems introduce a source of run-to-run variability, since several of their components make decisions non-deterministically. Such systems typically comprise a retrieval stage followed by a generation stage, and the retrieval stage in particular can behave differently across runs. For example, the agent might issue a different number of parallel searches from one run to the next, which alters the retrieved documents and therefore the final answer. In this paper we study this behavior in a deployed agentic RAG system for product-documentation questions, running each of 739 questions ten times and analyzing the execution traces to find where different runs first diverge. We find a substantial gap between success in any run and success in every run: the retrieval hit rate is 69.4% when the correct page is found in at least one run, but 50.9% when it must be found in all ten. Responses also stay similar in meaning while varying in wording, with an average BERTScore of 0.90 and a BLEU of 0.49. Trace-level analysis shows that retrieval is the largest source of divergence (43.9%), and the number of parallel searches at the first retrieval step alone accounts for 20.1% of divergent pairs. Taken together, these results show that single-run evaluation can hide reliability and consistency issues in agentic RAG systems, and that multi-run evaluation is necessary to reveal them.

authors.name: Karan Gupta
authors.institution: American Association of Colleges of Pharmacy

papers.title: Lazy Agents Answer Against Their Own Beliefs: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Beliefs Teaches Them to Act on What They Believe
papers.abstract: AI agents working on long tasks often commit to an answer before they have enough evidence, a behavior called laziness. In our evaluations, they frequently commit even while their stated belief still names several possible answers. An outcome reward at the end of the episode scores only the final answer, so it cannot teach the agent when to commit, because a lucky guess receives the same reward as an answer backed by evidence. During training, however, the simulator can compute the exact posterior over the answer at every step and tell whether the evidence is already enough. We propose Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Beliefs (RLVB), which rewards the agent for taking further steps while this posterior still allows several answers and for committing once the evidence is sufficient. The reward needs no judge, critic or reward model, and it never reads the belief line the agent writes before each action. We also introduce Pro Worlds, a benchmark of visual puzzles where the agent views a large world through a small window. We evaluate three vision-language models on three benchmarks, two of which are never seen in training. RLVB improves the base model in all nine settings, by 17.1% on average. Under the outcome reward, GRPO and PPO fall below the base model on average. RLVB also outperforms PPO with a process reward from an LLM judge by 9.3% on average while using 1.6 times fewer GPU-hours. The trained agent answers with sufficient evidence in 51%, 12% and 74% of the episodes on the three benchmarks, against 8%, 0.4% and 36% for the base model. Its accuracy gain therefore comes from answering more often at high levels of evidence. The belief line shows how the agent reaches this evidence: it acts on its own belief. It commits at only 0.1 to 2.2% of the turns at which the evidence is insufficient and its line still names several answers, against 3 to 68% for the base model.

authors.name: Soujanya Poria
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: Unit Lattices of Totally Complex, non-CM $D_4$-Octic Number Fields
papers.abstract: Given a number field, we can endow the unit group of its ring of integers, modulo torsion, with the structure of a lattice. Included in the study of the distributions of these lattices is the classification of shapes of unit lattices arising from $D_4$-quartic number fields with signature $(2,1)$. We extend this work to rank 3, by investigating the shapes of lattices arising from the unit groups of totally complex, non-CM $D_4$-octic number fields. In particular, we show all such unit lattices have automorphism group $D_4\times \mathbb{Z}/2{\mathbb{Z}}$, yet none correspond to Gram matrices whose entries are all algebraic.

papers.title: Reading, Writing and Repairing Game-Theoretic Policies in Weight Space
papers.abstract: Can a language model work in the weight space of a policy network for a repeated game? We put four questions to a mid-size open model, on recurrent networks of 1{,}218 weights with exactly checkable answers. Given a population of opponents described in English, write a policy that is optimal: its value is a finite computation over the agent's information state, so a submitted network has an exact gap from the optimum. Given a network's weights, report its action after each of fifteen opponent histories; recover the state machine it implements, judged on every opponent sequence to depth ten; or repair a network whose output was altered in one place and say which round first goes wrong. The model recovers the program in 62 of 66 replies, reports all fifteen behavioral entries correctly in 34 of 36, and attains the optimum in 20 of 20 when it states a policy the evaluator compiles. Repair is the exception: 4 of 18 repaired, 5 of 18 diagnosed, with a median patch covering one of the two entries needed.

papers.title: HDMark: Holographic Multi-Bit Model Watermarking for Intellectual Property Protection in Hyperdimensional Computing
papers.abstract: Hyperdimensional computing (HDC) models deployed on edge hardware are valuable intellectual property that is easy to steal, since a trained classifier consolidates its learned knowledge into a compact set of class prototype hypervectors; yet protecting their ownership through watermarking remains largely unexplored. We present HDMark, the first model watermarking framework native to HDC, which encodes ownership in the same hyperdimensional algebra the model computes with. HDMark maps a multi-bit owner identity to secret quasi-orthogonal carriers, superimposes them holographically onto the trained class prototypes, and verifies ownership with a statistical test. Across four datasets and three HDC learning rules, HDMark leaves accuracy essentially unchanged and verifies a 64-bit identity in 99.8% of trials at p < 0.001. We derive closed-form expressions for prediction fidelity and bit recovery that match measurements within 0.4 pp mean absolute error. The watermark survives fine-tuning and low-bit quantization, while attempting to erase it through noise injection, pruning, or overwriting severely degrades model accuracy. We further identify a dimension-permutation attack specific to HDC, which reorders hypervector coordinates to evade verification without altering predictions, and counter it through encoder realignment. Finally, an AMD ZCU104 FPGA implementation confirms that HDMark adds no hardware overhead, remains bit-exact under aggressive undervolting, and stays verifiable under timing faults until the classifier itself fails.

papers.title: An Exposition of Gerstenhaber's Proposition 1: Elimination of Coboundaries in Formal Deformations
papers.abstract: Gerstenhaber's foundational work on formal deformations of associative algebras relates the first non-trivial term of a deformation to the second Hochschild cohomology group. In the proof of Proposition~1 of his 1964 paper, a leading Hochschild $2$-cocycle which is a coboundary is successively removed by formal changes of variables. If this elimination terminates after finitely many steps, no limiting argument is required, but the possibility that coboundaries continue to be eliminated indefinitely is left largely implicit in the original treatment. This expository note makes that limiting argument fully explicit for deformations over $K[[t]]$ of a fixed associative $K$-algebra $A$. We use the $t$-adic topology on the relevant spaces of formal power series and formal endomorphisms, establish completeness and the continuity of composition, inversion and the action on formal multiplications, and show that an infinite sequence of successive changes of variables assembles into a single, well-defined formal equivalence. This yields a complete, self-contained proof of the classical result and its rigidity consequence.

papers.title: DAA for an Autonomous Delivery Drone: Maneuver Selection Policies for Near-Collision Risk Avoidance
papers.abstract:
Detect-and-avoid (DAA) systems for autonomous drones operating in shared airspace must select avoidance maneuvers under conditions that differ markedly from those assumed by conventional DAA architectures designed for crewed aircraft. Limited on-board sensing capabilities restrict detection of collision risk to near distances (sub-km), the time available for decision-making is severely limited, uncertainty in the predicted closest point of approach (CPA) and the time to reach it is substantial, and the maneuver envelope of a small uncrewed aircraft at low altitude is tightly constrained.
  This paper presents and compares two maneuver-selection strategies that address these challenges: (1) a purely geometric approach, steering in the direction away from the intruder at CPA, and (2) a method that also takes into account the known sources of uncertainty in the intruder's location, and steers away from a plane expected to contain the intruder's location distribution at CPA.
  Performance is evaluated using the risk ratio metric on a large dataset of simulated near-collision encounters with crewed intruders. Results indicate that both strategies are feasible (i.e., computable in closed form from an onboard track estimate), and that the second strategy substantially outperforms the first.

authors.name: Pradeep Yarlagadda
authors.institution: International Institute of Information Technology, Hyderabad

papers.title: Advanced Synthetic Image Detection Using Hybrid Feature Extraction
papers.abstract: In the realm of generative AI, models such as GANs, MidJourney, DALL-E, and others have been continuously evolving to generate increasingly lifelike images. This rapid advancement has created an urgent need for robust methods to distinguish between real and AI-generated images. This paper proposes a novel approach for the detection of synthetic images by employing deep learning techniques for feature analysis. The proposed architecture classifies images by identifying variations that generative models struggle to replicate, particularly fine-grained textures and complex object features. Deformations in complexes are examined with the help of the CBAM architecture along with ResNet50. We have performed a selective patch-based analysis using Discrete Cosine Transform (DCT) scoring, extracting the regions with the most and least complexity for further processing with an SRM Module and ResNet50 module. Experimental results show that our approach achieves high accuracy in classifying real-world images from synthetic ones, contributing to the development of more reliable detection frameworks.

papers.title: Embodied Neuro-symbolic AI: Making Robot Behavior Auditable, Safe, and Scalable
papers.abstract: Current Vision-Language-Action (VLA) end-to-end systems have driven major progress in robot learning, yet they still face persistent barriers to dependable real-world deployment. In practice, these models often exhibit brittle generalization under distribution shift (i.e., novel objects, layouts, lighting, or contact conditions), limited physical and causal reasoning, and inconsistent fine-grained motor control. Critically, many VLA pipelines offer limited ways to express and audit what a robot must not do, making it difficult to provide assurance in safety-critical settings. These limitations constrain scalability, maintainability, and trust when robots move beyond controlled demonstrations. We propose Embodied Neuro-Symbolic (NeSy) AI: a deployment-oriented paradigm that integrates learned perception, planning and control with explicit, machine-readable background knowledge and formal constraints. By combining knowledge-guided perception, constraint-aware symbolic planning, and hybrid learning, Embodied NeSy AI enables robots to reason about their environment, adapt to new tasks, and provide auditable, machine-checkable compliance with safety and operational requirements, thus supporting scalable, trustworthy robot deployment.

papers.title: Safe Autoformalization: Sufficiency and Necessity with Entailment Graphs
papers.abstract: Autoformalization translates a natural-language statement into a formula that captures its intent, which depends on the statement's context: the background that disambiguates it. LLMs make autoformalization practical, but their probabilistic output carries no formal guarantees. We propose techniques for safe autoformalization that certify one-sided logical adequacy: a formula sufficient for the intent is safe to enforce, and a formula necessary for it is safe to rely on.
