We determine how closely such a rule can match the average loss of the best single expert on the full sample. For any bounded loss that is a continuous nondecreasing function of absolute error and vanishes at zero, let $B$ denote its maximum value. Over classes of size $M$ and samples on which the best expert has average loss at most $r$, the minimax excess loss is of order $\min\{B, \sqrt{\frac{Br\log M}{n}}+\frac{B\log M}{n}\}$. For each class and loss, one deterministic rule attains this rate for every $r\in[0,B]$. The matching lower bound holds even for randomized proper rules given $r$.

papers.title: Network-Guided Automated Synthesis of MAC Units for Neural Network Inference
papers.abstract: In neural inference accelerators, multiply-accumulate (MAC) datapaths account for the majority of circuit area and critical-path delay, where operator-level numerical formats simultaneously dictate hardware overhead and quantization error. Yet no straightforward mapping exists between hardware cost and end-to-end network accuracy: logic synthesis transforms datapaths in a highly nonlinear manner, while numerical errors propagate and couple across layers. To address this disconnect, we present NAMSI, an automated network-aware MAC synthesis framework tailored for neural inference. NAMSI characterizes heterogeneous data formats using a format-distribution representation (FD) and leverages topology-aware accuracy and hardware-cost modeling (TaH), calibrated with actual post-synthesis Area-Delay Product (ADP) measurements, to jointly estimate coupled full-network accuracy and circuit cost. Furthermore, reversible lattice search (RLS) is introduced to tractably navigate the exponentially scaling design space. Evaluations across five neural networks on ImageNet-1K demonstrate that under post-training quantization (PTQ), NAMSI achieves 54.2%-60.4% reductions in post-synthesis MAC ADP compared with FP32 while retaining at least 99% of full-precision Top-1 accuracy, surpassing baseline approaches in both hardware efficiency and accuracy preservation.

papers.title: ADE: A Zero-Training Unlearning Method for Latent World Models
papers.abstract: Latent world models learn compact recurrent dynamics from offline trajectories, yet deployed simulators can retain backdoor triggers or stale transitions from outdated physical regimes. Existing unlearning methods fail in autoregressive physics: gradient updates distort latent manifolds and compound rollout drift, naive output zeroing suppresses valid control responses on trigger onset, and single-step deletion leaves corruption inside recurrent hidden states. We propose Analytical Dynamics Excision (ADE), a deterministic, zero-training closed-form unlearning algorithm for latent world models. Using only cached pretraining moments, ADE recovers retain covariances via single-pass matrix downdating without raw retain data and cascades closed-form edits across the input bottleneck, hidden states, and downstream heads. Pairing orthogonal excision with whitened recurrent damping and mean-preserving affine calibration neutralizes out-of-manifold backdoors and realigns in-manifold shifts without variance collapse. Across four regimes on three MuJoCo benchmarks, ADE outperforms seven tuned baselines on DreamerV1, eliminating HalfCheetah and Hopper velocity-flip triggers $4.4\times$ faster than fine-tuning, and transfers zero-shot to DreamerV3.

papers.title: DynaCue: Comparing Motion and Timing Between Groups of Videos
papers.abstract: A score that distinguishes videos with different temporal-consistency ratings can miss differences associated with motion preference. VideoScore's temporal consistency score distinguished higher- from lower-rated Pika videos in 95% of comparisons with 15 videos per group, yet could not detect the difference between preferred videos and their same-prompt alternatives in any of the 200 comparisons of 41 VideoGen-RewardBench pairs. We introduce DynaCue, a two-sample permutation test that combines complementary measurements of motion, frame continuity, and appearance to compare groups of videos without choosing a single cue in advance. DynaCue measures local changes in optical flow both before and after accounting for each clip's usual activity, captures interruptions through frame differences and freeze counts, and incorporates scores for motion and appearance. In controlled experiments, DynaCue detected group differences across five interventions affecting playback continuity, displacement, or rhythm. In real-world evaluations of generated videos where viewers rated temporal consistency or chose which of two videos they preferred for its motion, DynaCue detected group differences in at least 80% of resampled comparisons on each of the three datasets at the smaller sample sizes studied. Every other method evaluated on all three had a detection rate of 60% or less on at least one dataset.

papers.title: The polygonal Steklov--Weinstock inequality
papers.abstract: We prove that for every integer $N \ge 3$, the regular $N$-gon uniquely maximizes the scale-invariant first positive Steklov eigenvalue $L(P)\sigma_1(P)$ among all simple planar polygons $P$ of positive area with at most $N$ sides, up to similarity (and up to congruence at prescribed perimeter). Our proof combines two complementary realizations of the Rayleigh--Ritz variational principle. For convex competitors, we transplant a first Steklov eigenfunction of the regular reference polygon: for triangles, affine transplantation aligned with a longest side yields both the sharp inequality and a two-sided linear stability bound in terms of the maximal side-length deviation; for convex $N$-gons with $N \ge 4$, a piecewise harmonic fan transplantation across radial sectors matches traces along the internal seams. In the quadrilateral case, centering the fan at the vertex average pairs opposite sides and controls the displacement of the diagonal midpoints, whereas for $N=5$ the spectral deficit dominates both the area deficit and the squared vertex and Hausdorff distances to the regular pentagon. Nonconvex competitors are treated by stratifying them according to their number $p \le N-1$ of strictly convex corners: boundary moment inequalities handle $p=3$, while conformal disk tests localized on the gaps between positive turning prevertices rule out $p \ge 4$ via comparison with the regular $(p+1)$-gon. Finite parameter ranges are certified using exact rational arithmetic and outward-rounded integer interval enclosures. In addition, we establish the sharp fourth-order asymptotic expansion of the spectral deficit at a prescribed positive-corner count, together with a quantitative local and global stability theorem for polygons with a large number of sides.

papers.title: LoopDVR: Looped Transformer for Efficient Dense Visual Recognition
papers.abstract: We propose LoopDVR, a framework for converting pretrained Transformer-based dense visual recognition models into parameter-efficient looped networks. Rather than reducing the network width or depth directly, LoopDVR reuses Transformer blocks across layers in both the ViT backbone and Transformer decoder, reducing the number of parameters while retaining the original computational structure. However, naively sharing parameters can disrupt the distinct transformations learned at different depths. To address this challenge, we identify suitable sharing groups based on inter-layer representation dissimilarity and keep the final backbone block independent for multi-scale feature construction. We then initialize each shared backbone block with the pretrained weights of its group's terminal layer to better preserve the learned representations. An independent Loop Adapter at each layer further helps retain depth-specific transformations within shared blocks. Subsequently, we distill visual representations into the looped backbone and integrate it with a looped decoder for task-specific training. Experiments demonstrate that LoopDVR achieves the best accuracy--parameter trade-offs across dense recognition tasks. Compared with the reference models, it reduces parameters by approximately 28% while maintaining competitive accuracy. Notably, LoopDet-S achieves 50.9 box AP with only 7.0M parameters, highlighting its effectiveness in compact models.

papers.title: Asymptotically Optimal Two Source Extractors for Arbitrary Constant Entropy Rate
papers.abstract:
We construct explicit two-source extractors for any constant entropy rate with asymptotically optimal parameters. Specifically, for sources on $n$ bits with min-entropy $k =\delta n$ for any constant $\delta \in (0, 1]$, and error $\varepsilon \geq 2^{-b_{\delta}n}$ where $b_{\delta}$ is a constant depending on $\delta$, our extractor outputs $2k-O(\log(1/\varepsilon)+1)$ bits that are $\varepsilon$ close to uniform. In particular, this gives two-source extractors with $\Omega(n)$ output bits and $2^{-\Omega(n)}$ error for any constant entropy rate. Previously, explicit two source extractors with such error are only known to work for entropy rate roughly $4/9$ (Bourgain 2005, Lewko 2019). We also extend our constructions to give (strong) non-malleable two source extractors and sumset extractors for any constant entropy rate with asymptotically optimal parameters.
  Our extractors can be extended to handle slightly sub-constant entropy rate, with sub-optimal error. Using a different construction and analysis, we give explicit (non-malleable) two source extractors for entropy $k \geq C n/\log n$ for some constant $C>1$ with $\Omega(k)$ output bits and error close to $2^{-\Omega(\sqrt{n})}$.
  An independent work of Doron and Goodman constructed explicit two-source extractors for entropy $k \geq n^{1-\alpha}$ with error $2^{-k^{\alpha}}$ for some constant $\alpha>0$. Their extractors work for smaller entropy than ours, while our extractors have better error and output length for any constant entropy rate. Our extractors for entropy $k \geq C n/\log n$ are obtained independently before we were aware of their results, while our extractors for constant entropy rate with asymptotically optimal parameters are obtained after we learned their unpublished results at the Simons Institute, using different ideas and techniques.

papers.title: A Fused Gaussian Process Bandit Framework for Multi-Fidelity Bayesian Optimization
papers.abstract: Bayesian optimization (BO) is widely used to maximize expensive black-box functions when direct evaluation is costly. In many real-world applications, the high-fidelity objective can be approximated by a series of lower-fidelity models that provide partial but informative signals at substantially reduced cost. Multi-fidelity BO (MFBO) algorithms aim to strategically combine these information sources to achieve an optimal trade-off between accuracy and evaluation cost. However, existing MFBO methods often oversimplify the complex dependencies between fidelity levels or rely on heuristic acquisition functions that lack theoretical performance guarantees. To address these limitations, we introduce a new formulation of the MFBO problem as a fused Gaussian Process bandit and develop a corresponding Fused Gaussian Process Upper Confidence Bound (FGP-UCB) algorithm. Our approach accurately predicts the high-fidelity function by fusing multi-fidelity observations through an autoregressive Gaussian Process model and explicitly quantifies the uncertainty arising from parameter estimation across fidelity levels. The proposed method also provides theoretical simple-regret guarantees, overcoming a key limitation of existing MFBO algorithms that lack provable performance bounds. Effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated via both theoretical analysis and empirical studies.

authors.name: Huazheng Wang
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: Self-Reference and Relative Incompleteness: From Logical Obstructions to Hardness Hypotheses
papers.abstract:
We define relative incompleteness and use it to provide a unified framework for G\"odelian incompleteness and the limits of local observations in finite SAT. A background is incomplete relative to a target question if two realizations compatible with that background give opposite answers. G\"odelian diagonalization yields a sentence whose truth value differs across two models of the same theory, while solution-dependent blocking yields two formulas that agree on the observed clauses but differ in satisfiability. Both constructions realize a common diagonal relation between truth and acceptance that forces a sound partial evaluator to leave the target undecided.
  For a satisfiable formula, replacing a single unobserved clause without changing its variable support can make the formula unsatisfiable exactly when all solutions remaining after deletion of that clause agree on its support. If the original formula has a unique solution, this condition is equivalent to redundancy of the clause. More generally, an observation of a satisfiable formula determines satisfiability exactly when it includes a position at which the formula differs from each unsatisfiable completion. For uniquely satisfiable formulas, the positions that every sufficient observation must include are precisely the redundant ones. We also arithmetize solution blocking and construct a tagged fixed point that refers to its own blocking data. Finally, we use self-referential $K$-SAT to illustrate how relative incompleteness can provide a logical foundation for formulating a quantitative hardness hypothesis.

authors.name: Ke Xu
authors.institution: Beijing National Research Center for Information Science and Technology

papers.title: PhysRF-WorldJEPA: Transforming Heterogeneous Large Language Models into Manifold-Decoupled Millimeter-Wave Radar World Models
papers.abstract: Adapting Large Language Models (LLMs) to millimeter-wave (mmWave) radar enables privacy-preserving, all-weather physical scene understanding across darkness, smoke, and walls. However, standard instruction tuning treats continuous radar streams as static text-like tokens, causing near-random global radar-to-text retrieval and severe physical drift under sensor blackouts. Conversely, coupling pairwise contrastive losses (e.g., SigLIP) directly into the shared backbone improves retrieval but injects $O(B^2)$ repulsive gradients that fracture continuous coordinate manifolds ($R^2 < 0$). We present PhysRF-WorldJEPA, a manifold-decoupled Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) that separates continuous electromagnetic state prediction from cross-modal language alignment. An unattenuated 1.0x clock anchor and parallel dual-scale RF encoder feed a lean ~3% LoRA LLM trained with two-step state-space EMA-JEPA (Denoise -> Rollout) and sample-axis Batch-VICReg to predict +3.0 s physical states; a stop-gradient alignment head then maps frozen prompt states onto the text hypersphere with false-negative masking. On a 4,541-window tri-domain suite (77/60.25/60 GHz) against 10 baselines, freezing the physical backbone and training only the decoupled head lifts R->T R@10 from 5.95% to 15.01% and improves MedRank from 107.0 to 60.0 while preserving identical physical readout: 3.37 deg ($R^2=+0.961$) blackout +3.0 s torso tilt, 1.89 m ($R^2=+0.679$; 1.19 m/+0.863 at the RF front-end) cluttered UAV altitude, 2.04 m ($R^2=+0.461$) behind-wall NLOS range, 0.9976 virtual-RIS invariance, and 100% fall recall. Across five 0.5B-1.8B LLM families (15 zero-overhead models), World-JEPA improves retrieval and 75%-drop completion in 10/10 runs and blackout tilt in 4/5 (Span-Euc), 2/5 (Scatter), and 5/5 (per-family best) over SFT.

papers.title: SCOPE: Evaluating and Enhancing Permission Explanation Transparency in Mobile Apps
papers.abstract: Permission explanations, explanatory text accompanying mobile app permission requests, are crucial for user privacy transparency and informed consent. Despite their importance, current practices often fall short of regulatory expectations due to the lack of systematic evaluation mechanisms. Through an empirical study of 600 mainstream mobile apps, we reveal widespread deficiencies: 15\% of permission requests provide no explanation, others use vague language or technical jargon, and critically, many fail to disclose third-party SDK data access despite these components actively using granted permissions. To address these transparency gaps, we present SCOPE, an automated multi-agent framework that systematically evaluates permission explanation compliance and generates targeted optimization recommendations. SCOPE employs four specialized agents working collaboratively: multimodal LLM-based explanation extraction, few-shot learning-based linguistic analysis, dynamic API-based purpose inference, and adaptive report generation. Comprehensive evaluation demonstrates SCOPE's effectiveness, achieving 98\% accuracy in explanation extraction, 93.5\% consistency in compliance analysis, and 92\% accuracy in purpose inference. A user study with 30 participants shows 84.6\% preference for SCOPE-optimized explanations, confirming practical utility. Our work provides the first systematic analysis of permission explanation practices and establishes a scalable solution for enhancing mobile app privacy transparency.

authors.name: Tianshu Zhou
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

authors.name: Haoyu Wang
authors.institution: Changchun University of Science and Technology

authors.name: Xiyuan Liu
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Organic-Inorganic Composite Materials

papers.title: EditText: Structure-Aware Generation and Selective Visual Transport for Fine-Grained Text Editing
papers.abstract: Fine-grained text editing aims to accurately replace text in a specified region while preserving the source text's font, color, and texture, as well as visual consistency in unedited regions. We present EditText, a unified framework for fine-grained text editing that combines target character generation with visual transport from the source image. The model uses dual-condition Fill inputs: a masked image and a source text style reference, both sharing a spatial reference with the target image. The masked image hides the original text and retains unedited content as a source canvas; the style reference supplies appearance cues that guide new character generation together with the target text. We introduce an Attention Transport framework in which Source Weight describes the attention allocated to a condition and the Spatial Aggregation Kernel describes its internal spatial attention distribution. Accurate transfer of source details depends on attention strength, the retention of details in condition features, and spatially accurate aggregation. For selected non-edit queries, we therefore preserve the total attention weight assigned to the masked image while redistributing its attention toward spatially corresponding neighborhoods, enabling selective visual transport. Multi-stage training, combined with a Glyph-aware Structural Loss on local target character structure, teaches the model to generate accurate text, preserve source text appearance, and retain unedited details. We also introduce TBench, a fine-grained text editing benchmark covering Alphabetic, Logographic, and Arabic numerals, to evaluate character updates, appearance preservation, and the preservation of unedited details. On TBench, EditText achieves state-of-the-art non-edit-region SSIM (0.9769) and full-image LPIPS (0.0460).

authors.name: Guandong Li
authors.institution: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Weak--viscosity equivalence for the fractional Trudinger equation
papers.abstract: We prove weak--viscosity equivalence for the fractional Trudinger equation $\partial_t(|u|^{p-2}u)+\mathcal L_{s,p}u=0$, where $1<p<\infty$ and $0<s<1$. The functions are assumed to be continuous in the equation domain and continuous in time with values in the weighted tail space. We treat both functions that are strictly positive in the equation domain, with signed exterior values, and globally nonnegative functions with interior zeros. Exterior values need not be bounded or spatially continuous. For $1<p<2$, the viscosity formulation tests the evolution variable $|u|^{p-2}u$, retaining the nonlocal interaction at zeros. The viscosity-to-weak implication follows from localized multiplicative regularization and energy estimates independent of a positive lower bound. The reverse implication uses comparison with smooth functions, justified by a relative-energy identity. A zero-slice property allows the weak identities on positive time intervals to be joined across the zero set.

authors.name: Qi Xue
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

authors.name: Chao Zhang
authors.institution: Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs

papers.title: Encrypted Fixed-Point Multiplication in Quasilinear Complexity
papers.abstract:
Homomorphic encryption enables computation on encrypted data, but its high computational overhead remains a central obstacle. We overcome this obstacle asymptotically for high-precision fixed-point arithmetic. In this paper, we introduce focused encoding, which represents a fixed-point number of $n$-bit precision using a polynomial of degree $O(n/\log n)$ over a polynomially bounded modulus by concentrating precision at one embedding. We then introduce an error-shaping technique for homomorphic operations to preserve the encoding. This yields an encrypted fixed-point multiplication algorithm for the CKKS scheme that runs in online time $O(n \log n)$ at $n$-bit precision for any fixed multiplicative depth, with security parameter $\lambda = O(n/\log^2 n)$.
  Further, we develop bootstrapping for focused encoding to overcome the quadratic cost of conventional bootstrapping. We bootstrap ciphertext coefficients at an enlarged scale and shape the resulting error to preserve focused encoding, at the cost of additional modulus consumption. Then, to reduce the remaining logarithmic overhead, we decompose the ciphertext into components over a smaller subring and bootstrap each separately. This reduces the online cost per multiplication, including bootstrapping, to $O(n \log n + n (\log \lambda)^3 \log \log \lambda)$ for security parameter $\lambda = O(n/\log^3 n)$.

papers.title: Strategic Beam Brainstorming for Generative Site-Specific Beamforming
papers.abstract: A novel plug-and-play candidate beam selection strategy is proposed for generative site-specific beamforming (GenSSBF), a paradigm that draws on a learned conditional channel distribution to generate multiple plausible beams. Under a limited probing budget, realizing the full potential of GenSSBF requires identifying which candidate beams are worth probing. To this end, the marginal probing value is first derived to guide strategic candidate probing by quantifying each beam's additional gain beyond those already selected. Based on this criterion, two algorithms are developed without retraining the generator: 1) Greedy candidate probing (GCP) selects all candidate beams from a locally generated pool prior to over-the-air probing, requiring only a single feedback round; 2) Adaptive candidate probing (ACP) exploits reference signal received power (RSRP) feedback after each probe to update channel hypothesis weights and guide the next beam selection, without increasing the asymptotic complexity. Simulations across three ray-tracing scenarios under noiseless and noisy probing reveal that: 1) candidate complementarity is key to efficient beam brainstorming; and 2) ACP is particularly beneficial when initial sensing leaves substantial channel uncertainty and subsequent feedback is reliable.

authors.name: Zihao Zhou
authors.institution: Qingdao University of Science and Technology

papers.title: A Unified Control Framework for Gradient Inversion Defense in Federated Learning
papers.abstract: Gradient perturbations are widely recognized as an effective defense against gradient inversion attacks in federated learning, but they are equally known to impair optimization, creating a persistent tension between privacy and utility. In this paper, we show that existing gradient perturbation defenses, despite their different formulations, can be unified under a controlled dynamics framework, providing a cohesive understanding of their optimization behavior and enabling the derivation of universal convergence and safety conditions without relying on case-specific analyses. Leveraging this observation, we propose ``Near Orthogonal Gradient Projection (NODE)'', which injects perturbations only along directions orthogonal to the original gradient so that the defended gradient maintains a fixed cosine similarity with the true gradient. By preserving the first-order descent direction, NODE substantially reduces the optimization cost of strong perturbations while maintaining effective protection against gradient inversion attacks. We theoretically establish convergence guarantees under standard optimization assumptions and further show that, under mild conditions on the gradient distribution, NODE remains effective in preventing inversion attacks. Comprehensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets, including CIFAR-10, ImageNet, and Chest X-ray, together with a variety of gradient inversion attacks, demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves an improved privacy--utility trade-off over existing defenses across a broad range of training settings.

papers.title: Wind-Aware Trajectory Planning for Deformable Aerial Formations
papers.abstract: Coordinated aerial transport in dense urban environments requires drone formations to navigate confined spaces and adapt to spatially varying winds around buildings. Formation deformation enables passage through narrow spaces but changes individual drone velocities and the local winds they encounter, coupling formation motion with aerodynamic effects. We propose Family-Air, a wind-aware trajectory-family planner that constructs a virtual tube as shared collision-free flight space and jointly optimizes formation-center motion, deformation, and timing. A shared affine transformation represents a continuous trajectory family, incorporating spatially varying wind and deformation-induced velocities into a unified air-relative motion objective. The optimization enforces virtual-tube containment, inter-drone separation, and kinematic feasibility. Simulations across four urban wind-field scenarios demonstrate the importance of local wind-deformation coupling. Flight simulations further show improvements in trajectory tracking accuracy. These results demonstrate the potential of wind-aware trajectory-family planning for coordinated aerial transport in complex urban environments.

papers.title: The backtrackless circuits of $D(k,q)$ obtained by lifting
papers.abstract: For integer $k\geq2$ and power $q$ of prime $p$, the algebraic bipartite graph $D(k,q)$, proposed by Lazebnik and Ustimenko in 1993, is $q$-regular, edge-transitive and of girth at least $k+4$. For $q\geq4$, it was conjectured in 1995 that the exact girth of $D(k,q)$, denoted by $g(D(k,q))$, is equal to $g_k$, where $g_k$ is defined as $k+5$ if $2\nmid k$ and as $k+4$ if $2|k$. It is now known that this conjecture is true when $g_k$ is of form $hp^t$, where $h$ is a factor of $4(q-1)$. Sun proved in her thesis (2017) that, for $n\not\equiv 1(\bmod\ 4)$, any backtrackless circuit (BC) of length $l$ in $D(n,q)$ can be lifted to BCs of length $pl$ in $D(k,q)$, where $k$ is $p(n+5)-5$ if $n\equiv 3(\bmod\ 4)$ and $p(n+4)-4$ otherwise. This result implies that, provided $g(D(n,q))=g_n$, we must have $g(D(k,q))=g_k$ for any $k$ in the set $\{p^sg_n-5|s\geq 0\}$ if $n\equiv 3(\bmod\ 4)$ and for any $k$ in the set $\{p^sg_n-5|s\geq 0\}\cup\{p^sg_n-4|s\geq 0\}$ otherwise, where $D(1,q)$ is defined as the graph $D(2,q)$ if any. Sun's proof for this result is simplified in this paper, with the help of some new automorphisms of the graph $D(k,q)$ that are combinations of the known ones. A new proof for this result is also given in the last section of this paper by using a class of homogeneous polynomials.

papers.title: Relation Before Action: Explicit Relation Modeling for Latent Action Pretraining
papers.abstract: Learning latent actions from unlabeled video sequences offers a promising way to acquire reusable action representations without relying on embodiment-specific control annotations. However, existing latent-action pretraining approaches commonly couple the modeling of visual transitions with action inference, directly mapping paired observations or derived transition cues into latent action codes. This formulation leaves two distinct tasks entangled: characterizing the relational structure of an observed transition and abstracting it into a compact action representation. We propose RELACT, a relation-first framework that explicitly separates transition relation modeling from predictive action abstraction. RELACT first constructs a structured relation representation $R$ that captures how visual elements and their interactions evolve across observations. It then infers a compact, state-conditioned stochastic latent action $U$, whose predictive effects are learned through action-conditioned latent dynamics. The resulting action representation can be grounded in native control spaces for model-based planning or used to supervise downstream embodied policies. Extensive experiments across in-domain and out-of-domain image-goal navigation, goal-conditioned manipulation, and downstream policy adaptation demonstrate improved predictive action representations and consistent gains in planning and control, supporting the effectiveness and generality of relation-first latent action pretraining.

authors.name: Boning Zhang
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology Beijing

authors.name: Junyu Gao
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology Liaoning

papers.title: Refining and Aligning Clinical Reasoning with Health Guidelines via Formal Constraints
papers.abstract: Clinical reasoning from incomplete or conflicting patient evidence must account for low-probability but high-risk concerns while remaining grounded in health guidelines. We introduce VerClin, an explainable framework that extracts guideline conditions, exclusions, recommendations, and priorities into executable knowledge and represents patient conversations as scoped cases. A deterministic four-valued reasoner produces traceable guideline matches while preserving uncertainty and enforcing exclusions. Multiple specialty agents then screen matched guidelines for case applicability, and a consultation model synthesizes accepted guidance through specialty recommendations and a sentence-preserving formal-constraint channel. We present accepted guidance in ascending order of the sum of its priority and trigger-strength ranks, which can surface high-risk guidance with weaker triggers. VerClin outperforms direct generation and Top-5 RAG on HealthBench Hard and HealthBench Professional. On the LLMEval-Med subset, it outperforms direct generation and ties Top-5 RAG. Component analyses further examine semantic closure, example-guided refinement, specialty screening, and constraint-conditioned delivery.

papers.title: Hochschild operations and other invariants of stable equivalences of Morita type
papers.abstract:
We study stable equivalences defined by bimodule tensor identities over a commutative ring $R$. For the $R$-split exact structure, these identities preserve positive Hochschild homology and positive Hochschild cohomology with its cup product, Gerstenhaber bracket and, in prime characteristic, restricted power. A triangular comparison also identifies the relative singular Hochschild cochain complexes as $B_\infty$-algebras. For reduced pairs of finite-dimensional Frobenius algebras over an algebraically closed field, with diagonalizable Nakayama automorphisms, we construct compatible Frobenius functionals and compare the Tate--Hochschild BV operators in all degrees.
  For flat algebras over $R$ we give a Hochschild-cohomological criterion for comparing marked associative deformations. It applies to biadjoint Morita-type pairs and, by reduction, to all stable equivalences of Morita type between finite-dimensional algebras over any field. We compare the Bezrukavnikov--Ginzburg maps in characteristic zero by using a common triangular deformation or by lifting a two-sided tilting complex. We also compare marked module deformations over local Artin rings and their augmented universal rings.
  Further applications concern connected outer automorphism group schemes over perfect fields, the kernels of the quotient maps on ordinary algebraic $K$-theory, and the nonconnective $K$-theory of enhanced relative singularity categories. We construct biadjoint representatives over Henselian Noetherian local rings and relative stable tensor functors for almost $\nu$-stable derived equivalences. We also answer a question of Abe and Hoshino about preservation of the Gorenstein condition in a fixed codimension.

papers.title: Mayfly: Lifecycle-Aware High-Bandwidth Flash for Recursive Self-Improvement
papers.abstract: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) lets an LLM improve its agent system by proposing and evaluating candidate variants across tasks. A generation's sessions grow their KV caches together and release them as they finish, creating a burst followed by a decline. At high concurrency, even the KV of sessions ready to run exceeds the GPU's HBM. Offloading that KV to host DRAM or SSDs adds capacity but leaves ready sessions waiting for HBM space before execution. High-Bandwidth Flash (HBF) can serve the overflow in place, but excessive reads lengthen decode steps and repeated writes consume flash endurance. Our key insight is that where ready KV is read should follow the burst and its decline: from HBF in place while the burst overflows HBM, as much as each step's bandwidth allows, and from HBM again as the decline frees it. A switch between ready and parked decides only whether a block is read, so its flash copy stays valid, and a session's end, which the orchestrator announces, decides when its private KV dies. We present Mayfly, lifecycle-guided HBF management for RSI. Mayfly bounds per-step HBF reads during overflow and returns KV to HBM as sessions finish and free space. It retains a valid backing copy of each block evicted from HBM to avoid rewrites across state transitions, and forwards session-end signals to the controller to avoid copying dead KV during garbage collection. Experimental results show that, at 128 sessions per generation on four added HBF sites, Mayfly finishes 34% sooner than parking the same KV on HBF and 23% sooner than reading it from HBF whenever HBM is full; its gain over parking grows with concurrency, to 55% at 256 sessions on eight sites. Keeping one flash copy per block and trimming at announced session ends avoid write amplification.

authors.name: Chunlin Tian
authors.institution: Changchun University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Online outlier-resilient data-driven moving horizon estimation for linear discrete-time systems
papers.abstract: This paper addresses data-driven state estimation for linear systems of which online output measurements may be corrupted by sparse outliers of arbitrary magnitude. Using only offline input-state-output data without explicitly identifying a system model, we propose an outlier-resilient data-driven moving horizon estimation scheme, termed OORD-MHE, based on Willems' fundamental lemma. The scheme employs a truncated-quadratic loss on the output residuals, parameterized by a truncation threshold, to mitigate the influence of online outliers. We establish sufficient conditions under which the resulting estimation error remains uniformly bounded. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed OORD-MHE scheme generates accurate state estimates in the presence of sparse online outliers.

papers.title: Reproducing the Speech Labels of Qwen3-Omni's Talker: Mimi in bf16, and a Last-Frame Pitfall
papers.abstract: Qwen3-Omni speaks through a Talker predicting 16 codebooks of a 12.5 Hz audio codec, but the encoder that made its training labels was not released, so new voices cannot be trained on matching labels. We identify this encoder from the released model's behavior. White-box regression shows that the codebook embeddings of the Talker, its multi-token predictor and the Code2Wav decoder match the first 16 codebooks of kyutai's Mimi layer by layer. A decoder-based test looks convincing but fails calibration: decoders trained on known labels cannot tell them apart. Teacher-forced Talker likelihoods, calibrated with 13 code language models trained on known labels, do tell implementations apart: the Talker prefers labels from kyutai's moshi package with bf16 weights over every other variant we tried. Loudness normalization and band-limiting of 20% or more of the data are ruled out. Separately, transformers' MimiModel encodes the last frame differently from kyutai's encoder unless the input length is a multiple of 1920 samples. After LoRA fine-tuning on its labels, 44--55% of generated sentences end in a noise burst, and the same frame costs the Mimi-based CSM-1B 119 nats; padding the input removes both. We release the encoding recipe, a label checker and a Talker fine-tuning toolkit.

papers.title: A proof of the toughness conjecture for Kneser graphs
papers.abstract: As a measure of the connectivity of graphs, Chv\'atal \cite{Chvatal} introduced the concept of toughness. For integers $k\geq2$ and $n\geq2k+1$, the Kneser graph $\KG(n,k)$ has all the $k$-subsets of $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$ as its vertices, and two vertices are adjacent if they are disjoint. Cioab\u{a} and Wong~\cite{CW} determined the toughness of $\KG(n,2)$. Park et al.~\cite{Park} determined the toughness of $\KG(n,k)$ when $k=3,4$ and $k\geq5$ for large $n$. They \cite{Park} proposed a conjecture for $k\geq5$ and other values of $n$. In this paper, we resolve this conjecture.

papers.title: Delay-Tolerant Formation Tracking for Multi-AGV Systems via Reference-Shift Coupling
papers.abstract: Automated guided vehicles (AGVs) that transport a load together must keep a formation while each vehicle tracks its own reference, and they coordinate over wireless links with link-dependent, time-varying and jumping delays. We propose a cascade design for differential-drive AGVs modelled as kinematic unicycles: delayed data from the neighbours drive only a second-order filter that shifts each vehicle's own reference, and an unmodified gain-scheduled tracking law follows the shifted reference. A saturation keeps the shifted reference feasible, and the feed-forward is exact, so the tracking loop never sees the network. We prove that tracking and formation errors remain bounded for arbitrary delays and converge for every bounded delay and every directed, possibly switching, graph. We also construct a strict Lyapunov function with explicit constants and prove exponential convergence and a local input-to-state estimate with delay-independent gains. On undirected graphs, the coupling attenuates the formation error caused by persistent local errors by at least the factor lambda/(lambda+Lambda*lambda_2(L)) (leak lambda, coupling gain Lambda, algebraic connectivity lambda_2(L)), for any delay. Every inequality is verified with an event-driven, error-controlled simulation. A robustness study on a high-fidelity AGV model (drive dynamics, slip, localisation errors, clock offsets, lossy Wi-Fi) comprises 4,894 runs, including paired comparisons against tuned baselines. The cascade never failed, with latencies up to 4 s, 90% packet loss and up to 12 vehicles, whereas a direct delayed coupling failed when its gain saturated the drives. Coupling reduced the formation error after traction losses by 21-32% and after safety stops by up to 47%, at the price of tracking accuracy. Localisation bias and clock offsets, which no coupling law can observe, limit the achievable accuracy.

papers.title: Shock formation in traffic flow models with Arrhenius look-ahead interactions
papers.abstract: We study finite-time shock formation in a nonlocal traffic flow model with Arrhenius look-ahead dynamics. For the constant interaction potential, we derive a time-dependent lower bound for the minimum slope and obtain a sufficient condition with logarithmic dependence on the magnitude of the minimum initial slope. For the linear interaction potential with look-ahead distance $\gamma$, we show that the condition $u'_0(x_0)>\frac{1}{\gamma}$ at a single point is sufficient for shock formation, which is independent of the minimum initial slope. Our results strictly improve the corresponding conditions of Lee and Liu \cite{r17}.

papers.title: A Star is Reborn: The PHP Interpreter Rewritten in Safe Rust
papers.abstract:
PHP powers most of the web, yet its C interpreter has had many memory-safety vulnerabilities. Reimplementing the interpreter in safe Rust offers a promising way to eliminate these vulnerabilities. However, eliminating native memory violations alone does not necessarily prevent unintended accesses to the logical memory of the translated program.
  To prevent such failures, we introduce logical memory safety, which confines the program operations to their permitted memory. In this paper, we formalize this property for PHP through an abstract PHP machine model that captures how the PHP interpreter manages program values while abstracting away functionality details. Guided by this model, we reimplement the PHP 5.0.0 engine in safe Rust, and formally prove that, for a core fragment of PHP, our Rust translation refines the abstract PHP machine, thereby establishing logical memory safety for this fragment.
  Our translation safely handles all 173 memory vulnerabilities we collected that affect PHP 5.0.0 prior to the rewrite. The Rust version matches the C implementation on all functionality tests, and produces identical outputs for the real-world PHP applications we evaluate. To our knowledge, this is the first principled safe Rust port of a core fragment of the PHP interpreter that combines formal guarantees of logical memory safety with functional compatibility. The improved security comes at a modest average runtime overhead of only 15% compared to C.

papers.title: COHERE4D: Training-Free Dense Surface Alignment for Coherent Metric 4D Human-Scene Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Human and scene foundation models offer complementary strengths for monocular 4D reconstruction: human models recover metric-scale body meshes but lack scene grounding, whereas scene models estimate globally consistent 3D geometry and camera motion without reliable metric scale. Crucially, both models reconstruct the same foreground human surface. Yet existing methods do not directly exploit this shared surface: lacking reliable foreground human geometry in scene reconstructions, earlier approaches either resort to sparse contact constraints or learn data-driven alignment modules that generalize poorly to out-of-distribution scenes. We present COHERE4D, a training-free framework that directly registers the human surfaces predicted by independently pretrained human and scene foundation models to reconstruct a coherent, metric 4D world. COHERE4D establishes dense, pixel-aligned 3D correspondences over the visible human surface and employs RANSAC with cross-frame consensus to suppress outliers from occlusion, background contamination, and depth noise. This formulation solves for two complementary geometric quantities: a sequence-level shared scale that calibrates scene geometry and camera motion to metric human size, and per-frame human translations that align camera-space human meshes with the scaled scene geometry to enforce spatial and temporal consistency. Across diverse backbones and benchmarks, COHERE4D substantially outperforms prior methods in human--scene alignment, metric scene and camera pose reconstruction, and global human motion estimation, adding only 4,ms/frame, enabling overall inference at up to 14 FPS.

authors.name: Shaofei Wang
authors.institution: Merchants Chongqing Communications Research and Design Institute

papers.title: Integral Hodge/Tate conjecture of quotients via weak approximation
papers.abstract: For a finite group acting on a smooth projective separably rationally connected variety over an algebraically closed field, we prove that the rational quotient map induces a surjection from the coinvariants of its second Kato homology onto the second Kato homology of any smooth projective quotient model (with coefficients invertible in the ground field). The integral Hodge and Tate conjectures for one-cycles consequently descend to such quotient models. The proof uses weak approximation over function fields to retain the image of a smooth fiber in the total space.

authors.name: Yang Cao
authors.institution: Hunan University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

papers.title: Reliability-aware AI Agent Execution in Collaborative Edge Computing: A World Model Approach
papers.abstract: Collaborative edge computing supports AI agent applications by distributing execution across heterogeneous user-controlled devices with limited resources. This paper studies reliability-aware AI agent execution under node failures and wireless disruptions. These disruptions can make agent execution state unavailable or inconsistent, forcing recovery or recomputation that consumes the remaining deadline budget. Maintaining recoverable execution states can therefore improve request completion before deadlines. We formulate an online AI agent execution management problem that jointly selects resource allocations, state protection actions, and recovery targets to maximize the expected task success rate subject to resource, compatibility, and deadline constraints. We develop a world model that jointly captures evolving agent workflows and recoverable execution state under candidate management actions, accounting for node reliability, network conditions, and resource availability. The model enables the controller to simulate future execution and recovery trajectories under candidate actions and estimate their effects on execution progress and task completion before deadlines. We then employ world model-based model predictive control (WorldMPC) with Monte Carlo rollouts to jointly optimize resource allocation, state protection, and recovery decisions for long-term reliable agent execution under the dynamic environment. We evaluate the proposed approach on the simulation and real-world testbed using real-world and synthetic datasets. Experimental results show that WorldMPC improves task success rate over baselines in both simulation and real-world testbed.

papers.title: RePrism: Joint Request and Representation Scheduling for LLM Agent Serving
papers.abstract: Agentic workflows often invoke large language models multiple times. When the dependencies are visible to the serving system, it can use them to schedule requests and cache reusable content, improving workflow execution efficiency. Prior work has largely focused on ordering requests or managing shared resources under a fixed caching scheme. A reusable prompt that specifies model behavior, however, can have multiple representations. We present RePrism, a serving system that jointly selects which ready request to serve and which eligible representation of its prompt to use. Its goal is to improve throughput and shorten session completion time (SCT). The scheduler ranks pairs of requests and representations by combining each pair's immediate value with an estimate of its future value based on the visible workflow. The resource manager allocates GPU memory to both LoRA adapters and cached key-value states. It also coordinates their admission and eviction as memory pressure changes. We compare RePrism with S-LoRA on a dynamic workload with an arrival rate of 1.8 sessions per second, and it achieves 1.37 times the request throughput and reduces P95 SCT by a factor of 4.10. Under controlled load, RePrism reduces mean time to first token by a factor of 5.26 relative to S-LoRA. On a controlled workload, RePrism's joint scoring achieves 2.7% higher request throughput and 12.3% lower mean SCT than a policy that ranks requests before selecting their representations.

papers.title: Arithmetic Siegel-Weil formulas for unitary Shimura varieties with Iwahori levels
papers.abstract: In this paper, we formulate conjectural formulas for the arithmetic intersection numbers of special cycles on unitary Shimura varieties with Iwahori level structure. We first introduce a framework for formulating Kudla-Rapoport conjectures: we develop the theory of weighted representation densities and special cycles for general parahoric level structures, prove dimension-reduction formulas on both the analytic and geometric sides and duality relations for special cycles. We then formulate the Kudla-Rapoport conjecture for Iwahori level structures based on these properties. Finally, we prove the conjecture when $n=2$.

papers.title: ST-GNN-AAAS: Spatio-Temporal Graph Neural Networks for Anytime Automatic Algorithm Selection in the Traveling Salesman Problem
papers.abstract: Anytime Automatic Algorithm Selection (AAAS) aims to make solver choices under varying time budgets. The existing AAAS approaches largely rely on static instance characteristics and make limited use of temporal information revealed during solver execution. We propose ST-GNN-AAAS, a Spatio-Temporal Graph Neural Network framework for AAAS in the Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP). The framework represents evolving incumbent tours using time-varying node features, including distances from each node to its neighbors in the current tour, and combines these features with solver performance observations over a short history window. Given this short history, ST-GNN-AAAS predicts solver selections over a longer future horizon. We evaluate the method on a subset of diverse TSP benchmarks from NATIONAL, TNM, TSPLIB, and VLSI, releasing the corresponding solver execution data to support reproducibility. Our model achieves a selection accuracy of 76.59% and closes 46.05% of the average rank gap between the single best solver (SBS) and the virtual best solver (VBS).

papers.title: Constrained Allen-Cahn phase-field topology optimization of flexoelectric devices
papers.abstract: Topology optimization provides an effective approach to exploring performance-oriented designs for miniature devices. In this work, a phase-field framework for constrained topology optimization of microscale flexoelectric devices is developed using a continuum model under the assumption of infinitesimal deformations. The material distribution is optimized at the device level with the output voltage as the objective. The framework also accommodates objectives based on capacitance or stored electrostatic energy. Manufacturing variations are incorporated through a worst-case objective over the prescribed geometric realizations, with spectral constraints imposed to maintain the structural connectivity. The framework is applied to two-dimensional pressure and bending sensors and a three-dimensional thin-film device. The optimized nominal output voltages reach approximately 4.8 times the initial value for the pressure sensor and 2.5-3.4 times the initial values for the bending sensors. The voltage gains arise primarily from increased mechanically induced source charge, with capacitance reduction providing an additional contribution that varies with the device configuration. Erosion analyses of representative designs further show that structural connectivity is well preserved when structural members become locally narrower, with the output voltage remaining close to that of the nominal configuration. Combined with specific microfabrication processes, this optimization framework is expected to provide a numerical basis for configuration screening and prototype development of flexoelectric devices.

papers.title: Constraining the Binary Fraction and Mass-Ratio Distribution of FGK Dwarfs with Gaia XP Spectra: Metallicity, $\alpha$-Element, and Age Dependencies
papers.abstract: We present a study of the binary fraction and mass-ratio distribution for near 200,000 FGK dwarf stars within 1 kpc, utilizing the Stellar Locus Outlier (SLOT) method applied to synthetic Gaia XP photometry and stellar parameters from LAMOST DR9. By modeling the asymmetric color residuals relative to a metallicity-dependent single-star locus, we measure the binary fraction $f_b$ and constrain the power-law slope $\gamma_{\rm large\,q}$ of the mass-ratio distribution at high mass ratio $q$. Higher metallicity is associated with a steeper (more negative) $\gamma_{{\rm large}q}$, indicating a larger proportion of low-mass-ratio systems. For $\alpha$-elements, [Mg/H] and [Si/H] are anticorrelated with $f_b$ in thin-disk-dominated subsamples; conversely, [Ca/H] shows a positive correlation with $f_b$ in thin-disk-dominated subsamples. No correlation is found between $f_b$ and $\alpha$-element abundances in thick-disk-dominated subsamples. The binary fraction increases modestly toward older ages in the thin-disk population, a trend that likely reflects underlying correlations with chemistry. Our results shed light on how chemical composition and dynamical processes shape the binary properties of solar-type stars.

authors.name: Jia-Hui Wang
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Simultaneous Inference for Watermark Proportions in LLM-Generated Text
papers.abstract: Watermarking enables detection of text generated by large language models, but practical review also requires quantifying retained signals within content of interest. Readers may choose passages based on their content and refine their selections after examining the watermark evidence. We develop simultaneous lower confidence bounds on the fraction of selected tokens that retain a watermark signal. The bounds hold jointly for the full document and any passages selected during review. We develop structure-adaptive closed testing (SACT), which uses a working model of sequential signal clustering to construct scores for calibrated sign-based tests. Under a conditional null model, the bounds have finite-sample simultaneous validity even when the working model is misspecified. An exact reference-family representation recovers the full closed-testing bounds while enabling efficient repeated queries. In a constructed database-recovery review, SACT detects document-wide watermark signals and provides lower confidence bounds on watermark proportions in selected passages. Assessing related passages together gives a sharper lower bound on their combined signal count. In simulations spanning two watermarking mechanisms and a range of signal strengths and densities, SACT generally has higher power than competing methods.

papers.title: Two-Scale Diffusion Approximations for Many-Server Queues with Overdispersed Arrivals
papers.abstract: We study steady-state diffusion approximations for a many-server queue driven by overdispersed arrivals from a doubly stochastic Poisson process. Its arrival intensity follows a generalized Cox--Ingersoll--Ross (CIR) process, where $\alpha \in [0, 1)$ governs how the arrival-count variance scales as $\lambda^{1+\alpha}$ with the baseline arrival rate $\lambda$ under Taylor's law. For $\alpha > 0$, arrival-intensity fluctuations grow faster with $\lambda$ than counting fluctuations from arrivals and departures, so normalizing by $\lambda^{(1+\alpha)/2}$ pairs a nonvanishing intensity volatility with a vanishing queue-length volatility. This two-scale formulation differs critically from conventional diffusion approximations, which either apply a single $\lambda^{1/2}$ scaling with nonvanishing volatilities or drop the vanishing queue-length noise in the heavy-traffic limit. Retaining both scales, we compare two diffusions: one replaces the scaled intensity with its limiting Ornstein--Uhlenbeck (OU) process, and the other preserves the exact CIR intensity. Using Stein's method, we establish steady-state error bounds for smooth test functions of arbitrary polynomial growth that depend on $\alpha$ in opposite directions. Both diffusions achieve the classical $O(\lambda^{-1/2})$ rate at $\alpha = 0$. For $\alpha \in (0, 1)$, however, the OU rate degrades to the sharp order $O(\lambda^{-(1-\alpha)/2})$, whereas preserving the CIR intensity improves the rate to $O(\lambda^{-(2+\alpha)/4})$. Our proofs establish new derivative bounds for the associated Poisson equations that remain valid when the diffusion has vanishing volatility and nonsmooth drift.

authors.name: Xiaowei Zhang
authors.institution: Southern University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Path-probability gradients for optimizing force fields against dynamical observables
papers.abstract: Machine learning force fields inherit the errors of the electronic-structure methods used to generate their training data, and refining them against experimental measurements provides a direct route beyond this limit. However, such refinement remains difficult for dynamical observables because differentiating chaotic molecular trajectories yields unstable gradients. Here, we introduce PathGrad, which differentiates Langevin path probabilities instead of the trajectories themselves. The resulting gradient estimator is accumulated on the fly from thermal noise and force derivatives, and its variance remains stable as the trajectory length increases. We validated the gradient estimator against finite-difference calculations and used it to fine-tune molten-copper and water potentials against experimental diffusion coefficients together with structural constraints. For water, jointly optimizing diffusion and the oxygen-oxygen radial distribution function also improves the predictions of shear viscosity and rotational relaxation, neither of which is included in the optimization objective. Alignment at a single temperature also improves the apparent activation energies of multiple dynamical observables, bringing their temperature dependences closer to experiments. Moreover, the optimized potential exhibits smaller force errors relative to an independent, higher-level quantum-chemical reference, indicating that alignment with experiments improves the fidelity of the potential energy surface beyond the fitted targets. PathGrad thus establishes a general framework for incorporating experimental observables directly into force field optimizations.

papers.title: CityRecast: Suppressing Persistent Artifacts in Generative Satellite 3D Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Satellite-based 3D reconstruction is limited by sparse observations and changes across acquisition dates. Existing methods use generative priors to recover missing visual detail, but ghosting, streaking, and blur persist in their Gaussian scenes. These artifacts become particularly apparent in low-elevation renderings. We introduce CityRecast to suppress these artifacts through Gaussian scene repair and supervision calibration. To correct the Gaussian distributions that produce these artifacts, we first use multi-angle warm-up to constrain their spatial extent. This reduces the initial ghosting carried into progressive refinement. Surface-guided replacement then continues to repair the Gaussian distribution while preserving existing appearance. To provide more reliable supervision for this process, observation calibration mitigates interference from multi-temporal observations. Joint refinement further reduces conflicts among generated views. Experiments on DFC2019 and IARPA demonstrate reduced artifacts in low-elevation renderings while maintaining satellite-view fidelity. Compared with Skyfall-GS, CityRecast reduces FID-CLIP by 25.3% on DFC2019 and 51.8% on IARPA. MUSIQ increases by 14.54 and 24.95 points, respectively.

authors.name: Shuo Cui
authors.institution: University of Chinese Academy of Sciences

papers.title: Fresh Keys, Stale Secrets: Numeric Leakage across Linked LLM Prompts
papers.abstract: Small businesses repeatedly ask cloud language models about the same confidential prices, unit costs and margins. Numeric prompt disguises for such numbers are evaluated one prompt at a time, but a provider sees a firm's history, in which each fresh secret gives a new, independent view of the same numbers. Since real costs are not public, we measure on synthetic firms with known values how much an honest-but-curious provider recovers when it knows the disguise algorithm, holds sector-level price and margin statistics, and links a firm's queries. In one prompt, per-field scaling, a fixed-axis instantiation of Zhang et al.'s order-preserving substitution and Pr$\varepsilon\varepsilon$mpt's released sanitizer keep the attacker's margin-hit advantage over a prior-only guess between -0.6 and +4.4 percentage points. After 16 linked queries with fresh secrets, every disguise we test (Pr$\varepsilon\varepsilon$mpt at $\varepsilon\geq 0.5$) has a target recovered significantly more often: under the order-preserving substitution, margin recovery rises from 25.0% to 59.4%. The same attacker recovers 29.4 percentage points more margins with fresh maps than with one reused map. Theory explains the contrast: one reused secret bounds all queries by a single full-precision view of the fields shown, whereas fresh scaling keys are identifiable. Except for Pr$\varepsilon\varepsilon$mpt at $\varepsilon=0.5$, the gains persist when the attacker's prior comes from another population model and when values drift by up to 5% between queries; on our firms, whose prose cues are weak, reading the prose with a language model adds at most 2.5 points. Code and data: https://github.com/Jamli58/fresh-keys-stale-secrets

papers.title: Regression calibration for logistic regression with correlated measurement error and multiple misclassification in covariates
papers.abstract: Epidemiological analyses often suffer from covariate data quality issues: measurement error in continuous predictors and misclassification of categorical variables. Existing logistic regression correction methods mostly handle only one error type or a single misclassified variable, with limited tools for multiple misclassified categorical exposures together with correlated measurement error in continuous covariates. To address this gap, we extend regression calibration for logistic regression to jointly accommodate multiple continuous covariates with correlated additive measurement error and two or more misclassified categorical predictors. We build a unified framework integrating additive measurement error models and misclassification transition matrices, deriving the regression calibration estimator (RCE) using Kronecker product algebra. This computationally feasible approach extends naturally to more than two misclassified categorical variables. We evaluate RCE via simulations across varied misclassification rates, error magnitudes, sample sizes and effect sizes, comparing it with the naive estimator that ignores measurement error. We apply RCE to the EPIC-InterAct male case-cohort data to adjust for correlated error in protein and energy intake, plus misclassification in binary physical activity and three-category alcohol consumption. Results show that neglecting these error sources produces substantial bias and misleading inference for main and interaction effects in nutritional epidemiology. While the RCE is a practical correction tool, it treats validation nuisance parameters as known and does not account for their estimation uncertainty.

authors.institution: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Global regularities for the Dirichlet problem of Monge-Amp\`ere type equations
papers.abstract: We establish global a priori $W^{2,p}$ and $C^{2,\alpha}$ estimates for elliptic solutions of the Dirichlet problem for cost-generated Monge-Amp\`ere type equations under the weak Ma-Trudinger-Wang condition A3w, assuming continuous and H\"older continuous right-hand sides, respectively.

authors.name: Jian Lu
authors.institution: Shenyang National Laboratory for Materials Science

papers.title: Motion Conditioned World Modeling for Embodied Visual Tracking
papers.abstract: World models support embodied decision-making by predicting future environment states. In embodied visual tracking, uncertain target motion and robot-induced viewpoint changes jointly affect visual observations, making future-state prediction challenging. We propose Motion-Conditioned World Modeling, which incorporates predicted target-motion distributions and robot ego-motion into latent state transitions. A Geometry--Progress module jointly models geometric paths and single-step travel distances through shared motion modes and path-conditioned progress distributions. This formulation captures uncertainty in route selection and motion progress while preserving their dependence. Action-induced coordinate transformations express predicted paths in the next robot frame, providing geometrically grounded conditions for future visual-state prediction. Future visual feature reconstruction supervises the motion predictor through the conditioned transition branch, linking explicit motion representations to subsequent observations. The model is jointly optimized with motion likelihood, feature reconstruction, and expert-action supervision, enabling the tracking policy to combine visual context with predictive motion cues.Experiments on three embodied tracking benchmarks demonstrate improved tracking performance and cross-environment generalization with a lightweight $0.5$B backbone.

authors.name: Jiahao Zhang
authors.institution: Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences & Peking Union Medical College

authors.name: Junyu Gao
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology Liaoning

papers.title: LoomKV: Lossless KV Cache Compression from GPU Memory to SSD for LLM Serving
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) serving engines offload the key/value (KV) cache from GPU memory to host DRAM and SSD so multi-turn and agent requests can reuse prompt prefixes. Capacity then limits service at two levels: external tiers govern prefix reuse before eviction, while the GPU KV pool bounds concurrent long requests, and lossy compression alters KV values and outputs. LoomKV brings lossless KV compression to both external tiers (tier mode) and the GPU pool (pool mode) on an unmodified engine. Using a calibrated per-head two-level 3-bit code over BF16 high bytes (sign and upper seven exponent bits), LoomKV stores BF16 KV at 0.71 of its raw size across nine models and FP8 KV at 0.85-0.87. In tier mode, TileStream writes exact-length records with length readback off the load path, leaving tier storage, eviction, and prefetch unchanged, and decompresses fetched records straight into scattered GPU pages. In pool mode, FragPack packs variable-length records into smaller shared-budget GPU pages read in place by a fused decode-attention kernel faster than FlashAttention-3 on BF16. Built with LMCache and vLLM, LoomKV makes compressed tiers act as 1.4x larger raw tiers on AgentX: across LMCache's LRU cliff, tier mode delivers 2.7-3.6x raw's goodput and 1.9-3.1x lower mean time-to-first-token (TTFT), shifts the cliff identically under other simulated replacement policies, and cuts repeated-prompt TTFT up to 1.7x via SSD-to-DRAM promotion. When tiers hold the working set, pool mode fits 1.31-1.34x as many GPU tokens, admitting 12 long requests with roughly raw's queue and goodput at 8. On an AI IDE trace where both tiers and the GPU pool are constrained, tier and pool modes raise goodput by 1.24x and 1.59x. Where raw capacity suffices, compression costs at most 2.2% throughput; tier mode is bit-exact with raw tiers, and pool mode matches FlashAttention-3's numerical accuracy.

authors.name: Wentao Zhu
