papers.title: CAPER: PartGround and PlanRefine for Reliable Manual-Guided Robotic Assembly Planning
papers.abstract: Vision-Language-Models (VLMs) used in robot task planning to derive assembly procedures from existing manuals may correctly interpret individual assembly actions yet confuse exact part identities, predict unsupported Part IDs, or produce inconsistent parts across assembly steps. Thus, we propose CAPER (Capacity-Aware Part-grounding and Evidence Refinement), a manual-guided robotic assembly framework that enables VLMs to generate assembly procedures with two modules--PartGround and PlanRefine. PartGround aligns step-level manual evidence with product-specific inventory and part-reference information to identify exact Part IDs and quantities, transforming free-form hardware prediction into evidence-guided assignments represented in a shared Assembly Intermediate Representation (Assembly IR). PlanRefine audits PartGround assignments against finite inventory by removing the lowest-confidence assignments. Uncertain identity cases remain marked for review in the Assembly IR. We evaluate CAPER on the IKEA Assembly in the Wild (IAW) dataset. Experiment results show that CAPER reaches a Finite-inventory Consistency Rate of 83.33% and produces zero observed out-of-inventory Part-ID occurrences. At the plan level, PlanRefine removes all observed inventory-overuse pairs (9 -> 0) and excess units (51 -> 0). Overall, the results indicate that PartGround and PlanRefine improve part reliability, while also enhancing finite-inventory consistency and local prediction accuracy. Project page and video: https://xhzzzz123.github.io/CAPER/

papers.title: LEGOSpec: A Composable and Efficient Framework for Speculative Draft Design and Training
papers.abstract: Speculative decoding accelerates large language model (LLM) generation using a lightweight draft. Existing methods evaluate complete recipes under different training configurations, leaving component effects, interactions, and composition benefits unclear. Therefore, we present LEGOSpec, a composable framework for speculative draft design and training. LEGOSpec decomposes draft models into Context, Backbone, Proposal, and Objective components that share a unified training infrastructure. Using LEGOSpec, we systematically vary components and evaluate selected combinations under matched training conditions to isolate their effects and interactions. These experiments reveal three findings: (1) Different workloads favor different backbones, depending on context length and memory budget, with within-block dependency modeling particularly important for long contexts. (2) Proposal design must balance acceptance and latency. (3) The training objective should match token distributions locally and optimize acceptance length across the block. These findings guide workload-aware configurations and DFlux, a balanced general-purpose draft combining a convolution-equipped SWA--GQA hybrid backbone, Residual Corrector, and hierarchical supervision. Across Qwen and Gemma models, DFlux improves acceptance length over the strongest baseline by up to 13.7% on regular benchmarks and 34.7% on long-context workloads. To support efficient training, LEGOSpec integrates metadata-aware scheduling and asynchronous execution, increasing training throughput by up to 79% and accelerating offline supervision preparation by up to $3.11\times$ over SpecForge.

authors.name: Hanzhen Wang
authors.institution: Changchun University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Shifter Quantization: Compact Representations for Native Integer Computation
papers.abstract: Groupwise quantization is used in LLM quantization to improve accuracy at low bit widths, but grouping weights keeps standard integer MMA from spanning the full dot product for efficient GPU inference. We develop a new quantization method, Shifter Quantization (SQ), that reconstructs native-width integer operands by appending and shifting shared bits. To further extend the efficiency, we develop a special variant of SQ, Shifter Integer (SHI), to use INT4 kernels. We show that SQ and SHI formats perform better than standard groupwise quantization in quality, as measured by projection error and KL divergence, and in inference speed, as measured during decoding and prefill. For low precision like 2-bit quantization, SQ2 and SHI2 achieve 2.71-3.77x the 4,096-token prefill throughput of llama.cpp on a Q2_K checkpoint and reduce WikiText-2 KL by 6.6-7.8%. For mid precision like 4-bit quantization, SQ4 achieves 1.43-2.47x the prefill throughput of NInfer's groupwise-integer baselines across the tested models and prompt lengths, with 24-40% lower KL than the NInfer baselines. For high precision like 8-bit quantization, SQ8 achieves 27.4% higher batch-one prefill throughput and 72.7% lower KL than vLLM's online FP8.

papers.title: Classification of spin space groups and crystal magnetic orders
papers.abstract: Spin space groups (SSGs) describe magnetic crystals in the limit of negligible spin-orbit coupling, where spatial and spin rotations decouple. Although algebraic enumerations of SSGs exist, their abstract mathematical approaches obscure the physical meaning of the resulting classifications, leaving the direct correspondence between SSGs and real-space magnetic orders unestablished. Here, we present a physically motivated framework for enumerating and classifying SSGs based on their translation holonomy---the image of the spatial lattice translation group under the spin homomorphism. The three classes of abelian images in $SO(3)$ divide SSGs into three basic translation types. Translation holonomy constrains the spin operations associated with point-group elements, yielding a complete enumeration of SSGs organized by a physical hierarchy. Within this framework, translation holonomy classifies SSGs and magnetic orders into 17 universal spin-lattice types, each with unambiguous Bragg-peak geometries and polarization signatures in neutron diffraction. Beyond organizing known magnetic orders, this framework directly predicts four universal physical phenomena: (i) exact magnetization compensation enforced by certain spin-lattice types; (ii) an exact group-theoretic criterion for the emergence of noncommuting Brillouin zones; (iii) a new type of 3Q magnetic order with vanishing octupoles; and (iv) the realization of strictly collinear momentum-space spin textures protected by reflection-staggered coplanar spin lattices. We also construct a spin space group database organized according to this physical hierarchy.

authors.name: Y. X. Zhao
authors.institution: National Natural Science Foundation of China

papers.title: MetaFORGE: A Meta-Learning Framework for Harness Optimization in Automated Code Generation for Parallel Computing
papers.abstract:
Large language models (LLMs) can generate parallel programs, but their correctness and performance depend strongly on the instructions that guide generation. We present \textsc{MetaFORGE}, an execution-grounded meta-learning framework that iteratively optimizes persistent natural-language skill specifications for MPI C code generation. \textsc{MetaFORGE} combines correctness testing, compiler diagnostics, static-analysis findings, runtime measurements, and rank-level load-imbalance profiles into a scalar reward that drives textual-gradient refinement, while an external memory distills and retrieves reward-supported optimization knowledge across runs.
  Across six MPI tasks and three workload sizes, \textsc{MetaFORGE} improves static-analysis quality, runtime, and load balance relative to zero-shot generation and generally exceeds the evaluated \textsc{TextGrad} iterative baseline. A model-matched refinement ablation shows that the MetaFORGE advantage persists when its refinement model is reduced to \texttt{gpt-4o}. An expanded retrieval ablation across all 18 task--workload configurations shows consistent runtime benefit and broad static-analysis and load-balance benefit from retrieved context. Leakage-controlled held-out and zero-update experiments further provide evidence that optimization knowledge persists in both the transferred skill and external memory under the evaluated protocol.

authors.name: Shenyang Liu
authors.institution: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications

papers.title: SAG-Mem-1.0 Technical Report
papers.abstract: Long-term conversational memory requires retrieving complementary facts scattered across dialogue sessions, including intermediate evidence with limited similarity to the original question. Existing approaches often rely on derived memory representations or persistent relational structures, introducing construction costs and potentially losing source details. We present SAG-Mem, a conversational memory framework that preserves complete dialogue messages in non-overlapping chunks and discovers complementary evidence through query-time lexical expansion. Memory construction requires no model inference, using a lexical index without LLM-based extraction, summarization, or semantic relation construction. At query time, BM25 retrieves initial candidates, an evidence evaluator identifies useful chunks, and lexical cues from selected evidence guide an additional retrieval round. Retrieved dialogue is further annotated with calendar interpretations of supported relative-time expressions, preserving the original wording and temporal granularity. We also introduce SAG-Mem-Lite, an alternative configuration that replaces evidence scoring with embedding-based candidate scoring, achieving lower operational cost than Full Context and all memory-based baselines across both benchmarks with low query latency. On LoCoMo and LongMemEval, SAG-Mem achieves overall scores of 83.08 and 80.20, respectively, the highest among the evaluated methods on both benchmarks. On LongMemEval, it exceeds the strongest compared baseline by 7.20 points. SAG-Mem-Lite achieves scores of 77.09 and 77.20, respectively. These results support dialogue preservation and evidence-guided retrieval expansion as an effective design for long-term conversational memory.

papers.title: Recognizing potentially planar degree sequences
papers.abstract: Testing for a simple planar realization is strongly NP-complete even on graphic $n$-term degree lists of minimum degree at least three and sum $6n-12$. Two $13$-vertex triangulations have sorted degree lists whose midpoint is graphic and has no planar realization, ruling out a characterization by simultaneous affine inequalities in the sorted entries even at sum $66$. For arbitrary lists, an ordered interval rule and a finite difference in the degrees alone each give an exact criterion. On an $L$-bit input, a deterministic $O(L)+2^{O(\sqrt{n})}$-time search finds a realization or rules one out. At the first two even sums beyond the sparse bound of Bar-Noy et al., we classify all exceptions among positive graphic lists, giving linear-time recognition on a word RAM throughout the extended range. In particular, for $n\ge 8$, appending $n-6$ twos suffices to make every graphic $n$-term list of minimum degree at least three and sum $6n-12$ potentially planar.

authors.name: Renwen Tian
authors.institution: State Key Laboratory of Media Convergence and Communication

papers.title: SplatTok: Data-Driven Compression of 3D Gaussian Splats with Scene-Level Tokens
papers.abstract: 3D Gaussian splats enable real-time rendering but require substantial storage. Existing compression methods either encode the primitives of a given splat or optimize a compact representation independently for each scene. Yet a Gaussian splat is only one realization of a scene: different arrangements of primitives can produce nearly identical rendered views. We exploit this freedom on the decoding side with SplatTok, a learned scene-resynthesis codec. Trained across thousands of real-world scenes, a transformer encodes an existing splat into compact, spatially anchored latent tokens, and a shared decoder synthesizes a new set of standard Gaussian primitives without preserving correspondence to the input. The representation is learned through rendering supervision rather than primitive reconstruction. At compression time, a quantization-aware latent search refines only the scene code, keeping the networks frozen, and closes most of the encoder's remaining error. On standard benchmarks, using only renders of the input splat for the latent search, without the original training images, SplatTok matches the PSNR of the feed-forward codec FCGS with 4 to 6.5 times smaller files, compressing input splats about 75 to 110 times. With the training images, it exceeds the PSNR of the per-scene method HAC++ with 13 to 41% smaller files. A single model trained on DL3DV generalizes to unseen scenes with millions of Gaussians and supports multiple target rates without retraining.

authors.name: Guandao Yang
authors.institution: The University of Texas at Austin

papers.title: No Fixed Configuration Is Best: Context- and Cost-Aware Tuning of LLM Pipelines, with an Application to Schema Matching and Mapping
papers.abstract: The numeric settings of a multi-stage LLM pipeline (a compound AI system) are the usual target of tuning. We tuned all of them for an LLM pipeline for schema matching and mapping, with accuracy and cost as joint objectives, and we show what this buys, what it cannot buy, and where the remaining accuracy is. First, tuning buys cost and a little accuracy. On 35 tasks, with whole groups of tasks held out from tuning, one tuned configuration gains 2.9 points of top-1 accuracy (HR@1) over the default at 18% more cost, and another keeps the accuracy of the default at 32% lower cost. Second, the accuracy depends on a choice that numeric tuning cannot reach. Restricting the search for each source column to one assigned target table changes HR@1 by +30 points on a MIMIC-III to OMOP task and by -52 points on a task built from database views, more than numeric tuning gains on nine of ten test tasks. Neither setting is right for all tasks: on the larger set of 41 tasks used for the remaining results, mean HR@1 is 75.7% with the restriction (the default) and 83.1% without it. Third, choosing the setting per task is not enough either: even an oracle that picks the better setting for each task reaches only 87.8% on the 41 tasks, because the better setting differs between the columns of one task. The pipeline therefore runs both settings, and an LLM judge chooses among their candidate answers on the 26% of columns on which they disagree. This reaches 91.5% HR@1 on the 41 tasks, at 5.9 times the cost of the default, about one cent per column.

papers.title: Streaming instabilities and electron transport in electron transpiration cooling
papers.abstract: Electron transpiration cooling requires emitted electrons to travel through a surrounding plasma, where their relative motion with background electrons can drive streaming instabilities. We investigate these instabilities using particle-in-cell simulations with Monte Carlo collisions in a finite helium plasma. Lower neutral densities show pronounced wave activity, while higher densities give smoother electron distributions. A multifluid model constructed from simulated velocity distributions captures the frequency scale and decay direction in selected cases, but underestimates the separate driving and absorbing responses of electron populations. Distinguishing fast and slow emitted electrons and normalizing the field amplitude by the expanding two-peak length improves the low-wavenumber growth comparison, while discrepancies remain. Spatial growth estimates show that finite propagation distance also limits amplification. Strong late-time current fluctuations can coexist with nearly complete mean anode collection. These findings connect streaming instability to electron transport in the cooling model and show both the usefulness and limitations of a fluid description.

authors.name: Weixing Zhou
authors.institution: East China University of Science and Technology

papers.title: WaveSR: Physics-Inspired Wave Evolution Attention for Efficient Image Super-Resolution
papers.abstract: Recently, physics-inspired neural networks have gained widespread attention due to their interpretability. The closed-form, frequency-time decoupled solution of the wave equation offers linear complexity and allows different frequency components to evolve independently, making it a potential alternative solution for efficient image super-resolution. Therefore, a physics-inspired wave evolution attention framework is proposed, namely WaveSR. The WaveSR framework involves two key modules, i.e., wave evolution attention (WEA) and Frequency-Adaptive Feed-Forward Network (FA-FFN). The WEA module achieves feature interactions through the analytical solution of the 2D wave equation in the Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) domain, enabling independent evolution of different frequency components with learnable wave speed \(c\) and damping coefficient \(\alpha\). The FA-FFN module realizes adaptive frequency feature selection through learnable spectral modulation, effectively enhancing feature representation capability. Subsequently, we employ a two-stage training strategy with a hybrid objective that combines a spatial-domain pixel loss and a frequency-domain loss to improve reconstruction quality. Our method provides a preliminary exploration of physics-inspired neural networks for efficient image super-resolution.

authors.name: Tingwen Huang
authors.institution: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Putting a Robot on a Phone Call: Layered Signaling, Bounded Occupancy and Turn Arbitration over WebRTC
papers.abstract: We put a Thor robot on a browser voice call, with speech sent from Safari, answers played through the robot's loudspeaker and transcripts returned to the phone. We separate HTTPS signaling, relayed WebRTC media and speech generation into independently observable routes. The browser prefetches relay credentials and allows a 500 ms window after its first relay candidate. The backend starts speech and WebRTC-answer preparation concurrently within a 55 s deadline. A session slot and a non-blocking speaker lock coordinate calls with local voice access. A 2 s gate gives the controller an opportunity to suppress chat before playback. Fifteen of sixteen first dials reached ready-to-speak, comprising seven of eight Wi-Fi calls with a median of 5.57 s and eight of eight cellular calls with a median of 6.76 s. All twenty scored occupancy and recovery scenarios admitted a later call. During five 60 s outages, the backend released the line while the phone remained offline. Across 40 controlled replays, enabling the gate suppressed chat when the controller decided at 1 s. At 3 s, chat and controller feedback both played in sequence, with no overlapping output in any trace. Two additional boundary traces exposed a receipt naming a later feedback item and a new call's query returning its predecessor's feedback. These measurements cover application events on one platform and simulated controller decisions, with acoustic output and task correctness outside their scope.

papers.title: Electrons in a hard-wall cylinder with helicoidal metric: time-reversal pairing, cubic anticrossings, and twist-activated dipole transitions
papers.abstract: We study the scalar Schr\"odinger equation in a helicoidal metric when the axial direction is closed by Dirichlet walls built into the operator domain. With hard walls, the axial derivative cannot be replaced by a traveling-wave factor, and in a rotationally symmetric spinless cavity, time reversal makes the levels with azimuthal numbers $m$ and $-m$ exactly degenerate. We write the Hamiltonian as a Hermitian coupled-subband matrix and give an exact gauge-adapted variational representation. For a finite radius, the leading twist correction is quadratic, and changes sign at a critical aspect ratio; for an unbounded radial domain, it is linear in $|\Omega_g|$. Retuning the aspect ratio through an isolated radial--axial resonance within one $m$ sector opens an avoided crossing with gap $\Delta_{\mathrm{gap}}/E_R=1.648775\ldots|\Omega_gR^2/L|^3$ to leading order. A transverse dipole transition forbidden without twist acquires an oscillator strength quadratic in the twist, with leading coefficient $0.0559408010$ for $R/L=2$ from perturbation theory. Dipole sum rules and the convergence of the currents serve as checks on the numerics. We also give the inverse-mass tensor required for a scalar realization and re-examine each statement and figure of the earlier article [Opt. Quantum Electron. \textbf{58}, 113 (2026)] within the corrected model.

papers.title: VLAs Execute, Code Recovers: 3D Skill Envelopes Bridge the Compositional Gap in Agentic Manipulation
papers.abstract: Composing frozen Vision-Language-Action (VLA) skills under an agentic planner promises scalable long-horizon manipulation without long-horizon demonstrations, yet strong atomic skills routinely fail at seams even under a correct plan. Standard remedies reset the robot's pose or draft entry conditions in language, missing the physical cause we uncover via causal interventions: even after re-homing, a frozen VLA rigidly retraces its habitual trajectory and collides with displaced scene residue, whether or not it can see it. We propose the Skill Envelope, a policy-measured 3D geometric precondition capturing the volume a frozen skill sweeps during successful executions. Exploiting the insight that the rigidity making a frozen skill fragile at seams also makes its trajectory predictable in advance, we expose each envelope as two classical 3D tools (CHECK to detect blocking residue and FREE to locate safe placement regions), establishing a division of labor where VLAs execute in-distribution manipulation and code repairs out-of-distribution states. On LIBERO-Goal with frozen $\pi_{0.5}$, our zero-failure envelope predicts collisions at 0.946 AUROC (0.944 from one RGB-D view) and beats frontier VLMs on seam readiness (0.902 vs. 0.793); using it for skill ordering and code repair lifts success from 82.8% to 92.3% on two-step seams and from 29.7% to 93.8% on drawer-bearing 3-4 step chains, matching privileged world reset. Together, these results show that reliable VLA composition hinges on measuring a policy's physical workspace rather than guessing preconditions in language. Ongoing work closes the loop with autonomous LLM orchestration, synthesized free-object recovery, and cross-policy evaluation on cluttered benchmarks and real hardware.

papers.title: EmbodiedStudio: A Task-Driven Simulation Generation Platform for Embodied Learning and Evaluation
papers.abstract: Training and evaluating robots across diverse tasks requires a supply of simulation environments suited to those tasks. While recent scene and task generators offer a promising way to expand this supply, delivering a usable task environment still faces two practical gaps: generated scenes that look plausible in appearance often fail to support the intended task interactions or remain physically stable in simulation, and generated scoring programs frequently attempt task conditions without implementing them faithfully. We present EmbodiedStudio, a task-driven simulation generation platform that bridges these gaps by jointly authoring scene, task, robot-behavior, and rubric programs under closed-loop simulation feedback and independent review. Crucially, as the coding agent iteratively debugs scenes, behaviors, and stateful rubrics in simulation, this closed-loop process natively yields both forward construction experience for learning to build environments and physical execution experience for policy learning, all bound to frozen environment revisions for repeatable evaluation. Across scene generation, rubric evaluation, ablations, and learning studies, EmbodiedStudio substantially improves task readiness and rubric faithfulness while improving physical stability and retaining actionable supervision signals for layout authoring and policy adaptation.

papers.title: Coherent meson-baryon conversion in a cold-atom non-Abelian lattice gauge simulator
papers.abstract: Quantum chromodynamics (QCD), the non-Abelian gauge theory of quarks and gluons, provides a microscopic description of strongly interacting matter, including hadron structure and dynamics. Real-time dynamics and finite-density properties of these systems remain challenging for conventional Monte Carlo methods because of sign problems. Quantum simulation provides a complementary approach, although circuit depth and noise limit digital implementations and non-Abelian gauge-matter interactions remain difficult to engineer in analog systems. Here we realize a non-Abelian lattice gauge model with dynamical matter in an analog cold-atom simulator and directly observe its hadronic dynamics using site- and spin-resolved quantum gas microscopy. This realization is enabled by harnessing two hyperfine states and site-occupation configurations of 87Rb atoms to jointly encode both matter and gauge fields. We tailor resonant tunneling in a spin-dependent optical superlattice to implement a gauge sector of a truncated one-dimensional SU(2) quantum link model with independently tunable mass and gauge coupling. Leveraging this control, we track the conversion of an initially mesonic state into baryonic or vacuum-like configurations through slow mass ramps. Near resonance, we observe coherent oscillations between mesons and baryon-antibaryon pairs and characterize the conversion efficiency as a function of mass, gauge coupling and net baryon density. Our realization establishes an atomic platform for non-Abelian gauge dynamics, opening a route to microscopic studies of nonequilibrium dynamics in strongly interacting matter.

papers.title: A New Population of Jovian Exoplanets Suitable For Direct Imaging with the Habitable Worlds Observatory, the Roman Coronagraph, and ELTs Identified from HARPS Radial-Velocity Data and Hipparcos-Gaia Astrometry
papers.abstract:
We jointly analyze archival radial-velocity data from the HARPS spectrograph and astrometry from Hipparcos and Gaia to identify and constrain the dynamical properties of new and known long-period jovian exoplanets. Our search yields 14 new confirmed planets with masses of 0.04--6.1 $M_{\rm Jup}$ and semimajor axes of 0.1--12.6 au. Planets include a super-Jupiter in a near-Saturn-like orbit producing a strong astrometric acceleration (HIP 669 b), an eccentric Jupiter around a K star with a modest acceleration (HIP 39039 b), a 74-day-orbit warm Neptune (HIP 64550 b), and a giant planet around a Tier A Habitable Worlds Observatory target that may endanger any habitable zone Earth (HIP 17378 b). Three systems show evidence for candidate planets requiring additional data for confirmation. Our modeling also constrains the dynamical masses and orbits for 32 previously known radial-velocity-discovered planets.
  Orbits, masses, and ages for our sample show that five targets are potentially detectable in reflected light with the Roman Coronagraph, 28 should be imageable in reflected light with the Habitable Worlds Observatory, and six may be detectable in thermal emission with E-ELT/METIS. These results demonstrate the power of combining archival radial-velocity data with astrometry to discover and characterize long-period giant planets, a capability that will only grow with Gaia DR4. It provides a new sample of targets for future direct-imaging observations, and shows a path forward for timely vetting of targets for exo-Earth imaging with the Habitable Worlds Observatory.

papers.title: Tentative Excess Dispersion Measures toward DESI Galaxy Groups from Localized Fast Radio Bursts
papers.abstract: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) provide sensitive probes of ionized baryons through their dispersion measures (DMs). In this work, we test whether localized FRB sight lines intersecting foreground galaxy groups exhibit a measurable excess in cosmic DM relative to clean nonintersecting sight lines. We crossmatch 117 localized FRBs with measured DMs and host redshifts against a foreground group catalog from the DESI Legacy Imaging Surveys. Within the catalog footprint and at $z_{\rm host}<0.5$, we identify 23 sight lines intersecting foreground groups and 18 clean nonintersecting sight lines for the main comparison. A joint fit to this sample gives a positive offset of $143.3^{+53.2}_{-53.0}~\mathrm{pc\,cm^{-3}}$ in the inferred cosmic DM, $\mathrm{DM}_{\rm cosmic}$, for the group-intersecting sight lines relative to the nonintersecting control sample. A template fit for the foreground halos gives $A_{\rm halo}=0.34^{+0.51}_{-0.50}$, with a positive posterior median but a weakly constrained detailed halo contribution. A mock forecast within the DESI footprint indicates that larger samples of localized FRBs would improve the foreground halo template constraint.

authors.name: Jiale Wang
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Not All Interpretation Methods Are Created Equal: Tiered Evaluation of AI Interpretability
papers.abstract: As AI transitions to sociotechnical deployments, uninterpretable models pose serious threats to reliability, public trust and contestability. However, not all interpretation methods are created equal: for interpretability to enhance deployment safety and effectiveness, interpretation methods must be evaluated in a tiered system to differentiate evidence levels of trustworthiness, rather than validated through isolated interpretation instances. Our core vision is that elevating the evaluation of interpretation methods to a core AI assessment metric will drive robust knowledge discovery from data (KDD) and ensure safe, contestable sociotechnical deployments of AI. To this end, we propose TRUST, a tiered evaluation framework that builds upon the Predictability-Computability-Stability (PCS) principles for Veridical Data Science (VDS) and the Predictive, Descriptive and Relevant (PDR) foundations. To differentiate interpretation methods effectively and systematically, TRUST grades interpretation across five tiers: Task-Aligned PDR Foundations, Rigorous Epistemic Grounding, Unifying Semantic Understanding, Scope Transferability, and Targeted Prospective Validation. We present a start-to-finish case study of the iterative Random Forest (iRF) family under TRUST and contrast it with other LLM interpretation methods that struggle to clear specific tiers. Finally, we conclude with brief initial thoughts on how TRUST principles can extend in autonomous agentic frameworks. Ultimately, the TRUST framework fosters contestability and epistemic grounding as foundational evaluation principles for human-machine workflows and, eventually, autonomous agentic workflows.

papers.title: Field-Dependent Kinetics, Exact Kinks, and a Moduli-Space Route from Self-Dual Yang-Mills Theory
papers.abstract: We study scalar-field models in 1+1 dimensions with field-dependent kinetic coefficients, motivated by self-dual Yang-Mills (SDYM) theory as a generator of integrable equations. We derive the Euler-Lagrange equation, traveling-wave reduction, and first integral, and solve the inverse problem: given a kinetic structure and a prescribed tanh kink, which potential makes it exact? A quadratic spatial deformation with a canonical temporal sector yields a sextic potential. We obtain: (i) a closed-form kink energy with a Bogomolny-type formulation, independent of the odd parameter, which nonetheless shapes the energy density asymmetrically; (ii) vacuum curvature relations tying the spectrum to the kinetic function at the vacua; (iii) two propositions on speed families, plus a lemma showing single-speed data probe only one combination of the kinetic functions; (iv) a unified admissibility analysis in which positivity of the spatial kinetic function controls hyperbolicity, the potential bound along the kink, and the vacuum masses; (v) a self-adjoint fluctuation operator with a closed-form potential whose asymptotes are the vacuum masses, an exact translation zero mode, and numerical spectra with no negative mode on the admissible region, evidence for spectral stability. Exact SDYM reductions yield integrable equations, whereas the deformed model is generically non-integrable and cannot be an exact reduction. The correct bridge is the moduli-space route: SDYM reduces to the Bogomolny equations, whose BPS monopole and dyon dynamics produce field-dependent kinetic terms; any smooth one-dimensional moduli metric expands, to second order, to the quadratic model studied here, and the Taub-NUT metric of well-separated dyons gives an explicit realization. Full identification of the sextic potential within a specific gauge-theory moduli dynamics remains open and is formulated as a research program.

authors.name: Ji Wang
authors.institution: Harbin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Annular-curvature effects on high-frequency azimuthal fluctuations in 3D PIC simulations of Hall-thruster plasmas
papers.abstract: Azimuthal instabilities and associated plasma fluctuations play an important role in anomalous cross-field electron transport in Hall thrusters. Kinetic studies often approximate the annular discharge using local Cartesian domains, but the influence of the neglected curvature on threedimensional fluctuation dynamics remains insufficiently quantified. Here, three-dimensional cylindrical electrostatic particle-in-cell simulations assess this geometric effect in a reduced channel-plume model by varying the minimum computational-domain radius rmin at fixed channel width and imposed magnetic-field profile. The dominant channel wavenumbers on the centerline-reference scale remain similar, while pronounced radial amplitude asymmetry develops in the smaller-radius configurations. At rmin = 10 cm and 2 cm, the outer-channel electric-field amplitudes in the dominant wavenumber band exceed the inner-channel values by 26% and 53%, respectively. In the plume, low-wavenumber fluctuations favor the inner region, whereas high-wavenumber components favor the outer region. Density-electric-field covariance is preferentially concentrated in the outer channel and inner plume, with outer-to-inner magnitude ratios of 2.71 and 0.58 at rmin = 2 cm. These persistent spatial preferences connect the geometric redistribution of fluctuations to the correlated axial ExB drift contribution. For the 1.28 cm channel width studied, these results support retaining cylindrical geometry at rmin = 10 cm and 2 cm to resolve local fluctuations and transport-related correlations, even when the imposed magnetic-field profile is unchanged.

papers.title: AI, Bias, and Inclusion: A Two-Phase Mixed-Methods Study of Gender Bias, Awareness, and Trust in Artificial Intelligence
papers.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems are widespread across fields such as healthcare, finance, employment, and criminal justice, with a substantial impact on the lives of individuals and society. However, it has been established that AI systems perpetuate existing social inequalities, particularly through biases that are not easily discernible. Such biases are embedded in the technical and social structures of artificial intelligence systems, making them difficult to detect. These biases challenge the concept of Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion (EDI), which recognizes diversity as the acknowledgment of individual differences, equity as fairness and equal access, and inclusion as the value placed on all participants. This study argues that fairness in artificial intelligence systems cannot be achieved by focusing solely on their technical aspects, necessitating a holistic approach. This study employs a two-phase mixed-methods design. Phase 1 applies computational content analysis to 360 occupational narratives generated by ChatGPT across four countries (Canada, Germany, India, and Bangladesh) using gender-neutral prompts to examine whether professions are predominantly associated with one gender and whether these patterns remain consistent across regions. Phase 2 examines the extent to which students recognize potential bias in AI, their trust in AI for consequential decision-making, and how these perceptions relate to themes in EDI and AI ethics scholarship. By combining output-level bias analysis with user perception data, this study identifies the empirical foundations necessary for future EDI-AI co-design frameworks, outlining the sociotechnical dimensions that such frameworks must address to be effective.

papers.title: Characterizing $T_0$-spaces where GIS-convergence is topological
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce and investigate the GIS-convergence in $T_0$-spaces and the related concept of GIS-continuous spaces(GSI-continuous spaces). It is proved that $SI(X)$ is a locally hypercompact space iff $(X, \tau)$ is a $GSI$-continuous space iff GSI-convergence in $X$ with respect to the topology $\mathcal{O}_{SI}(X)$ is topological. We also show that the $GIS$-convergence in $(X, \tau)$ is topological if and only if $(X,\tau)$ is a $GIS$-continuous space.

authors.name: Fugang Zhang
authors.institution: Yunnan Provincial Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine

papers.title: Volume difference inequalities for central sections of origin-symmetric convex bodies
papers.abstract: Giannopoulos and Koldobsky \cite{GK} asked whether, for origin-symmetric convex bodies $L\subset K\subset\R^n$, the difference $|K|^{(n-k)/n}-|L|^{(n-k)/n}$ is bounded by $C^k$ times the largest difference of their central section volumes in codimension $k$, with a single absolute constant $C$. We prove that the optimal constant $\gamma_{n,k}$ for fixed $n,k$ satisfies $\gamma_{n,k}\ge c\sqrt{n/k}$ for an absolute $c>0$. For $k=1$, this lower bound grows as $\sqrt n$ with the dimension, giving a negative answer to the question.

authors.name: Jiangyan Tao
authors.institution: Tianjin Medical University Cancer Institute and Hospital

papers.title: Linear-Quadratic Graphon Mean-Field Games in Hilbert Spaces and Applications
papers.abstract: This paper investigates a class of linear-quadratic graphon mean-field games (LQ-GMFGs) in Hilbert spaces, where heterogeneous agents are distributed over large networks. A distinguishing feature of our model, compared with the model of well-studied finite dimensional LQ-GMFGs, is that the dynamics of agents are governed by infinite dimensional stochastic evolution equations (SEEs) involving an unbounded operator. The diffusion coefficients are allowed to depend on the state, the control, and the weighted state-average. In addition, the parameters in cost functionals could be indefinite. As the number of agents, $N$, tends to infinity, following the Nash certainty equivalence methodology, the solvability of the limit GMFG is reduced to that of an operator-valued Riccati equation and a GMFG equation system. The existence of a strongly regular solution to the former is characterized by an equivalent, easily verifiable condition, and the sufficient conditions are established for the solvability of the latter by applying the spectral decomposition method. Therefore a Nash equilibrium for the limit game is obtained. Under some adequate convergence assumptions, a set of decentralized strategies for the $N$-agent game is designed based on the Nash equilibrium of the limit GMFG, and the obtained strategy profile is shown to constitute an $\epsilon$-Nash equilibrium. Finally, the theoretical results are applied to an optimal investment problem with delay in a competitive environment.

authors.name: Zhen Wu
authors.institution: Tianjin University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Bound-preserving Flux Limiters for Hyperbolic Conservation Laws on Two-Dimensional Adaptive Moving Meshes
papers.abstract: In this paper, we develop a bound-preserving finite-volume method on adaptive moving meshes for two-dimensional hyperbolic conservation laws. The proposed method extends our previous one-dimensional framework [Y. Gu, G. Hu, and T. Tang, Adaptive mesh methods for hyperbolic conservation laws with bound-preserving flux limiters, arXiv:2602.12580] to two dimensions within the arbitrary Lagrangian-Eulerian framework. The mesh velocity is determined by solving a moving mesh equation, allowing the numerical solution to evolve directly between consecutive time levels. A key challenge in this extension is to ensure compatibility between the evolution of the mesh geometry and the update of the numerical solution, as geometric information is essential to the convex decomposition underlying the bound-preserving construction in two dimensions. Specifically, the high-order scheme is reformulated as a convex combination of high-order sub-cell schemes, each of which is blended with its first-order counterpart to enforce the bound-preserving property. The discrete geometric conservation law ensures the compatibility needed to maintain this convex decomposition on moving meshes. The resulting correction acts locally at individual cell interfaces and is equivalent to applying a bound-preserving flux limiter, making the approach applicable to general unstructured or irregular meshes. The associated bound-preserving CFL conditions are established for both scalar conservation laws and the nonlinear Euler equations of gas dynamics. Extensive two-dimensional numerical experiments demonstrate the accuracy, robustness, and effectiveness of the proposed method.

papers.title: CLAIMGATE: Cautious On-Device Checking of Spoken Legal and Clinical Claims
papers.abstract: In law and medicine, a misstated rule can shape a decision before anyone has time to check it. Checking such claims in real time helps only if the checker keeps pace with conversation, keeps sensitive audio on the device, and stays silent rather than mislead. We present CLAIMGATE, an on- device assistant that listens to a conversation, detects checkable claims, retrieves the relevant official rule, and labels each claim as supported, contradicted or not covered, with a citation. CLAIMGATE is designed to fail towards silence: its 4-bit 7B- parameter language model may cite only retrieved rules, and the verdict is derived in code from the claim and rule the model quotes. We evaluate it on traffic stops and medical visits using real official rule text (5,742 Florida and Texas statute subsections; CDC, FDA and MedlinePlus guidance), real transcripts, live speech and author-written gold-labelled claims. On 141 held-out traffic-stop claims, CLAIMGATE reaches 80.1% accuracy and cuts serious errors (a true claim called false, or the reverse) from 20 to 5 compared with the same model without retrieval; deriving the verdict in code alone reduces them from 13 to 5 at no cost to accuracy. The claim gate passes 95.7% of held-out claims and rejects all 30 everyday sentences, and feedback arrives a median 1.86 s after a speech window closes on an 8 GB consumer GPU. On 148 allergy claims, with only the claim gate to rebuild, CLAIMGATE reaches 87.8% accuracy with 5 serious errors, against 20 without retrieval.

papers.title: POISE: Curvature-Aware Critic Regularization for Smooth Actor-Critic Control
papers.abstract: Actor-critic methods achieve high returns in robotic control, yet trained actors exhibit high-frequency action oscillations. Most smoothness methods constrain the actor, whereas PAVE regularizes the critic by separately penalizing action-gradient variation and encouraging negative action curvature. The same gradient change, however, moves the critic's preferred action farther where the critic is flat, and separate penalties do not measure this motion. We characterize this motion through the greedy shift, which approximates greedy-action displacement across state transitions to first order under local concavity. Since displacement alone does not reflect its critic-value consequences, the analysis further shows that the shift's curvature-weighted energy approximates the value lost by retaining the previous greedy action to second order. Based on this relationship, POISE regularizes the curvature-weighted energy along temporal and spatial state displacements. It employs a saddle-free curvature metric and reward-scale-consistent scaling while leaving the actor unchanged. On six continuous control tasks with TD3, POISE reduces the smoothness score on every task by $5.9\times$ on average ($4.5\times$ geometric mean), compared with $2.2\times$ ($1.9\times$) for the strongest baseline, and achieves the lowest score on five tasks. Paired return intervals include zero on four tasks, with a 14% increase on Ant and an 11% decrease on Hopper.

papers.title: BendGS: Observation-Conditioned Gaussian Self-Modeling for Continuum Robots
papers.abstract: Visual self-models learn from images how a robot moves under motor commands. Continuum robots need them even more, as they bend continuously without measured joint angles or fixed link geometry. Existing continuum self-models predict point clouds, image-space curves, or future images, but not the next 3D shape, appearance, and tip pose together from an observed body. 3D Gaussians offer a renderable representation of shape and appearance, yet articulated Gaussian self-models rely on joint angles to drive deformation. In this work, we propose BendGS, which uses a virtual backbone estimated from observation to drive command-conditioned Gaussian deformation, enabling next-state prediction for continuum robots without measured joint angles. In Gaussian modeling, a feed-forward network reconstructs the robot as 3D Gaussians from multi-view images, and the backbone, a chain of coordinate frames, is fitted to back-projected depth points to estimate the bending state. In transition, a network predicts its change under a relative motor command to deform the bound Gaussians. The deformed Gaussians render the next images and the 3D shape, and the distal frame gives the tip pose. Training losses use RGB-D images and masks, without bending or tip labels. On simulated and real robots, BendGS achieves the lowest Chamfer distance, best image quality, and lowest tip errors among the compared methods.

papers.title: Grounding Language Models in Revealed Audience Behavior
papers.abstract: Language models are increasingly used to simulate how an audience will respond to a headline or a post, and such simulators are validated against what people say. We validate them against what people do. We call a model grounded in revealed audience behavior when it is fine-tuned on records of what audiences actually clicked, liked or watched, and we ask not only whether asking a model falls short of grounding it, as prior work found, but why and where. Why: the gap is a property of the training signal, not mainly of model size or prompting. The same 8B model is right about half the time when asked which headline readers will click and 86.5% of the time when grounded in the clicks; the strongest prompting we tried only matches a text classifier; a grounded 0.6B model beats every prompted frontier model in our runs; and whether the clicks are fitted as counts or as shares makes no detectable difference in a pre-registered test. The asked 8B model also reproduces stated-preference cues, favoring question headlines that in fact lower clicks. Where: across four behaviors, grounding wins where the text carries the signal (short-video likes, +20 points on 200 pre-registered videos), only ties an asked model given the reader's history (news clicks), and nothing text-only gets far from chance on watch time. Code, adapters and run outputs will be released.

papers.title: SofaSpace: A Benchmark for Executable Visual Spatial Reasoning in Continuous Motion and Environment Construction
papers.abstract: A rigid body can fit at its start and goal yet collide with a wall as it moves between them. Inspired by the moving sofa problem, we introduce SofaSpace, a benchmark for visual spatial reasoning through continuous planar rigid-body transport and environment construction. SofaSpace contains 3,000 scenes organized around three challenges: geometric compatibility, nonlocal maneuver planning, and interactive and temporal coordination. Four task views ask models to plan a motion, reconstruct a layout, design an environment that meets transport requirements, or jointly generate a layout and a motion. A separate set of 534 SofaSpace-Hard tasks tests planning and judgment. A geometric verifier checks the entire body throughout each submitted motion. On static planning tasks, endpoint agreement and continuous validity differ substantially within the same submitted plans: Claude drops from 97.2% to 52.8%, DeepSeek from 100.0% to 30.6%, and Kimi from 97.2% to 29.4%, while the strongest configuration retains 98.3% full validity. Environment construction reveals a further gap. Of 295 feasible layouts generated by the strongest configuration, 181 satisfy all evaluated functional requirements; for Kimi, one of 172 does. These results show how executable checks distinguish endpoint agreement from valid motion and geometric feasibility from functional compliance.

papers.title: Single-shot on-chip measurement of the modal Stokes parameters
papers.abstract: Integrated photonics has recently facilitated manipulating multimode partially coherent light in a compact mesh of Mach-Zehnder interferometers. A critical task in this context is on-chip reconstruction of the coherence matrix through a sequence of measurement configurations, thus giving rise to a speed bottleneck stemming from temporal delays in tuning on-chip phase shifts. Here we demonstrate single-shot reconstruction of the coherence matrix for two-mode partially coherent light by parallelizing the on-chip measurements of the modal Stokes parameters, thereby exchanging space for time. Although a larger chip area is required, the reconstruction is limited only by detection speed, thus potentially paving the way to real-time reconstruction of coherence matrices for applications in high-speed communications, cryptography, computation, and sensing.

papers.title: Can LLM Judges Catch Unsafe Clinical Actions? A Fault-Injection Study
papers.abstract: As clinical AI agents begin to interact with electronic health records (EHRs), large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to evaluate their actions. But how reliably can these judges recognize clinically dangerous mistakes, especially when an agent appears to have completed its task successfully? We investigate this question using MedAgentBench by introducing controlled clinical errors into verified agent trajectories. The experiments include 416 faulty trajectories, eight error categories, and six open-weight LLM judges. By comparing each faulty trajectory with its correct counterpart, we measure whether judges genuinely recognize errors rather than simply flagging more actions as unsafe. The findings show that access to clinical evidence significantly improves judge reliability. When shown only the final answer, judges cannot distinguish errors that leave it unchanged, while flagging 56% of correct trajectories. With full trajectory information, the ability to distinguish unsafe actions from correct ones reaches a score of 0.75, and providing actual EHR responses improves discrimination by 0.39. Surprisingly, including the agent's reasoning does not improve overall performance and reduces detection of incorrectly reported clinical values by 0.18, which remain the hardest errors to detect. MedGemma performed worse than the general-purpose model and was the only judge to miss potentially dangerous medication overdoses. We also find that the benchmark's original grader accepts all 38 trajectories with an intentionally skipped laboratory check, while combining LLM judges with a rule-based checker informed by the full EHR record detects 97% of injected faults.

papers.title: Describe, Don't Ask: Caption-Driven On-Policy Distillation for Fine-Grained Visual Perception
papers.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) often recognize fine-grained details more accurately in a relevant crop than in the full image. Multimodal on-policy distillation (OPD) methods exploit this by transferring the advantage of a crop-view teacher to a full-image student. However, their supervision relies on region-specific questions curated through an elaborate synthesis pipeline, which brings three weaknesses: (1) every region needs a question--answer pair written exclusively for it, locking training into costly QA curation that is hard to scale to unlabeled images; (2) all rollouts of a region answer the same question, so the teacher supervises only the details it asks about, leaving other visual elements in the region unsupervised; and (3) every question presupposes that its target exists, so the student becomes prone to answering even when the target is absent. In this paper, we study how to turn unlabeled images into broad visual supervision through multi-aspect self-description and privileged-view distillation, and propose CaptionOPD, which replaces tailored questions with a fixed set of image-agnostic caption prompts, ranging from general descriptions to focused captions of parts, colors, counts, text, and layout. The rollouts of a region receive different prompts, so the teacher supervises various aspects of the region. Moreover, because caption prompts mask the model to describe what is visible instead of querying a specific target, they avoid presupposing what the region contains. Using the model itself as the crop-view teacher, CaptionOPD requires no questions, no answers, and no larger model annotations: only images and region boxes. Experiments show that, trained on the same images and regions, CaptionOPD outperforms prior OPD methods across multiple fine-grained and general perception benchmarks.

papers.title: Fluctuations in the k-cut numbers of random recursive trees
papers.abstract: We consider the k-cut procedure introduced by Cai et al. [EJP, 2018] on random recursive trees. Our main result identifies the fluctuations in the number of cuts required to isolate the root as the tree size tends to infinity. This extends the results by Drmota et al. [RSA, 2009] and Iksanov et al. [ECP, 2007] for the classical cutting procedure.

papers.title: "I Do Intend to Deliver": Will LLMs Run a Marketplace Advance-Fee Scam?
papers.abstract: Online fraud is traditionally limited by the cost of the human labor needed to talk to potential victims. We ask whether hosted large language models will now supply that labor. We prompted ten off-the-shelf models to play the seller in the "free item, just pay delivery" advance-fee scam common on buy-and-sell sites, using a plain system prompt with no jailbreak. Each model played 30 conversations against each of four buyer personas, from credulous to guarded, with the same model playing the buyer (1,200 conversations). We label each conversation by what happened to the buyer's money, and validate the labels against two human coders. 737 conversations (61%) ended with the buyer paying in advance. Eight of the ten models played in almost every conversation, and running both sides cost about 2.5 cents per payment. Only the guarded buyer, who wanted a findable identity, resisted, and the most willing sellers got past it by inventing names and phone numbers. Sellers that recognized the scam still took the money in 133 conversations, usually reasoning about their own honesty rather than the buyer's risk. Several models protected the buyer without refusing, by conceding payment on delivery, so refusal rates alone misstate safety. We release the benchmark, prompts, code and labels.

papers.title: Efficient spin-lattice dynamics and spin thermometry with machine-learned magnetic potentials
papers.abstract: In finite-temperature spin-lattice dynamics, conventional force-only spin thermometers fail for energies nonlinear in each spin, while the standard semi-implicit SIB integrator requires two model evaluations per step. Here we introduce a geometric-probe spin temperature that is exact for arbitrary high-order smooth Hamiltonians using first-order spin forces alone without Hessians, making it naturally suited for nonlinear many-body machine-learning (ML) magnetic potentials. Complementarily, our cached-field integrator (CFI) stays second-order accurate with a single model evaluation per step, about halving the time per step with ML potentials. Extensive benchmarks against Monte Carlo across analytic and ML systems confirm both exact thermometry and accurate thermodynamics.

authors.name: Hongjun Xiang
authors.institution: Collaborative Innovation Center of Advanced Microstructures

papers.title: Area-minimizing surfaces and the rigidity of three-dimensional electrostatic systems
papers.abstract: We study three-dimensional electrostatic systems, the Riemannian data of static solutions of the Einstein--Maxwell equations with cosmological constant $\Lambda$, by means of locally area-minimizing surfaces. Such a surface with non-empty boundary on the horizons is a totally geodesic hemisphere and forces the de Sitter system. A closed one in the interior forces a system of product type, one of eight models if the scalar curvature is somewhere positive on it, among them the Bertotti--Robinson, Nariai and cold and ultracold black hole systems. No compactness, asymptotic or pinching assumption is needed. In particular, closed systems without horizons are flat or compact quotients of the Nariai--Bertotti--Robinson system. For compact systems with connected horizon, the electric field vanishes even when the system is not simply connected, and the area of the horizon is either $12\pi/\Lambda$, for de Sitter, or at most $4\pi/\Lambda$. With several horizons, every horizon whose area does not exceed the sum of the others is stable, minimizes area in its homology class and satisfies an area--charge inequality, with equality only for the charged Nariai systems; its charged Hawking mass and charge therefore lie in the parameter region of the Reissner--Nordstr\"om--de Sitter black holes. Compact systems with horizons are spherical space forms with balls removed. Noncompact systems with strictly mean-convex ends have one end, and their horizons are stable and $\pi_1$-injective and satisfy a strict area--charge inequality.

papers.title: Evaluating Large Language Models on Iranian Doctoral Entrance Exams in Electrical and Computer Engineering
papers.abstract: We evaluate four large language models (LLMs) on multiple-choice questions from the 2024 and 2025 Iranian national Ph.D. entrance examinations in Electrical Engineering (EE) and Computer Engineering (CE). Of the 440 questions in the four official booklets, 7 were excluded because the question statement or its figure was ambiguous, leaving 433 questions (186 EE, 247 CE), of which 171 (39.5\%) depend on a figure. Each question was presented in the original Persian and in an English translation, giving 3,464 scored responses. GPT-5, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Claude Sonnet 4.5 and Grok 4 were queried zero-shot, with reasoning enabled, through a single commercial web interface (Perplexity) in October 2025, using an automated script. Because every model answers the same items, all inferences use paired tests or question-clustered models. Accuracy separates into two tiers: GPT-5 (79.9\%, 95\% CI 76.6--83.1) and Gemini 2.5 Pro (78.4\%, 74.8--81.9) are statistically indistinguishable, and both outperform Grok 4 (71.7\%) and Claude Sonnet 4.5 (71.3\%) by 6.7--8.7 percentage points (Holm-adjusted $p < 0.001$). The English--Persian accuracy difference is small for every model ($-0.2$ to $+2.5$ points; exact McNemar $p \ge 0.28$). For three models the 90\% confidence interval lies within $\pm 5$ points, so differences larger than this can be excluded. Questions with figures are much harder: the odds ratio is 0.30 (95\% CI 0.21--0.43) after adjusting for discipline. The apparent EE deficit of two models disappears once the larger share of figure-based EE items is accounted for. We describe the dataset, the protocol and its limitations, including the uncontrolled web-retrieval and decoding settings of the interface, and release item-level responses and analysis code.

papers.title: Saddle-focus to saddle transition of 4D heteroclinic orbits resembling oscillatory and regularized shock waves of some dissipative Boussinesq systems
papers.abstract: Oscillatory and regularized shock waves have long been studied to understand the formation and dynamics of undular bores in shallow waters, phenomena that typically arise from the interplay between dispersion, nonlinearity, and dissipation. In this work, we investigate and describe the nature and shape of traveling wave solutions that resemble oscillatory and regularized shock waves of some Boussinesq-type water wave models known as Bona--Smith systems in the presence of dissipation. The associated traveling wave equations are solutions of four-dimensional dynamical systems, leading to both computational challenges and rich structural behavior. In particular, to describe the properties of these traveling waves, we analyze heteroclinic orbits that connect two distinct equilibria, one of which undergoes a transition in the four-dimensional phase space from a saddle-focus to a saddle point as the dissipation parameter increases. This transition governs the nature of the wave profile, which evolves smoothly from an oscillatory shock wave to a regularized (non-oscillatory) shock wave. To compute such solutions, we introduce a finite-difference-based numerical method tailored for this class of problems.

papers.title: Privacy Disclosure Control Benchmark (PDC-Bench): How Faithfully Do LLMs Keep Privacy Constraints on In-Context Disclosure Granularity?
papers.abstract: In LLM task execution, a constraint on the permitted disclosure granularity of personal attributes is sometimes imposed on the output. For example, if a person's private attribute is their location (San Francisco) and disclosure is permitted only at the country level, an output at the state level (California) violates the constraint. Detecting such violations requires capturing not only direct privacy leakage (San Francisco) but also semantic leakage (California). However, existing benchmarks cannot measure the degree of leakage with respect to a given semantic constraint such as the country-level limit. We therefore formalize disclosure control as a constraint on the permitted ceiling over the hierarchy of a knowledge graph. Building on this formulation, we construct PDC-Bench, a benchmark of 16,105 samples covering geography, age, race and ethnicity, and occupation. In our experiments applying PDC-Bench to eleven LLMs, 62% of the constraint violations were semantic leakage. We further found that semantic leakage depends less on the model than on the permitted disclosure granularity and the task's need for the private attribute; reliable auditing must therefore target semantic leakage together with these two factors. Data, prompts, and code are available at https://github.com/fuji1655/PDC-Bench.

papers.title: Verifying Type Soundness for Nontransitive Information Flow Security
papers.abstract: We present a machine-checked soundness proof of a type system for the nontransitive noninterference (NTNI) information flow security property in an imperative programming language using Dafny. The original formulation of NTNI was developed for a functional programming language augmented with memory access operators, where security policies are expressed as coarse-grained information flow constraints over component-based software systems. Although subsequent research has extended NTNI type systems in various directions, to the best of our knowledge, no prior work has established a machine-checked soundness proof for type-enforced NTNI. As a result, the correctness of existing NTNI enforcement mechanisms has not been formally verified with a high degree of assurance.

papers.title: TANDEM: Temporal Anchor Densification With Reliability-Aware Memory for Lightweight Sparse Depth Completion in Endoscopic Robotic Navigation
papers.abstract: For endoscopic robotic surgery, accurate dense depth perception serves as a foundational capability, which enables navigation, instrument localization, and tissue interaction. However, endoscopic video lacks reliable metric depth, while metric measurements obtained via tracking, time-of-flight sensing, or instrument contact only cover a small fraction of pixels in each frame, rendering sparse depth completion an urgent and unsolved challenge. In this work, we propose Temporal Anchor Densification with Reliability-Aware Memory (TANDEM), a causal sparse depth completion framework for endoscopic video. It adopts a lightweight design and leverages the video stream: past measurements re-projected into the current view recover the metric evidence unavailable within a single sparse frame. To keep this evidence interpretable, accurate, and efficient, an explicit memory scores each re-projected measurement with analytic re-observation, age, and motion-parallax factors without overriding current measurements. A compact network then reconstructs depth via reliability-weighted gradient integration and a frequency-gated reference prior. We evaluate TANDEM on the C3VD colonoscopy and StereoMIS laparoscopy datasets. With only 5.58 M parameters, TANDEM reduces the root mean square error by 11.7% and 32.0%, respectively, compared with the strongest baseline, and achieves state-of-the-art accuracy. It also remains accurate under pose errors of the magnitude reported for endoscopic pose estimation. Code will be released at https://github.com/Wk-cpu-art/TANDEM upon acceptance.

authors.name: Jinlian Ma
authors.institution: Henan University of Traditional Chinese Medicine

papers.title: On Waring's problem for fourth powers
papers.abstract: We prove that every sufficiently large integer $n$, satisfying $n\equiv 1,2,3,\dots,11\pmod*{16}$, can be written as a sum of $11$ biquadrates. In particular, $G^{\#}(4)\leq 11$. This improves upon $G^{\#}(4)\leq 12$ due to Vaughan in 1989.

authors.name: Lilu Zhao
authors.institution: University of Science and Technology of China

papers.title: Breaking the Binary-Lifting Barrier for DNA Minimizer Density: Exact Optimization of a Native 4-ary Order at (w, k) = (12, 5)
papers.abstract: Minimizer schemes sample at least one $k$-mer from every window of $w$ consecutive $k$-mers via a total order $\pi$ on $\Sigma^k$. For DNA ($\sigma = 4$), state-of-the-art lookup schemes such as GreedyMini and OptMini optimize a binary order ($2^k$ ranks) and lift it to $\Sigma^k$ by ranking one bit-plane primarily and breaking $2^k$-way ties lexicographically on the other bit-plane. At $(w, k) = (12, 5)$, this projection locks sets of $32$ DNA $5$-mers into contiguous blocks and restricts the active universal hitting set (UHS) prefix to $448$ of $1024$ $5$-mers, giving exact expected DNA density $2246214544 / 2^{34} \approx 0.1307468945$ for OptMini (k5-w12-13.txt) and $2248978620 / 2^{34} \approx 0.1309077849$ for GreedyMini (w12_k5.gm). We bypass binary lifting and optimize directly over native $4$-ary permutations ($|\Sigma^k| = 1024$) from scratch via: (i) an exact de Bruijn endpoint transfer-matrix dynamic program over $B(4, 4)$ ($256$ states), (ii) a weighted set-cover ratio initializer (SetCover4) producing a compact $U = 314$ UHS prefix, (iii) bitmask-sparse simulated annealing preserving the zero-cost $w$-walk-free tail invariant, and (iv) two-pass $O(N)$ exact best-insertion sweeps with large-neighborhood ruin-and-recreate search. The resulting explicit $4$-ary order achieves exact expected DNA density $2234289615 / 2^{34} \approx 0.130052772292$ (density factor $1.690686$), cutting charged windows by $11924929$ contexts ($-0.530890\%$ relative) below OrensteinLab/Minimizers and $14689005$ ($-0.653141\%$) below w12_k5.gm at $8200$-byte lookup storage ($1280$ bytes bit-packed). Warm-start relaxation stalls at $U = 379$ ($0.1301728789$), whereas native $4$-ary initialization breaks $32/32$ high-bit blocks across all $2+2$ nucleotide partitions.

papers.title: Multi-Frequency Inversion of Meridional Flows Using Wave-Simulation-Based Sensitivity Kernels: Kernels, Method and Validation On Synthetic Data
papers.abstract:
Measuring the solar meridional circulation is central to understanding how magnetic flux and angular momentum are redistributed within the Sun. While time-distance helioseismology has been a primary tool for probing these internal flows, current methods generally rely on broadband travel-time measurements that compress the frequency dependence of the wavefield into single values for each measurement geometry. This approach overlooks the fact that different temporal frequencies sample the solar interior differently, potentially limiting our ability to resolve complex, depth-dependent flow structures. In this paper, we present a framework for performing meridional circulation inversions using frequency-dependent travel-time shifts and corresponding sensitivity kernels derived directly from global-scale, 3D wave-propagation simulations.
  We analyze sensitivities for horizontal and radial flows, noting that higher temporal frequencies offer increased spatial resolution while their practical application is balanced by the lower signal--to--noise ratio of travel-time measurements at frequencies above the 3 mHz peak of solar oscillations. Using an iterative regularized least-squares solver, we demonstrate that our method successfully recovers many aspects of complex circulation models while remaining robust against the stochastic noise of realistic simulations. We consider the impact of different regularization operators on the inversions, and enforcing constraints like mass conservation to improve inversion results.

papers.title: Spontaneous Synchronization in Cellular Circadian Clocks
papers.abstract: We study a population of identical cellular circadian oscillators, each a four-species transcription--translation feedback loop of the type analysed by Wang and Peskin, coupled by the exchange of cytoplasmic mRNA with a shared, well-mixed bloodstream at rate $\epsilon$. Simulations started from uniformly random phases show a collective damping of the mean rhythm followed by spontaneous synchronization. We show that the blood compartment tracks the population mean on the time scale $1/[N_c(\epsilon+\delta_m)]$, and that the population means obey the single-cell equations with a correction proportional to the variance $\sigma_{pn}^2$ of nuclear protein across cells; the correction is accurate only near synchrony. Deviations from the mean obey a linear system with periodic coefficients, whose leading Floquet exponent $-\kappa(\epsilon)$ is the asymptotic synchronization rate. Using the fact that the four first-order stages of the feedback loop commute, we prove that $\kappa(\epsilon)=\epsilon/4+O(\epsilon^2)$ on the limit cycle in the large-population limit. Numerically computed exponents agree with the decay rates measured in simulations to within $0.2\%$ for $5$ to $400$ cells. The approach to synchrony from an incoherent state is slower than $\kappa$, and at the weakest coupling tested the population remains in a two-cluster state. With intrinsic molecular noise, uncoupled cells lose their autocorrelation within about ten cycles, whereas coupled cells retain it and sustain a Kuramoto order parameter of $0.68$ to $0.93$.

authors.name: Yuelong Li
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Exact transport exponents for random mosaic operators
papers.abstract: We determine the exponentially time-averaged transport exponents of period-two random mosaic operators, with zero potential on the even sites and iid potential on the odd sites. For every bounded, strictly positive, nonconstant single-site law, on one event of probability one, $\beta_f^-(q)=\beta_f^+(q)=\max\{0,2/3-\nu_H(f)/(3q)\}$ for all nonzero finitely supported states $f$ and all $q>0$. The positive odd integer $\nu_H(f)$ is determined by divisibility by $H$ and cancellation against the bounded zero-energy solution. In particular, the large-moment exponent is $2/3$ for every such state, while point sources on the two sublattices have second-moment growth powers $1$ and $1/3$. We obtain matching resolvent bounds by retaining the vanishing orders of two polynomial source channels through the singular normalization at zero energy. We also prove deterministic lower bounds for every bounded positive configuration. No density assumption is imposed on the law.

authors.name: Xu Xia
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

papers.title: On the generalized foliated cone theorem of rank one
papers.abstract: We prove the cone theorem for generalized foliated quadruples of rank one in arbitrary dimension. As an application, we prove the uniqueness of MMP outputs for log canonical generalized foliated quadruples of rank one.

authors.name: Mengchu Li
authors.institution: Kunming University of Science and Technology

papers.title: Finite rank and compactness of finite sums of Toeplitz products on the harmonic Bergman space
papers.abstract: We completely characterize finite rank and compactness for finite sums of products of Toeplitz operators on the harmonic Bergman space of the unit disk, assuming boundedness only of the full harmonic symbols. Reflecting the appropriate symbols reduces sums of Toeplitz products and small Hankel products to Toeplitz product sums. For sums of mixed Toeplitz and small Hankel products in either order, right multiplication by a fixed unitary reflection gives the corresponding reduction. These reductions preserve rank and compactness. Finite rank is characterized by symbol identities and a cubic divisibility condition on the coefficient polynomials obtained after choosing bases over one-variable rational function fields. We also obtain an exact rank formula. Compactness is characterized by boundary vanishing of the diagonal symbol sum and uniform decay of the centered symbol tensor on hyperbolic disks of fixed radius as their centers approach the boundary. For a sum of $N\ge1$ products, an equivalent compactness criterion uses weighted derivatives of the symbol components up to order $N$. When $N$ is even, the conditions of order $N$ cannot be omitted. Mixed commutators of finite rank vanish. We characterize small Hankel commutators of nonzero finite rank in terms of a bounded analytic function and its bounded reciprocal, both with rational primitives.

papers.title: Sharp inequalities for fractional spherical maximal operators on finite graphs
papers.abstract: This paper presents a systematic study of (quasi-)norm bounds for the fractional spherical maximal operator $M_{\alpha,G}^{\circ}$ on finite connected graphs $G$. We establish sharp estimates for the operator norm of $M_{\alpha,G}^{\circ}$ from $\ell^p(G)$ to $\ell^q(G)$ for $0 < p \leq q \leq \infty$, with explicit extremal values attained by complete graphs $K_n$ and star graphs $S_n$. We solve the corresponding extremal graph problem by showing that complete and star graphs are the unique maximizers of the operator norm in different parameter regimes. Additionally, we characterize graphs containing a universal vertex in terms of their operator norm. Finally, we analyze the spherical maximal operator $M^{\circ}_{G}$ on paths $P_n$, uncovering a clear divergence in the operator's behavior between odd and even lengths.

papers.title: Certified minimax normal-scale mixtures for the logistic-normal integral
papers.abstract: The logistic distribution function is a scale mixture of normal distribution functions, and Monahan and Stefanski approximate it by the $K$-term mixture $\Lambda(x) \approx \sum_{i} w_i \Phi(s_i x)$ chosen to minimise the uniform error on the real line. Each such mixture reduces the logistic-normal integral to a sum of $K$ normal distribution functions with the mixture's uniform error bound. This integral is the expectation of a logistic sigmoid over a normal distribution in statistics and the Gauss-Fermi integral in semiconductor physics. Monahan and Stefanski tabulate constants for $K \le 8$ and conjecture that the optimal error equioscillates at $2K$ points, while above $K = 8$ the Remez exchange and local solvers stall at nonequioscillating stationary points. We prove that the tangent space of the mixture family is a Chebyshev system, which forces $2K$-point equioscillation at every interior minimiser and makes any such solution the unique global minimax, and we prove interior attainment for $K \le 11$. A certification algorithm audits a candidate mixture in multiple-precision arithmetic, using a proved bound on the number of extrema as its completeness test, and three search pipelines reach $K = 9, 10, 11$, the last with certified worst-case error $1.26 \times 10^{-11}$. A signed $K = 22$ mixture carries a relaxed certificate at $3.605 \times 10^{-15}$. In causal mediation with a binary outcome, the certified sum replaces a biased Taylor expansion and stochastic integration with one closed-form evaluation.

papers.title: SD-Cache: Learnable Memory Consolidation with State-Guided Dynamic Caching
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as persistent services that must reason over large volumes of external knowledge. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) grounds model responses in relevant documents, but the retrieved content must still be encoded and stored in the key-value (KV) cache. As this content accumulates, the cache grows linearly, increasing memory consumption and inference cost. Existing memory-compression methods address this problem either by retaining a subset of cached states or by learning context compressors that map documents to compact latent representations. Despite these advances, consolidating information under tight memory budgets while preserving its usefulness for future queries remains challenging. We investigate how the model's native KV states can be selectively consolidated into a fixed-size working memory without access to future queries. To this end, we introduce SD-Cache (State-guided and Dynamically updated Cache), a query-agnostic KV-memory consolidation framework that operates alongside a frozen generator LLM. SD-Cache learns to consolidate layer-wise KV states into fixed-size memory through selective anchor-based pooling and state-guided refinement, processing new contexts in a single forward pass without context-specific optimisation. Experiments on retrieval-augmented question answering and synthetic long-context benchmarks show that SD-Cache maintains competitive downstream performance under constrained memory budgets.

papers.title: The Capacity of Conference Key Agreement over GHZ Networks
papers.abstract: $K$ users share independent GHZ states, each held by a subset of the users, and want a common secret key, using local operations and public classical communication (LOCC). We show that the conference key capacity, the largest number of secret key bits per copy of the resource, equals the key capacity of the classical source obtained by measuring every GHZ state. Measuring first is therefore optimal, even when the users keep quantum memory and communicate over any number of rounds. The capacity also equals the GHZ distillation capacity, the largest number of GHZ states shared by all users obtainable per copy.

papers.title: Are Web Agents Still Detectable? Stress-Testing Bot Defenses with Coordinated Evasion
